When the coding-rate is 0.7812 bits/pel., the signal-noise-ratio is 26.04 dB in the restored image. When the coding-rate is 2.5 bits/pel., the signal-noise-ratio is 32.44 dB.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and application of expert intelligent control system in production process of benzene
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, based on the mathematical model established by the authors, an expert intelligent control system (EICS) which is being used in tracing the set-points of temperature and pressure in production process of benzene, has been designed. The implementation of the computer control system based on EICS shows that the performance of this system and the tracing effectiveness are satisfactory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hybrid fuzzy logic and neural network controller for spacecraft docking system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new hybrid fuzzy logic and neural network control architecture is proposed and its application to attitude control of a spacecraft docking system is described. The controller uses fuzzy logic control to construct a knowledge base of control rules and learns by updating its prediction of the physical systems behavior and fine tuning a control knowledge base. It is applicable to control problems for which the analytical models of the process are unknown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of robust controllers in linear quadratic optimal systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the U-parameter interpolation design method is applied to a linear quadratic optimal system to minimize a cost function which includes the control input minimization and model reference signal tracking. A direct derivation of the closed-loop transfer function in terms of free parameters is first outlined. And by minimizing the cost function with respect to the free parameters the authors can determine these free parameters and then obtain the optimal result with desired robustness.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor based automatic power factor control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper discusses the development of a microprocessor based automatic power factor control by using LV switched capacitors for reactive power compensation. The complete system is designed for use with an Intel 8085 microprocessor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intelligent design approach for control system with interval parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An intelligent design approach for the multivariable control system with interval parameters in the frequency domain is presented. The interval system is defined in the frequency domain. The expected specification is constrained by the upper bound and lower bound of the step response. The quantitative feedback technique (QFT) is used. Two expert systems SEPE and SLSE are employed with a user-friendly interface, which can offer more information to adapt the software to different kinds of user (expert or novice). The motivation for studying this type of intelligent design approach include many useful applications. As an applied example the compensator for fast following synchronization of a generator is designed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The principle of minimum production cost model for multiple area interconnected power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A minimum cost production model which can be used to account economical energy exchange between utilities and evaluate production cost saving in multiple area interconnected systems is proposed in this paper. A fast probabilistic production simulation model is used to determine the thermal incremental cost of each system separately. Based on the thermal incremental cost of each subsystem, a nonlinear optimization model which minimizes the total production cost of the whole interconnected systems is used to determine the economical energy exchanges in the interconnected systems. Then total production cost and cost saving are for whole interconnected systems and each system. The minimum cost principle based on Lagrange multipliers is proposed to solve this nonlinear optimization problem. The tie line capacity limit and energy loss are included in the energy exchange process. Hourly loads are used in the model. The thermal incremental cost of each system and the energy exchanges between interconnected systems are evaluated hour by hour. Then a period summary report is produced. The proposed minimum cost model has been incorporated into FEPSS (Fast Electricity Production Simulation System) package. The Pacific Power Corporation, Australia has used this model to study power system interconnections in Southeast Australia.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of computer communication networks under link reliability constraints
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes a method to design a cost effective computer communication network which employs unreliable links. The design is aimed at obtaining a minimum cost network which satisfies the given constraints of grade of service defined in terms of the degree of availability of the network and the node to node traffic capacities in normal conditions. We present a general mathematical model for this problem and formulate the constraint equations. We then solve the problem by applying Lagrangean relaxation to the constraint equations based on subgradient optimization technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive hierarchical image coding technique using transform vector quantization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We developed an adaptive hierarchical transform vector quantization (AHTVQ) coding technique which applies discrete cosine transform (DCT) coding of variable image block-size in combination with adaptive vector quantization (VQ) coding. To reduce complexity the subvectors are quantized with a cascaded VQ instead of full-search VQ (FSVQ). Simulation results presented show that compression rates and subjective quality compare favourably with methods previously described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IFS avionics bus communication system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on GJB 289-87, the IFS avionics bus communication system is a distributed communication simulation system. It provides a real-time environment and experimental data for the engineering implementation, optimization and testing of avionics integrated tasks. It's architecture and design are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of pencil-of-functions method in the digital deconvolution
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper introduces the fitting principle of observed data using the pencil-of-functions (POF) method and first applies it to digital deconvolution. The result shows that this method has the advantages of insensitivity to noise and high quality of fitting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple source location-recursive approach for coherent sources
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In the paper, the multiple source location problem is considered. The coherency characteristics of the sources is analyzed. An new recursive method based on the coherent group classification is developed to provide high resolution source location estimations independent of the incident source coherency characteristics. The number of signals is also found simultaneously,.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An enhanced octree structure for representing the spatial/boundary decomposition of 3-D objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper describes an enhanced octree in which both the volume and the surface boundary of a 3D object are represented in the same data structure. An enhanced octree includes those octants right beneath the boundary surface of an object. The fully exposed faces of an octant will be associated with the boundary surface patches nearest to the them. For those exposed faces partially covered by smaller octants, quadtree decomposition will be performed and the exposed quadrants will be associated with the surface patches in the same way as the fully exposed faces. In this manner, an enhanced octree facilitates the modelling of a 3D object by providing both the volumetric and the surface properties in a single hierarchical structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An extensive Markov process for ECG noiseless coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In the paper, an extensive Markov process for noiseless ECG data compression is presented. It is an extension of the Markov process to measure the entropy value of a discrete signal. The extensive Markov process utilizes the inter sample correlations by predicting the incoming three samples based on the previous three samples which constitute an extensive Markov process state. In every state, there is a Huffman code table for the third extension code of the incoming three input samples, and the sizes of-the tables vary from state to state. Results show that an average of compression ratio (Cr) being 4.550 can be achieved. This corresponds to an average of 2.6376 bits/sample for each ECG signal, while the average entropy value for the original signals is 8.396 bits/sample. Although many noiseless ECG data compressors have been presented before, few has its Cr being greater than 4.0.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A concurrent production system (CUPS)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on traditional production systems and the member system model, the paper puts forward a concurrent production system (CUPS). This CUPS is described by outlining its syntax, basic structure of a member, working principle of the interpreter, and compatibility with OPS5. A test example is presented to illustrate that CUPS is a concurrent production system programming language supporting general and cooperative problem solving.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Software model of power communication network management
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Existing power communication supervision systems cannot serve as a network management systems. A software model of a network management system is proposed to meet the requirements of the development of power communication systems. The model contains four parts: operating system; application system; man-machine interface; and database. The structure and function of these parts is studied based on actual situations and requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Object-oriented integration of heterogeneous distributed databases
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper explains an object-oriented virtual integration approach of heterogeneous distributed databases, which is used in CIMBASE+. We introduce the basic concepts and features of the global data model OSAM* and global data language OSDL of CIMBASE+, explain the virtual schema integration approach, and describe the manipulation process of the virtual integrated database.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-aided design on the VLSI 45/spl deg/-mask compaction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We combine 1D compaction with reshaping-a new action to improve the result of the compaction. Our algorithms change layout element shapes automatically according to some criteria and make neighboring layout element shapes as similar as possible. The more similar they are, the more compactable space we can obtain. The main part of our compaction is reshaping. If elements of a certain 45/spl deg/ layout can have their geometric shapes reassigned, we reshape them in order to gain a more compactable space. Some experimental results of this 45/spl deg/ compactor with and without reshaping of both Manhattan and nonManhattan 45/spl deg/ layouts are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On guaranteed task scheduling in real time distributed process control systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Having considered various kinds of factors and many assumptions, we have developed a guaranteed task scheduling algorithm for workstations in real time distributed control systems that is mainly composed of three parts: active scheduling policy, guaranteed routine and cooperation bidding. We describe a general guaranteed task scheduling condition by birth-death process. We also analyse the influence of different demands of fault-tolerance on active scheduling policy, guaranteed routine and cooperation bidding; and we explore the performance change of guaranteed routine and cooperation bidding, given different active scheduling policies. Simulation studies are used to evaluate the performance of the algorithm, given the real time distributed process control systems composed of three workstations and six front-end controllers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ZKBE: a knowledge base environment for mechanical design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: ZKBE, a knowledge base environment for mechanical design, is proposed in this paper to deal with large-scale mechanical design-relevant knowledge. Some special technologies used in ZKBE, including the knowledge representation model OOS (Object Oriented Structure) and the design problem-solving architecture, are discussed in detail. Also, some function modules (e.g. the knowledge base storage system, the knowledge maintenance system, etc.) are also outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Conditional annulling for superscalar processors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper proposes an architectural feature for superscalar processors called conditional annulling. The conditional annulling mechanism achieves both the effects of conditional execution and speculative execution without incurring a significant increase of hardware complexity and cost. All effectiveness evaluation carried out in this paper shows the conditional annulling mechanism is effective in improving superscalar processor instruction scheduling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Embedding the production system in C language
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Production systems, such as ops5, have been widely used in menu knowledge-based systems and expert systems. With the development of large scale knowledge-based systems and more sophisticated expert systems, the processing ability of production systems has become a bottleneck. C is a general purpose language, it is used in many fields of software design. But C hasn't the components to represent knowledge and perform inference; it is not quite suitable for knowledge processing. We embed production systems in C, and design a new version of C (PSC). This makes use of the advantages of C and production systems. The design and implementation of PSC are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some strategy of routing in the B-ISDN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The ATM (asynchronous transfer mode) which has been determined by the CCITT recommendation I. 121 as the transfer mode for the B-ISDN (broadband-integrated services digital network) can be considered as a very fast packet switching method with a connection-oriented transport principle. However, the ATM effects new problems for the control mechanisms in the B-ISDN, from which the routing strategy is an important one. This article investigates the method of adaptive routing for B-ISDN system and compares it with fixed routing. Beside this the influence of the topology and the speed of dispatcher has been taken into account. It will be shown that adaptive routing algorithms do not improve the performance of an ATM-network under the assumptions made. Moreover it has turned out that a minimal speed of the dispatcher is existing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ada language and software fault tolerance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Ada language has a powerful ability to detect and correct faults. There is a tight relationship between Ada and fault tolerance. We discuss the interface of Ada language and fault tolerant techniques and design an Ada multitask-oriented software hybrid redundant system supported by a multicomputer environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The most compact digital regulator for thyristor excitation of large alternators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a new variety of the microprocessor-based excitation regulator (MPER), which has been operating on thyristor excitation systems of many large alternators. Several essential improvements significantly reducing the hardware as much as possible are introduced. The hardware elements are replaced by software elements leading to the most compact digital regulator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Online security analysis based on database method for electrical power system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Online security analysis (OSA) is one of the important functions of dispatching automation for modern power systems. In this paper, a new method of OSA based on a database is presented. The fundamental principal of this method is that a large amount of real time calculation would be substituted by a small amount of processing data which are obtained from the OSA database. This database is established by means of organizing the offline calculation data. The results of finite and reasonable offline calculation are taken as an OSA database. Then the theory of OSA using the database and its algorithm are developed. The application of this method to two practical power systems shows that it is a new way to carry out OSA in large power systems and has a wide spectrum in power system real time applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System identification using dynamic neural networks and its application to plasticating extruders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Proposes a dynamic neural network (DNN) model and gives the conditions under which the DNN has a unique equilibrium point. The synthesis of a DNN for solving quadratic optimization is given. The resultant approach is applied to the identification of a plastic extruder system. The results show that the model gives results that match those of an actual system. The approach proposed is thus shown to be effective.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A Kohonen-based structured codebook design for image compression
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The Kohonen neural network (KNN), creates a vector quantizer by adjusting the weights from input nodes to output nodes. Using this model, we obtain a codebook and also the neighborhood relations between the codewords of this codebook. Based on these neighborhood relations, we can create a structured codebook to improve the search time and/or bit rates. However, there is an intrinsic problem of applying the KNN directly. When the codebook size increasing, the coding performance is not good uniformly. To overcome this bad situation, we propose a modified version of the KNN, called the hierarchical KNN (HKNN). Using this method, the image "lenna" (of size 512/spl times/512) can be coded at 0.5 bpp with PSNR 32.197 dB. Besides, we also present an adaptive VQ scheme, adaptive HKNN, for image sequence coding. According to our experimental results, the improvement of adaptive HKNN can be up to 2.5 dB with 0.16 bpp transmission overhead for the image sequence "claire".<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Online measurement of quality variables in paper: formation and creping
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, two novel techniques developed by the authors to measure certain quality variables in paper manufacturing are described. These methods are based on the new online image sensors for digital image processing of paper samples. The techniques use the two dimensional Fourier transform of the original images to estimate basically two variables: the floc size distribution in paper formation and creping of tissue paper. In the first case, a new method to estimate the floc size distribution in paper is presented. The method computes only a reduced portion of the spectrum to determine, in frequency, the floc sizes present. The technique to measure creping gives the degree of roughness that has been induced on the tissue paper by looking also at its power spectra distribution. This characteristic is essential in determining the smoothness of tissue paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An energy function approach and its application to a new clustering algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper addresses the problem of natural partitioning of a set of geographically distributed nodes. For this purpose an energy function has been defined. Based on this energy function a clustering algorithm, which partitions the nodes into clusters, has been presented. It has been assumed, intuitively, that if the energy function attains a peak, the clusters produced follow the natural partitioning. The algorithm has been tested on a set of non-trivial node distribution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dead-beat control in the theory of state covariance assignment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: It is quite common in stochastic control problems to have performance objective that are expressed in terms of the covariances of the system state. In this research the following control problem is solved: design the linear feedback controller so that the covariance of the system state achieves the steady-state value during finite beats, and this steady-state covariance achieves the specified state covariance simultaneously. The existence conditions and the design methods of this class of the feedback controllers are discussed in this paper. The straightforward design steps are also given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and implementation of a distributed graphics language
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We present a distributed graphics programming language called DGLa, which facilitates the development of distributed graphics application. DGLa is an upward compatible extension of programming language C. Facilities for distributed programming and graphics support are included in it. It supports synchronous and asynchronous communication and provides the programmer with multiple control mechanism for process communication. The graphics support of DGLa is powerful, both sequential graphics library and parallel graphics library are provided. The design consideration and implementation experience are discussed in detail. Application examples are also given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The robust inverse Nyquist array (RINA) method for the design of multivariable control systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: It is pointed out in this paper that the criticism raised by Doyle and Stein (1981) against the inverse nyquist array (INA) design method was not tenable. Actually, the robustness behaviour of a diagonally dominant control system depends on its degree of diagonal dominance. Based upon a large amount of numerical calculation, this paper gives the least degree of diagonal dominance required to keep a system robustly stable under the perturbation of given intensity. On this basis an improved design method is proposed-the robust INA method (RINA). An example is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated supply/demand planning of electricity systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The complexity of the supply, demand, financial and pricing aspects of electricity planning demands an integrated approach such as provided by the PROSCREEN II integrated planning system. The authors describe the planning concept, the planning process, and the use of PROSCREEN II.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development toolkit for OSI network design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Reports on the creation of a development toolkit to facilitate the simulation of an OSI network environment. This facility can then be used to test any user-defined OSI protocol profile as well as for the testing of any non-OSI-to-OSI protocol converter. This toolkit also permits the generation of the layer protocol drivers required for the set-up of a DOS-based PC network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency domain median filtering for narrow band interference rejection in BPSK-PN signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Narrow band interference suppression in direct sequence signals is a classic communication problem that has received much attention and numerous solutions have been proposed. The paper proposes the use of a non-linear transform domain modified median filter that offers several advantages over the other techniques. Detailed simulation has been carried out and some graphic results are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expert system for HF communication link
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Fading is one of the major factors upon which reliable communication through an HF link depends. Due to this phenomenon, errors occur in the received message in terms of the character error rate (CER). This paper describes the design of an expert system (HFEXPERT), for data transmission over an HF channel, based on CER analysis. HFEXPERT was to improve the performance of a 100 Watt HF communication link at 4075 kHz between Pilani and Delhi, spanning a distance of 158 km.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel method of enhancing Fourier descriptors for 3-D planar shape recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new method of recognizing a two dimensional (2D) shape of a single perspective image taken from an unknown viewpoint is presented. This method is based on a set of new defined Fourier descriptors (FDs) to describe the contour of a planar shape lying in the three dimensional (3D) domain. In order to generate the 3D planar image from the 2D perspective image, we use inverse paraperspective transformation instead of general inverse perspective transformation. Based on the linear approximation of the transformation, new FDs for the 3D planar contour have been developed. They are proved to be merely dependent on the FDs of the 2D contour of the projected image and the slope of the world plane. Thereafter, opportunities for simple and efficient computation for 3D planar shape recognition can be realised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The variable-signed graph and its application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We propose the signed-graph that has signs attached to vertices as well as edges or arcs. We call it "variable-signed graph" (VSG). The algorithm to minimize the number of bipolar as its application is presented. The algorithm is useful not only to minimise the number of inverters in analogue computer programming, but also to solve the sociometry problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-line control of the colour printing quality by image processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A prototype called ARGUS is under development for automatic colour quality inspection of the printing web. The inspection is performed by a movable( 2D) colour CCD-camera which takes images under stroboscopic Light. To guide the measurements, the digital "page design files" are analysed by image processing techniques and used to determine several measurement spots and templates under a set of criteria. These measurements include co-ordinate system reference, colour registration, colour density, grey balance, micro-homogeneity and ink consumption pattern, which are all needed for printing press control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement and control of combustion process of industrial furnaces
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper studies a kind of combustion control strategy based on the power spectral distribution property of the minute pressure pulsation signal (MPPS) of flame. The experiment research shows that the power spectral distribution property of MPPS can describe the combustion state of industrial furnaces and the MPPS can be fastly obtained by direct detection. The proposed method can provide faster and more effective regulation on the fuel-air ratio than the conventional ones based on the measurement of excess O/sub 2/ content in the exhaust gas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An abstract execution model for temporal logic programs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper proposes an abstract execution model which can be used as the basis for implementing temporal logic programs on multi-processor architectures. Temporal logic programs offer a form of parallelism, which we call temporal-parallelism, that does not exist in standard logic programs. Temporal-parallelism means that computations at different moments in time can be performed in parallel and independently of each other. We also outline the mapping of the abstract model onto a network of processors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a relational query language with teams
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We introduce the concept "team" and incorporate the team query into the data language SQL. Existing relational query languages use tuple variables of tables to specify required data. Queries that are expressed by these languages are used to get all the data which satisfy the specified conditions. While a team variable represents a subset of a table, a team query is used to retrieve all the teams that meet certain constraints. We introduce team qualifications and briefly describe team query processing. The search space of a team query may be very large. Therefore, instead of using conventional breadth-first search method, we adopt a depth-first search method for query processing. Thus, users can always get a result if one exists.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of a GTO inverter in a 600 kV high voltage test system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A static frequency variable generator (60 kVA, 30-300 Hz) was designed and built to drive a high voltage L-C series resonant test circuit. Besides the general principles in the design of the power electronic device, certain situations must be carefully considered according to the high voltage test procedures and working conditions. Corresponding measures were taken in the design to guarantee proper operation. The generator has been tested in a high voltage test system and then in real test situations. The generator was found to function properly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CIM methodology and its application in some Chinese factories
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Computer integrated manufacturing (CIM) has been widely accepted by industries all over the world. But how to design the integration of different subsystems to reach the expected goal of great improvement of flexibility, efficiency, high quality and competition ability is not clear at the moment. It is anxiously necessary to develop a CIM design methodology for guiding the development of CIM. Methodology is a set of methods, including three parts: modelling methods, reference models, and structured approach. This paper describes the contents and applications of CIM methodology in some Chinese factories. The experiences and comments are proposed as well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Steady-state stability assessment of multimachine power systems using catastrophe theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Catastrophe theory as a qualitative mathematical tool which specially deals with the discontinuities occurring in nonlinear dynamic systems may be used to analyze the stability of power systems. In this paper a new and more appropriate catastrophe model, the cusp catastrophe manifold, and corresponding algorithm are proposed to analyze the steady-state stability in power systems. Compared with the model (A.A. Sallam et al, 1983) and the algorithm (A.A. Sallam, 1988) presented earlier, its resulting analyses are more accurate because its derivation is closely related to the initial operating conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributing computational processes to an attached RISC processor by code translation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: With the RISC architecture, it is now possible to attain supercomputing power on a single microprocessor chip. However, developing a stand-alone system harnessing their power could be slow and difficult. In this paper, we describe attaching RISC to a host computer which acts as a front-end platform. Instead of writing new compilers, library routines, and applications for the RISC, we translate existing application programs on the host computer for it. It means that ordinary software development tools of the host computer can be used for program development and debugging without the presence of the RISC. Once the program is ready, it can be automatically translated into RISC codes for execution on a host computer with the attached RISC microprocessor. Since all the I/O functions are now done by the host computer, all the user interfaces remain the same thus the distribution of the task to the attached RISC microprocessor is transparent to the user except for much higher performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive force control for position-controlled robot manipulators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive force control method for robot manipulators based on Popov's hyperstability criterion. As many researchers have found, one of the difficulties of the control problem is that the stability of the robot force control system is sensitive to the changes of the stiffness of the environment on which the force is exerted. To solve the problem, model reference adaptive control theory is used to identify the environment stiffness, and to determine an adaptive force feedback gain corresponding to the contacted environment. The theoretic analysis and experimental results show that this method can realize a stable force control when the environment stiffness changes to a sufficiently large extent.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real-time simulation algorithms of "generator-infinite busbar system" and transputer implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A real-time simulation model of a single generator-infinite busbar power system and its transputer implementation are described. Based on this model, real-time algorithms for solving differential equations are approached and a comparison is made among Tustin conversion, the ordinary trapezoidal method, the damping trapezoidal method and the underrelax iterative method. The last method is shown to be highly stable in solution for large simulation steps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SYST-a synthetical tool package for software development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: SYST is a comprehensive tool package for software development. It supports software system design, detailed design, and coding in a top down refinement way. Meanwhile, in the reverse direction, by parsing C source code, SYST may generate many kinds of design documents automatically from source code. Therefore, the design documents and source code say easily be kept consistent during the phases of implementation and maintenance. This paper discusses SYST's design goals, functions, and the experience of its use. Key techniques of its implementation are briefly depicted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A gigabit ATM-LAN protocol for multimedia communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An ATM (asynchronous transfer mode) based MAC (medium access control) protocol for gigabit LAN/MANs is proposed and its performance behavior for various load conditions is evaluated. The main design object of the protocol called HMR (high-speed multimedia ring) is the minimization of medium bandwidth loss by the function of fairness and priority control in the 1 Gbps-times-100 Km class. The effective solution of this object is the multiple window-token algorithm where each priority level has its own window-token for fairness control. In the multiple window-token algorithm, the rotation time of priority k window-token represents the offered load of priority k and higher. If the window-token rotation time of priority k exceeds a given threshold, access units cannot transmit cells of priority lower than k and they hold tokens of priority lower than k. As a result, the maximum access delay can be bounded in a certain range with minimum bandwidth loss whereas the window-token rotation time is kept under a certain value.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrating AI techniques into CASE environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The main topics and approaches touched on in this paper focus on the combination of software engineering with artificial intelligence into the CASE environment, and building a CASE environment model based on representation. There are two points we emphasize: (1) requirements analysis as a crucial phase, and (2) mapping most software-intermediate products into kernel representation forms based on a representational schema, which gives the developer the opportunity to generate these products automatically. At present, we have finished the preliminary work and have applied these techniques to a prototype system to support the development of large-scale mechanical CAD software.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of three-dimensional (3-D) QMF recursive digital filter banks for HDTV
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A design approach to linear phase 3-D QMF recursive digital filter banks has been proposed. The design is based on a transfer function which adopts the Bessel function of the S domain as its original lowpass filter. By bilinear transformation of the 1-D S domain to the 3-D Z domain to the function, a linear phase 3-D recursive digital filter can be realized. The realized 3-D IIR filters not only keep the advantages of the linear phase characteristics in the pass band and approximately linear phase characteristics in the stop band, but also compress the transition band and increase the attenuation of the stopband. The 3-D QMF IIR digital filters can be realized by lower order ones to accomplish real-time image separation and reconstruction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The linear quadratic integral optimal variable structure control for linear systems with delay
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the control problem for linear time delay systems is studied. In order to weaken the effect of the "inheritance" of the control law in the linear quadratic integral optimal control strategy, and to reduce the chatter of the variable structure control at the same time, a novel control method linear quadratic integral optimal-variable structure control is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High speed optical LAN based on SCM-WCM techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A number of optical networks based on the WDM-SCM technique are proposed. Physical realization of such networks are discussed. It is seen that cost saving as well as increased user numbers can be achieved using technologies easily available today. Various factors which affect the performance of such a network are also discussed. Further study of the performance of such networks under different traffic patterns will be carried out, this will facilitate the design of such networks in the near future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of robust control systems: equivalent system method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper is concerned with the problem of design of robust control systems preserving the stability and high performance under conditions of considerable uncertainty of the plant behavior. For solution of this problem the authors propose the equivalent system method based on construction and investigation of equivalent block diagrams of the control system, the output coordinate of which describes the additional motion of the explored system when its parameters are changing. The effectiveness of proposed design method is demonstrated by the example of design of a flight control system for a landing maneuver satisfying the given requirements with and without the presence of wind shear.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electric load forecasting using structure variable neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on the new developed structure variable neural networks, two models-the daily peak load (DPL) model and daily 24-hour load (DHL) model are proposed in the present paper. The cluster Gaussian analysis (CGA) is used for the training of the models. The effectiveness of the new forecasting strategy is demonstrated by training and testing using the data collected from the Jing-Jin-Tang network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed computing structures for efficient evaluation of matrix determinant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Considers the relatively unexplored problem of identifying efficient structures for computing matrix determinants, and presents four alternative solutions for this problem with a comprehensive analysis of each of the proposed approaches in respect of computation time and number of processors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new representation for programmable logic arrays to facilitate testing and logic design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Presents a new graph model and an associated set of operations for representing programmable logic arrays (PLAs). Through this graph model, most realistic PLA faults, including crosspoint, stuck-at, break and bridging faults, can be modeled. The work of diagnosis and test generation is thus simplified. Also, many logic design problems, such as folding, minimization and decomposition, can be done using this representation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of trellis-coded QPSK/SS systems with long PN sequence combating multiple-access and tone interferences
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Trellis-coded modulation is applied to code division multiple access spread-spectrum (SS) systems where a long pseudonoise (PN) sequence is employed to meet a large number of users. The performance of the trellis-coded QPSK/SS combatting multiple-access and tone interference is analyzed. The results obtained are compared to the conventional SS systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The double equalization technique for HF fading channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a new adaptive equalizer structure. The study shows that the performance of the new equalizer is close to that of the square root Kalman algorithm and its computational requirements can be reduced remarkably. It can be used in a fast HF data transmission system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overdetermined recursive instrumental variable algorithm for FIR system identification with noisy data based on polyspectra
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We address the problem of identifying the impulse response of a finite-dimensional system, when output observations are provided. The relation between the bispectrum and tricepstrum of the system output is set up and over-determined recursive instrumental variable algorithm for FIR system identification is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CCD camera based automatic dimension measurement and reproduction of 3-D objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents an automatic CCD camera vision based measurement system having capabilities to measure dimensional parameters and reproduce a 3-D object on computer numerical controlled machines (CNC). The operations of image acquisition, digitization, storage and transfer to computer are performed by the vision system. The vision system provides the required coordinates to computer for the movement of machine tools. The CNC machines integrated with the vision system form an automatic object reproduction system. This automation enhances the quality and quantity of production. The associated analysis software employs graphic techniques like edge detection, surface filling and mensuration of regular 3D objects. The linear parameter (i.e. dimensions) of the objects are obtained by area measurement using the surface filling algorithm. The measured dimensions are in the form of coordinates to be input to the CNC part program.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improvement of phase margin of AMB control system by flux time derivative
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper introduces a new method to improve the characteristic of an active magnetic bearing (AMB) control system by flux time derivative. The theoretical analysis and computer simulation results show that this method can improve the phase margin effectively, and simplify the design and realization of the compensation device.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Campus-wide distributed library search system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper discusses the mechanism of accessing multiple libraries geometrically distributed in an academic institute in a uniform manner. Searching of any library item in such a system may amount to blindly querying every single participating database in the system (broadcasting the query). If the information about these databases and their holdings is kept in the form of indices distributed over a group of brokers, the queries can be forwarded to a set of appropriate databases, thus avoiding a broadcast. The proposed distributed library search system is based on the client-server model and consists of a collection of database servers which maintain the multiple library databases in the campus, brokers which hold a variety of distributed indices, and clients. This approach helps minimize the network traffic which rises otherwise due to broadcasting, and reduces the average search time. The design approach here resembles that of a heterogeneous, bottom-up distributed database design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of an expert system on man-machine interface for the SPC switching system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: It is very important to improve man-machine interface of computer system for the people. We know that the daily maintenance or management of SPC switching system requires many man-machine communications, but now many kinds of man-machine communications of SPC switching system are neither very easy nor very perceptive directly for the operators. This paper presents a user-friendly intelligent man-machine communication tool for SPC switching systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis and modeling of a dynamic vision based robotic system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The preliminary results of a work for analysis and modeling of a dynamic vision based robotic manipulator are presented. The major motion related factors such as motion blur of images, and dynamics of the robot joints are emphasized. Simulations in two and three dimensions are implemented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using the parallel second-order predictor-corrector algorithm for dynamic real-time simulation of synchronous generator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a second-order parallel predictor-corrector algorithm which is used to solve ordinary differential equations on parallel processor transputer networks. It has been realized to simulate the machine-network transient real-time performance on a single generator to infinite bus power system. Some features of the algorithm such as the recurrence formula, the application domain and the numerical stabilization, etc., are discussed. Using this algorithm for the dynamic simulation of a single generator to infinite bus power system in symmetrical fault situations, the real-time stabilization results can be obtained satisfactorily on a four-transputer parallel network with a calculating interval <2.5 ms. The calculation time is about 1/3 of that of a single processor. This parallel algorithm is excellent for engineering applications. If large transputer networks are used, the dynamic real-time simulation of multigenerator power systems may be realized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method to generate test sequences for protocol conformance testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a method to generate test sequences which test both data flow portion and control flow portion of Implementation Under Test (IUT) for protocol conformance testing. The method is based on a model called Normal Extended Finite-State Machine (NEFSM) which makes the conditions and variables used in the state transition externally controllable. Algorithm to generate test sequence is given. As an example, the proposed technique is applied to class O transport protocol TPO specification described in NEFSM throughout the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hypertext-base software document system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: During the life cycle of software development, we propose to adapt knowledge representation mechanisms in artificial intelligence and apply hypertext techniques into the software development process. On this basis, diverse documents can be organized, structured and managed effectively. We provide facilities for developing a document base and combine auxiliary tools distributed in different phases in order to make a unified software development environment to solve traditional problems which exist in hypertext.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Strategic planning and considerations of broadband access networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A methodology for finding out an appropriate access network architecture on B-ISDN is proposed. The authors extract the considerations to determine the most economical and efficient access network architecture and set up the organic interrelationships between them. They also show the network evaluation methods to choose the most appropriate access network architecture among the alternatives. Finally, they propose a broadband access network architecture and its evolution scenarios that are suitable to the Korean environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Buffer size and switching capacity study in packet switches of broadband ISDN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper investigates packet loss probabilities of two alternative two-stage output-buffered switches. The performance of these switches can be improved as the switching capacity per output and buffers size increase. Two traffic models, uniform random traffic and bursty traffic are considered. The effects of bursty traffic can degrade switch performance significantly. Especially, the packet loss increases significantly in the buffer when mean burst length increases. In addition, the effect of the bursty traffic on the switching capacity can be ignored. The paper also compares the requirement of the buffer size and switching capacity of the two switches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high-level MIMD programming tool for image understanding algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Image understanding algorithms involve different parallel architectures. Among them, there is MIMD computers for the purpose of executing complex algorithms. Unfortunately, programming such computers is difficult. A high-level MIMD programming tool based on the Linda programming paradigm is presented which can be used to implement parallel image understanding algorithms easily and efficiently. We describe the implementation of this software on a message passing multicomputer. The overhead of the primitives and the experiences with two well known problems are presented for providing an idea of the practicability of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Covariance control and robustness of bilinear stochastic discrete systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this research, a characterization of all controllers that assign specified covariances to the closed-loop bilinear discrete systems is given explicitly. Also, this paper introduces several different new robustness result for the systems from a deterministic viewpoint. The robustness measure presented is expressed in terms of the system state covariance matrix.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An urn theoretical approach towards modelling of thinning algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The urn theoretic model introduced has been applied in deducing some interesting results for image processing. One of the most intuitively appealing applications of urn models is in the area of stochastic learning theory. Using this concept, the performance of a class of pattern thinning algorithms in image processing has been analysed. The performance can be visualized as the probability of a correct response in a multiple choice problem. A simple replacement model has been used for the performance analysis of some thinning algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application and potential market of low temperature district heating reactor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A vessel type integrated natural circulation 5 MW low temperature district heating reactor has been developed and successfully operated by Institute of Nuclear Energy Technology (INET), Tsinghua University since 1989. Now a 200 MW (HR-200) heating reactor is under design. The HR-200 has relatively low operating parameters, a simpler system and easier fabrication for equipment, so the capital cost of the HR-200 is lower than the PWR and the cost of heat production is lower than that of a conventional boiler. This kind of reactor also can be used as supplementary heating for industrial processes, sea water desalination, cogeneration, air-conditioning, oil recovery and so on. This paper discusses the potential market and relative economic analysis for the low temperature district heating reactor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reconfigurable architecture of cube-connected cycle multiprocessor system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Recent advances in VLSI technology has stimulated research in massively parallel computers to satisfy the continuous increasing demand for computer power in advanced science and technology. The cube-connected cycle (CCC) is one of the most attractive interconnections and architectures for massively parallel computers. This paper addresses a new reconfigurable architecture to implement the cube-connected cycle on a silicon wafer by wafer scale integration (WSI), which is expected as a promising technology to construct massively parallel computers on silicon wafers. The performance of the proposed architecture is discussed with respect to yields of system. It is confirmed by comparing with previous work that the reconfigurable architecture based on the row-column redundant scheme achieves the better yield enhancement than earlier designs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel stereo technique based on anisotropic character of human visual system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a novel technique for stereo matching according to the anisotropic character of human visual system the original stereo images are decomposed into several directional images. The primitive extraction, description and matching are performed parallelly in each pair of directional images. Since the information in each directional image belongs to only a limited interval of direction the matching in each directional image is rather precise and robust. The process is more consistent with the physiology and it directly leads to extensions of Marr-Poggio theory in several aspects. The experimental results have shown the efficiency of the stereo technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new write-invalidate snooping cache coherence protocol for split transaction bus-based multiprocessor systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We present a new write-invalidate snooping cache coherence protocol called MMESSII cache protocol which addresses several significant drawbacks of existing write-invalidate snooping protocols under the split transaction bus based multiprocessor environment. In this protocol, each cache block maintains the ID information to identify the processor module that invalidated the block most recently. It also maintains seven cache states which consist of two updated states, one exclusive state, two shared states and two invalidated states. By using these states and the ID information, our protocol can reduce the contention for both memory modules and system bus significantly. We also present the simulation results which. Show better performance of our protocol than that of existing write-invalidate protocols.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New stability test theorems for two-dimensional IIR digital filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In the paper, new stability test theorems for 2D IIR digital filters are proposed, which can simplify the algebraic test procedure, especially for the test of high order 2D digital filters. The authors directly use the modified 1D Schur test that is revised to test zeros in |z|/spl les/1 instead of searching real roots in all x /spl isin/[-1,1]. The test is a very exact test and can overcome the drawbacks of other algebraic or nonalgebraic test methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new NFA algorithm for SPC switching systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a new approach for the formal description of the software of stored program controlled (SPC) telephone switching systems. An event-driven algorithm based on nondefined finite automaton (NFA) are created. By using the algorithm, a new SPC 1+1 call processing technique for a party-line telephone switching system are implemented, and the problems which the traditional party-line technique find difficult to resolve, such as communication in secret, separate ringing, no-answer call forward and transferring call forward, are implemented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effects of skew ratio on zeros of a sampled-data system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The effects of sampling time on the open-loop zeros of a sampled-data system were explored by Astrom et al. (1984). However, the effects of skew ratio on the behaviour of the open-loop zeros are relatively unknown. In this paper, we show how the locations of the finite zeros of a sampled-data system are affected by skew ratio via theory and an example. Analytical expressions to measure the sensitivity of these zeros with respect to the skew ratio are provided. The behaviour of the finite zeros with respect to skew ratio is also demonstrated by simulation studies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Information approach of intelligent system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The entropy is essentially a measure of information uncertainty. In this paper, we discuss the information-theoretic application to intelligent control. Our research involves the fuzzy control, the neural network and fault diagnosis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A switch node architecture for multimedia environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A bus oriented centralized switch-node architecture to provide service to the three broad types of traffic viz., (1) Connection-oriented service for real time (RT) voice traffic, (2) Connection-less service for interactive data (ID) traffic, (3) Connection-oriented service for non-interactive data (NID) traffic, for multimedia environment in a LAN has been proposed. The paper discusses the performance aspects of the proposed media-access scheme and the centralised scheduling policy which have been analyzed through simulation in particular for ID and NID traffics alone.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fusion algorithm of sensor data for robots
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The probability distribution function is used to describe the characteristics of the sensor. The system configuration of sensor data fusion is described. Five modules for the gathering and fusion of sensor data are represented. A linear Gaussian form measurement model of the sensor system is defined. Moreover, the authors define an optimality criterion for fusion of sensor data to get the optimal value from sensor measurements by maximizing the conditional probability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stability criteria for trajectory simulation in transient stability assessment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, novel and efficient stopping criteria for power system post-fault trajectory simulation are proposed for expediting the speed of transient stability assessment (TSA). Based on the criteria, an algorithm is developed to determine the critical clearing time (CCT) for a multimachine power system. The algorithm combines the merits of both the fast speed of the technique of potential energy boundary surface (PEBS) and the reliability of the time domain simulation method. Examples are given to show the problems of integration stopping criteria published in recent papers and how they are overcome in this paper. Extensive tests were done on several systems and the results show that the proposed criteria are reliable and the algorithm improved the efficiency of traditional time domain numerical simulation methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generic expression of digital function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The relation of logical functions is analyzed. The fundamental function which includes independent function is introduced and generic expression of logical function which is similar to Walsh function is given. The analysis and results are based on linear space theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A structuring scheme for the representation of manageable semantic information in a hypermedia database
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: One reasonable way to alleviate the problems of navigation in current hypermedia systems is to construct a search space in accordance with user's view of a query. To do so, the hypermedia system must accumulate sufficient amount of semantic information about its hypermedia databases (HDB). This paper describes a conceptual structure to efficiently represent and store semantic information inherent in each node of a HDB. Also, A concept concretization operation is set up to characterize inherent semantic information of a node. This scheme allows a user to express his/her intent into a query only with descriptors and without any structural information about the HDB. It enables the system to execute content-based search.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New solving method of eigenvalue under parallel process
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Presents a new method for finding real and complex eigenvalues and eigenvectors. We call this method the pole Gaussian method, since it was inspired by the Gauss-Seidel method. The idea is to use the approximate distance between the eigenvalue poles on the complex plane to iteratively calculate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors. A proof of convergence is presented in this paper, and it is shown that, in some cases, accurate solutions can be obtained by a small number of iterations. The dependence of the convergence speed on the initial values is also investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A cost-effective self-routing permutation network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A cost-effective self routing permutation network that is able to connect any input set of permutations assuming one-to-one connection is discussed. The network resembles the baseline network topology, and thus has log N stages.
