However, a re-circulation scheme is adopted in each stage of the network as in a single-stage shuffle-exchange (S/E) network. The inputs are re-circulated in each stage of the network before they are passed to the subsequent stage. The routing scheme is a binary radix routing. The hardware complexity of the network is O(N log N). The complexity is much less than O(N log/sup 2/ N) of the Batcher network which can be used as a self-routing permutation network when a banyan network is attached to it. The propagation delay of the network is O(log/sup 2/ N) stages. The hardware overhead to implement the self-routing is small, and the implementation has a good regularity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compiling relative set abstractions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In recent years there has been a lot of interest in combining the functional and logic programming paradigms. One of the most semantically elegant of the various proposals is the set abstraction construct. This paper addresses the issues involved in implementing set abstraction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Novel extended equal area criteria with detailed power system models
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Incorporated into extended equal area criteria (EEAC) in a parametric manner, detailed models of generators with field flux decays and excitation systems in varying degrees are taken into consideration. A simple and convenient cluster of modular EEACs with excellent adaptability both in model and application environment are developed in this paper. Corresponding methods to calculate the critical clearing angle (CCA) of the one machine infinite bus (OMIB) system are constructed in fully analytical forms. A new approach for correction of large errors of EEAC resulting from inaccurate OMIB equivalency is proposed. The invalidity of EEAC is greatly minimized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A graphical reconstruction of FIR filter from its morphological kernel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A morphological kernel, or a subset of the kernel known as the basis, can be used to represent both linear and nonlinear filters. However, reconstruction of a linear shift invariant (LSI) filter is impractical since both its basis as well as its kernel are infinite. The paper presents a graphical property of the morphological kernel for LSI filters. A graphical reconstruction method is also introduced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The computer aided temperature monitor and control system for the hydraulic valve
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper deals with the temperature control applied in hydraulic valve testing. The control system parameters can be identified online with the algorithm, and the parameters can also be optimized. For improving the control system performance, the penalty function is led into the process of identifying parameters. The distributing points of measuring temperature are considered. There are about five measuring temperature points and three controlling temperature points in the control system. Oil is used to test the hydraulic valve flows in the pipeline. The temperature control system consists of two levels of computer: the top level computer is the SUN 286, its tasks is to calculate the parameters and penalty function, optimize the parameters, draw the temperature curve, display data, and print data tables; and the front end computers are STO industry control computers whose task is to sample the temperature data and control temperature. There are four front end computers in the control system. One of them is used to control temperature, and the rests are used to control the oil pressure and flow.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study on basic steps from databases to knowledge bases
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We discuss one important development of current research efforts on extensible database management system, ie., extensible query optimization, which provides a flexible platform to organize the query processing or optimization component to handle large sets of facts. We also outline a possible extension of existing processing strategy for relational DBMSs to the new and extended requirement of KBMSs and propose possible solutions for improving the evaluation efficiency of user submitted requests. Finally, we discuss the two alternative evaluation strategies for processing queries in KBMSs ie. top-down and bottom-up evaluation. Discussing their differences and commonalities is important for understanding the impact of the two methods when evaluating user requests in a KBMS environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel zero switching loss step up/down three phase AC/DC converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A novel zero switching loss three-phase AC/DC power converter is proposed. Merits of the proposed switch set include zero switch loss, simple control logic (with fixed frequency and without using current sensors), unity displacement factor as well as reduced harmonic contents. Analysis of the switching process is given and conditions achieving zero switching loss are derived. Finally, some experimental results are also given as a demonstration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallel algorithm for robot generalized forces/torques computation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, based on a PUMA 560, studied with the resolved Newton-Euler inverse dynamic equations as the model, the authors propose the principles of decomposing the equations. An efficient heuristic scheduling algorithm, based on an activity on edge acyclic directed graph to express the priority relationship of the decomposed subtasks and the task-execution procedure is presented to (1) find a schedule to achieve the critical path time with minimum number of processors; and (2) find a schedule such that the execution time is minimal with fixed number of processors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of fuzzy logic controller for power system stabilization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The application of a fuzzy controller to improve the stability of power systems is presented in this paper. To achieve good damping characteristics over a wide range of operating conditions, speed deviation and acceleration of a synchronous generator are chosen as the input signals to the fuzzy controller. The stabilizing signal is determined according to the nonlinear fuzzy membership function depending on the speed and acceleration states of the generator. Simulation and implementation studies have been carried out on a one-machine and two-machine infinite bus system respectively. The simulation and implementation result show that the proposed fuzzy controller is very effective and gives better performance than the conventional power system stabilizer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On construction of Markov tree in reasoning about uncertainty
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Preliminary results on the construction of a Markov tree in reasoning about uncertainty are presented in this paper. A Markov tree is one kind of special graphical model where a local computation scheme is feasible. It is shown that a maximum cardinality search algorithm on a hypergraph gives a construction of a Markov tree if the hypergraph is a hypertree. It is also shown that the transformation from an arbitrary hypergraph to minimal hypertree cover is NP-complete.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and simulation of the LOW RISC II/sub R/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We present an analysis of the decision making process adopted by the LOW RISC Design Group which led to the microarchitecture level design of the LOW RISC II. By investigating the fundamental factors relating to the design of RISC machines and logic programming, we have derived a general design methodology for application-specific RISC processors. The details relating to the choice of specific design schemes are explained, while at the same time we engage in practical design work by proposing alternative design schemes. The resultant architecture is called the LOW RISC II/sub R/, the subscript denoting a redesign.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new robust controller of robotic joint
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A measurement and computation method of acceleration for each joint is described. Measured acceleration signals are filtered by a fourth order Butterworth filter. The robust principle of acceleration feedback is analyzed. Nonlinearities and disturbances of the system can be diminished by feeding back a dead zone nonlinearity around the integrator. The overshoot and saturation of the integrator can be reduced by the controller. The general principle of selecting parameters of the dead zone nonlinearity is presented. Thus, a robust joint controller is obtained and control performances of the system are improved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System development and maintenance with reuse-in-the-large
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The approach introduced provides a solution for application reuse-in-the-large. According to this approach, reuse-in-the-large is not only an attractive issue but also a means to automate the process of application development and maintenance on a large-scale.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The multimedia information link control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes the preliminary design of a multimedia information link control (MILC) that provides a framework for multimedia application development. Many of the multimedia systems, such as distributed multimedia database system and multimedia conferencing system, involve communication via the network. However, the existing transmission protocols do not preserve the characteristics of multimedia information, like real-time requirements and the preservation of temporal relation between data streams. All these features must be included in the next generation transport protocol in order to efficiently support multimedia communication. The design of MILC is not only to exploit the characteristics of multimedia information, but also to modularize information and processing rather than processing alone. The object-oriented approach has been applied to model MILC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Call admission control for ATM networks using instantaneous QOS estimates
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) has been suggested as a flexible and efficient transmission standard for future broadband ISDN (B-ISDN). Admission control determines whether to accept or deny a new connection request based on traffic characteristics of the new call, its quality of service (QOS) requirements, are current network status. In most of previous work the long-term time-averaged cell loss probability and/or the cell transmission delay are adopted as the criteria of admission control. Using the long-term time-averaged values may not be appropriate in ATM networks because the traffic can change rapidly and dynamically. In this paper, we propose to use a minimum mean square error estimator of the instantaneous cell loss rate as additional criterion for admission control and study the dynamic behaviour of an ATM switch with burst-silence inputs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An I-CASE system for automatic generation of MIS software-MISG/CASE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Introduces a newly-developed intelligent CASE tool, called MISG/CASE (Management Information Systems Generator using Computer-Aided Software Engineering), for the generation of MIS software. For MISG, we have defined two descriptive languages: one is FDL (Function Description Language), for requirements description, and the other is QSL (Query and Statistics Language), for query demand description. The MIS Generator, based on the two languages, is integratively composed of requirements analysis tools, data analysis tools and code generation tools. The system has now been applied in practice.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of internal buffered crossbar-based ATM switches with LQFS policy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Crossbar switches have always been attractive to switch designers because they are internally nonblocking and they are simple. For switching in the ATM mode, this fabric has many advantages and the main drawback is that the total memory required is large. In order to reduce the large buffer memory the longest queue first service (LQFS) policy is used. The performance of internal buffered crossbar-based ATM switches with LQFS policy is studied. It is shown that the switch with LQFS policy has better performance with smaller memory compared with the one with round-robin policy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Short-term thermal unit commitment including reliability and dynamic economic dispatch
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a probabilistic technique which can be used to develop unit commitment schedules for continually changing loads in a power system for a specified period. The technique is developed on the basis of a system fulfilling reliability and dynamic economic dispatch. Typical unit commitment cases are illustrated with numerical examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interframe predictive coding for two special cases: zooming and rotation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a new interframe predictive coding approach to deal with the two special cases of zooming and rotation for transmission of image sequences. Tests show that in many aspects performance of this new approach is as good as or even better than that of motion compensation for such special occasions. The author also investigates how to reduce the computational burden and enhance the search accuracy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The linewidth of DFB semiconductor lasers calculated by two-dimensional theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Distributed feedback (DFB) semiconductor lasers are essential devices for high-bit-rate and coherent optical fiber communication systems. The authors derive a new transfer matrix based on two-dimensional theory. They use this new transfer matrix to analyze the X/4 phase shift DFB semiconductor lasers. The linewidth is calculated. The results show that the linewidth calculated by two-dimensional theory is larger than one-dimensional results, this is due to the transverse effects of semiconductors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Full-digital controlled cycloconverter induction motor drive for underground hoist application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Cycloconverter induction motor drives are finding increasing application in the mining industry. A full digital controlled cycloconverter induction motor drive system for underground hoist is developed. To realize the speed control and cycloconverter control, multiple single chip microprocessors are used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An algorithm for robust indirect adaptive control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new indirect adaptive control scheme is proposed to achieve robustness to bounded disturbance and a class of unmodelled dynamics. A key feature of this scheme is that the dead zone is used but the knowledge of the parameters of the upper bounding function on the unmodelled dynamics and the disturbance is not required. Stability analysis is provided for the new scheme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power system load forecasting with ann and fuzzy logic control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Power system load forecasting is an important subject both in power system planning as well as in online power system operation. The authors show that for both long term forecasting for planning and short term forecasting for online power system operation, simpler speedy and robust forecasting software is very useful. For this purpose, an artificial neural network plus fuzzy logic is shown to be very appealing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural computing for building statistical macromodels of circuits and systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the application of a backpropagation neural network in building statistical macromodels of circuits and systems is studied and the way to analyze the characteristics of the circuits with the help of the macromodel, a well trained BP network with the data measured from the circuit, is discussed. The neural network methodology is a novel way for circuit analysis, and as compared with statistical method, it's much easier.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and implementation of a transmission interface between a host and a communication subnet
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes the theory of designing a parallel transmission interface circuit between a host and a communication subnet. It also gives a circuit diagram and drive instruction series applied to a particular system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a gate array matrix processor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The design of a matrix arithmetic processor using the Gould CMOS 2-μm gate array design kit is described. The background leading to the formulation of the matrix arithmetic processor is presented, along with its design, implementation, simulation and analysis. A 16-bit floating-point format is proposed.

articleTitle: An analytical method of nonlinear distortion in direct sequence spread spectrum multiple access communication systems in baseband
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We analyse the effects of the nonlinearity, which resides in a transmission line, on the baseband signal in a direct sequence spread spectrum multiple access (DS-SSMA) communication system, assuming that the nonlinearity is represented by the power series of the input signal. We have studied the dominant part (up to the 3rd order) of the signal distorted by the nonlinear circuit in the line using the Fourier method, and propose an analytical method of the S/N at the output of the correlation detector. We also justify our method by comparing calculated results with the simulated ones in the case when the nonlinear circuit model is expressed by the error function as a typical example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Enacting objects for plant-wide HARD real-time online distributed control system (P-hard-RODCS): Oosim
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Distributed control networks running in real-life industrial environments that can support the development of plant-wide hard real-time online distributed control system (P-hard-RODCS) are rare. Due to the lack of practicalities, traditional simulation method is not feasible for realistic utilization. The practicality of constructing object-oriented nodes to simulate the plant-wide HARD real-time online distributed control system (Oosim/P-hard-RODCS) is the main concern of this research. Although P-hard-RODCS is widely available from many distributed process control system suppliers or vendors, they are at high cost. However, from the feasibility investigation and development enhancement point of views, we demand a versatile model that can: (1) handle the dynamics of hard real-time data highway traffic; and (2) can mimic the dependability of online interactive operations. The communication constraints and capabilities of the enacted objects are delineated. These objects are built from the operating system software primitives and the physical hardware units versus the traditional process-oriented evolutionary-type of development methodology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer vision for spacecraft docking system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new computer vision method for estimating the relative parameters of spacecraft docking system is presented. Based on binocular computer vision system, the relative mathematical model between the two spacecrafts is established. The relative position and attitude parameters are obtained using optimization approach. It has advantages over the traditional methods. Simulation results show the feasibility of the proposed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Models and performance analysis of integrated voice/data multiplexer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Two models of a fixed frame length, movable boundary, integrated voice data multiplexer with finite buffers for both voice and data packets are proposed and analyzed. Expected queueing length and delay are derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Information flow in shop floor controllers at GINTIC's EPCBAF
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents the approach taken by GINTIC in implementing an information system for the experimental printed circuit board assembly facility (EPCBAF). It begins with a brief description of the information architecture, hardware and network communication configurations and the process flow. It then discusses the control strategy and functional modules at the shop floor area. The data flow among the functional modules during various production phases, the information processed and/or generated and the control of this information are described in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic real-time simulation of synchronous generator based on parallel processing technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a parallel processing network, a "transputer network", on which the dynamic real-time simulation of a single turbine generator to infinite bus power system can be realized. Based on a second-order predictor-corrector algorithm, using the features of the transputer network, a parallel simulation model of the turbine generator is proposed. The simulation program, which is written in OCCAM, has been implemented on a four-CPU transputer network. The real-time simulation results can be obtained with fifth-order generator models. Some simulation curves and discussions are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed scheduling of tasks exempt of any timing failure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In the design of distributed computer systems, especially real time distributed systems the scheduling problem is considered to be an important one. First, the problem of testing feasibility for a set of time critical tasks that run on each node-processor machine locally has been studied. The acceptance tests and the scheduling algorithms are described as follows: scheduling sporadic tasks within idle times; scheduling periodic tasks as late as possible; scheduling periodic and sporadic tasks together. Second, the problem of tasks which haven't been executed locally in the node is studied. There are three algorithms for cooperation to be evaluated in the distributed system: the focused addressing algorithm; the bidding algorithm; the flexible algorithm. The results show that distributed scheduling is effective in a hard real time environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of output-buffered ATM switch with two priority classes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents an N/spl times/N modular ATM switch which uses a fully interconnected switch fabric for no switch blocking and places two buffers at every output for storing high priority packets (realtime traffics) and low priority packets (non-realtime traffics). The switch operation is slotted. Packets of both priority classes can be queued in order when waiting for service and the service principles are FHLL (first high last low priority packets) and FCFS (first come first service within each priority queue). The paper analyzes completely performances of the switch, including the maximum throughput, the mean queue length of each buffet, the mean queueing delay and loss probability of packets, and then, a performance evaluation test is made on an 8/spl times/8 experimental switch architecture, the results show that this ATM switch meet perfectly requirements of high and low priority packets and is successful.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tool-path verification using computer graphics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a method to simulate a cutter tool-path using computer graphics. It can show the cutter tool-path in the X-Y and Y-Z planes simultaneously, and can reduce the errors in NC programming. Example parts are machined to demonstrate all the supported functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The architecture and experiment of the customer premises network for a microwave ATM network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper discusses the architecture of an experimental research prototype for a microwave ATM customer premises network (CPN). Based on the architecture of the CPN, some of the key technologies for realizing the CPN functional blocks are discussed and part of the application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) design results are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Teleconferencing video transmission control in microwave network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The video transmission control is the key technique in a broadband teleconferencing system. Besides the video channel, to transmit images, a control channel is needed to provide information of how to control the video channel during a teleconference. The control signals can be inserted into the field blanking interval and transmitted with the video signal in the microwave network. The related hub communication stations in the network receive the mixture signals, extract the control command, then get the exchanging equipment into operation automatically to establish the video transmission links. The paper presents the video transmission, video exchanging and control signal channel establishing technique based on a local TV broadband microwave network. The network management protocol and hardware are also mentioned.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A Petrov-Galerkin finite element method for designing optical soliton communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A Petrov-Galerkin finite element method (FEM) is developed for designing optical soliton communication, which is modeled by a nonlinear Schrodinger (NLS) equation with loss. It is proved that the numerical scheme has accuracy of order 2 and 4 with respect to the space and time variables respectively. The numerical results not only show the high accuracy and stability of the method, but also presents the physical process of optical soliton transmission, which is in good agreement with the experiment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of all stabilizing controllers for bilinear discrete-time systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this research, necessary and sufficient conditions are given for the existence of a controller of specified order n/sub c/, which is assigned a specified matrix value X to the covariance of the closed-loop system. If a solution exists, the entire set of stabilizing controllers that assign X can be parameterized by two orthogonal matrices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intellectual principle and design in image guidance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Analyses and summarizes how image-based guidance systems have been taking shape. Taking as an example the "Fighting Axe" cruise missile, which is presently the most advanced in the world, as a background, the author elaborates the intellectual principle behind image guidance. On the basis of a new guidance model, called "organisms", the visual guidance and the development of intellectualization are analysed. Meanwhile, the difficulties which are likely to occur are also revealed in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 8098 single-chip microcomputer adaptive controller developed in PL/M high-level language
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The real-time adaptive controller is generally complicated because its algorithm involves a large amount of computations. The assemble language has its inherent disadvantage of low efficiency and maintenance difficulties. This paper presents the developing method of 8098 single-chip microcomputer adaptive controller with PL/M high level language, by which the efficiency of designing and debugging is enhanced greatly. The design of identification and adaptive control algorithms, and high precision A/D and D/A conversions are discussed in the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reasoning about motion: product theories of motion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes a technique of combining two theories to obtain a combined theory called the product theory. We combine theories of time and space to obtain a product theory useful in modeling motion and motion planning. We begin by combining propositional temporal logic (PTL) with itself to obtain a two dimensional temporal logic (2D-TL). 2D-TL is expressive enough to represent useful motion information. Though PTL itself is decidable, we are able to express any instance of the post correspondence problem as a formula of 2D-TL. This proves 2D-TL to be undecidable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A general switchbox router with via minimization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Proposes a new switchbox router based on the segment assignment for circular routing. In fact, our switchbox router is divided into three phases: the iterative phase, the merging phase and the via minimization phase, to solve the routing specification. As a result, many benchmark examples have been tested on the proposed switchbox router. The routing results on all of these benchmark examples are routed successfully in the routing region. In addition to the successful routing on these switchboxes, our switchbox router is compared with other switchbox routers with respect to the number of vias and the wire lengths.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a slow frequency hopped radio modem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper a slow frequency hopped radio modem is designed for use in a licence-free frequency band (known as the ISM band). The design emphasis is on the hopped frequency synchronization. To evaluate the performance, a frequency hopped system is set up using the software package SPW allowing the consideration of various forms of interference. Implementation using DSP chips is also conducted. Testing has shown that this modem is very practical for commercial use and can be used as mobile modem in a multiple access system with the existence of multipath fading and other interference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of fan filters with arbitrary angle and /spl plusmn/45/spl deg/ orientation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Fan filters with arbitrary angle and orientation are used in geographical and image data processing, so the design of fan filters is very important in the field of signal processing; however, most algorithms cannot be used to design this kind of fan filter. In the paper, a method to design fan filters with arbitrary angle and /spl plusmn/45/spl deg/ orientation is introduced. Because some approximation techniques are used, the method is very simple. Experiments show that the cut-off frequency contours are very close to the idle ones.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multilayer perceptron structures applied to adaptive echo canceller for ISDN subscriber loops
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Echo cancellation is the main method used to realize two wire full-duplex transmission on ISDN subscriber loops. In the data echo canceller there exists nonlinear echo distortion which comes mainly from the A/D or D/A convertor. A conventional FIR filter is not sufficient to cancel this nonlinear distortion. In this paper a nonlinear echo canceller using a multilayer neural network is described. The coefficients of the multilayer perceptron are adaptively adjusted by a back-propagation algorithm. The computer simulation shows that by using a neural echo canceller nonlinear echo distortion can be effectively cancelled. The performance of the neural echo canceller is better than that of the conventional FIR echo canceller.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A universal real-time controller capable of fast calculation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: There is wide need of real-time controller having both fast calculation capability and flexible control ability for industrial applications. It is well known that a digital signal processor has the advantage of fast and strong calculation, but lacks strong control functions. This paper describes a universal microcomputer-based real-time controller supported by an IBM-PC, and it consists of a DSP56001 application development system (DSP ADS), and a M68HC11 EVB evaluation board, etc. It is easy to satisfy the above-mentioned requirement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Standardized parallel sorting on SIMD array processor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We present the standardized parallel sorting algorithm. Instead of the most basic CCI (compare and conditional interchange) operation in traditional sorting algorithms, this algorithm compares sorting data with a standard value sequence simultaneously and synchronously on an SIMD array processor. The algorithm possesses three significant advantages. First, the running time T is independent of the problem size, T=0(1). The second attractive feature of the algorithm is that it is not necessary to build a communication network between PEs. Finally, no bottleneck occurs in output. We have implemented the algorithm in an SIMD array processor that is designed by our research group. The experiment verifies all the theoretical predictions. For these merits the algorithm is of significance in both theory and practice.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and low level control of the USTB multifingered robot hand
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Stable grasping and fine manipulation with the multifingered robot hands are playing an increasingly important role in manufacturing and other application that require precision and dexterity. This paper describes a new two-thumbs USTB multifingered robot hand. The authors have developed a multifingered robot hand well suited to flexible grasping, dextrous manipulation, and capable of autonomous objects shape adaptation. This paper deals with mechanical configuration, multi-level control system architecture and low level control strategy of the USTB hand. A description of the software function that implements position control is also given. Finally, future work and directions of control aspects for the USTB hand are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The construction of an open INMS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper analyses the continuity, compatibility and inheritance of network evolution, points out the existence and complexity of second order information and gives an open intelligent integrated network management system model that can adapt to continuous network evolution. The author discusses design concerns, and analyses the interactions between the managing and managed entities within a network element which influence the network element evolution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: One step coordination procedure in real time application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: One step coordination procedure is introduced allowing a real time implementation of the control process. An online operating algorithm is developed, presenting the optimal operating rules of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive controller for an HVDC power system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents the derivation, design, and evaluation of an adaptive controller for an HVDC transmission system. The control strategy is to minimize the variance between outputs and set points. The controller parameters are directly estimated from input-output data by a simple recursive algorithm. Interesting results from both digital simulation and laboratory simulators are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Survey of formal description techniques (FDTs) for protocol converter design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Protocol conversion is one of the very important research areas in protocol engineering. It is an effective approach to provide interconnectivity and interoperability between two different protocols. A protocol converter is a very complex piece of software, and its design must be precise and complete to provide the expected conversions. Formal description techniques (FDTs), which have formal syntax and semantics, are useful tools for its design. In this paper, we present a survey of existing and widely adopted FDTs, which has been made in view of the requirements of protocol converter design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Topological designs of broadband customer access networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In an effort to minimize per-subscriber cost for broadband customer access networks, their topologies are considered in the overall design of the broadband networks. This paper examines three different service scenarios and describes four general network architectures for broadband customer access network. We finds that an active double star network is most suitable for a business area, while a passive double star network is for an urbanised residential area. The service requirements of a newly developed residential area can be satisfied by either an optical bus or a self-healing ring network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some supporting tools for the algebraic specification of data types
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The algebraic specification technique is one of the most influential formal methods in software engineering. In this paper, we describe some supporting tools for writing, verifying and executing algebraic specifications. Examples are given to illustrate the use of these tools.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel associative memory model applied to handwritten character recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel associative memory model used for setting up a handwritten Alpha character recognition system. This special kind of associative memory model, is of the simple algorithm operations needed for training and recall. It is also easy to understand and is very fast, even in simulations on sequential computers. Furthermore, due to the binary weights of synapses, it is very suitable for implementations using digital VLSI technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Steady-state stability analysis of a power system containing power system stabilizers and SMES controllers: a comparative study
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents the results of a comparative study of two damping controllers, i.e., the power system stabilizer (PSS) and the superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) controller, on damping generator oscillations. The developed scheme employs proportional-integral-derivative (PID) damping controllers to enhance the damping of both the mechanical mode and exciter mode of the studied power system. The parameters of the proposed controllers are determined by using a unified approach based on modal control theory. A frequency-domain approach based on root loci analysis and a time-domain approach based on nonlinear model simulations are accomplished in order to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed schemes and to compare the different damping effects provided by two damping controllers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two channel CPFSK coherent FDM fiber communication system at 154 Mbit/s
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We describe an experimental 154 Mbit/s two-channel coherent FDM fiber communication system using external grating cavity lasers operating at 1546 nm. It includes a laser frequency stabilization IF servo-circuit consisting of an optical phase-locked loop used for IF frequency stabilization and direct current modulation of a wide range tunable laser with narrow linewidth. The receive sensitivity, measured at the output of the transmission link were -49.2 dBm and -47.8 dBm at a 10/sup -9/ error rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applications of digital controller in industrial control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The availability of computers and microprocessors has resulted in a steady increase of digital control applications. The system performance obtained is quite satisfactory in comparison to the continuous case. This paper presents the study of various digital control strategies. For the self-tuning controller some approaches are investigated and evaluated. The comparison of the different controllers and influence of various algorithms or function blocks are also illustrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Three-dimensional object modeling for computer vision using artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Presents a neural network method for modeling 3D objects and discusses its potential applications in computer vision. Various 3D object models with freeform surfaces and different textures can be generated using this method, by training the network based on the main geometric features of the objects. It is also very flexible and capable of providing the different photometric geometries which are desired in many computer vision applications. Experimental results indicate that the method can be used as a modeling tool in computer vision.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Model predictive control for a class of nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper a two-level model predictive control algorithm for affine nonlinear systems is presented. A static nonlinear state feedback is at first designed to obtain an I/O linearized closed-loop system. A model predictive control algorithm is then adopted for the closed-loop system to achieve good dynamics and robustness. The effectiveness of the algorithm is also verified by the simulation example of an inverted pendulum on a cart.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The new three phase VFVA sine wave generator and the speed control of cycloconverter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new three phase VFVA sine wave generator is presented in this paper. The authors describe the three-phase reference sine wave which is produced by this generator's circuit and is required by a cycloconverter which is also presented. The authors also introduce the speed control and harmonics analysis of a variable frequency cycloconverter. A new sample-and-hold three-phase VFVA sine wave generator principle, circuit and experimentation waveforms are introduced. The principle of this sample-and-hold circuit is simple and the realization of hardware circuit is easy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A tolerance design method based on orthogonal array optimization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper introduces a method of tolerance design based on orthogonal array method. By determining the center and radius of the maximum sphere inside an acceptable region, the optimal center values and tolerance assignment can be defined. The process of tolerance design is being simplified since it uses the orthogonal array optimization method. The paper gives two examples to illustrate that the design method is correct and feasible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advanced curve and surface design in CAD system using STEP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, methods and techniques newly developed are presented for high-quality curve and surface modeling in CAD systems. The data structure and data exchange are based on STEP, the international standard for external representation of product data. While accurate algebraic representation is used for lower degree curves and surfaces, NURBS (Nonuniform Rational Bspline Surface) representation is adopted as a unified approach to advanced curve and surface design. We thus have both advantages for accurate shape processing in CAD/CAM and high-quality design of shapes with free-form surfaces.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Viterbi hardware implementation for GSM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a novel Viterbi decoder hardware implementation, with the code rate R=1/2 and the constraint length K=5, for the GSM land mobile system. With the use of one XILINX FPGA 3090 chip to replace the ACSs' function, which results in a much simpler hardware and routing structure, this system makes the final ASIC fabrication a very direct consequence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Specifications and measurements of service areas coverage for mobile radio systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper briefly reviews the behavior of mobile radio signals and the performance of radio mobile systems associated with its service area coverage. Two methods of specifying the area coverage are defined. With the area coverage clearly defined, together with the definitions of shadow areas and the associated integrating time, the area coverage of any mobile radio system can be clearly specified. The specifications used for an actual system are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Structural disambiguation using statistical information and the measurement of confidence in attachment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, we propose a statistical approach to structural disambiguation of verbal phrase attachment. Instead of handcoded semantic knowledge that raises knowledge acquisition bottleneck problem, collocations are proposed to be used for structural disambiguation. Since some types of structural ambiguity cannot be resolved using simple collocations, they are augmented with information-theoretic concept of mutual information. The augmented collocations can be automatically acquired from a corpus. From the concept of mutual information, a new concept of confidence measure is derived that can be used for indicating how reliable the attachment is.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance comparison between DAR and FR in grid topology circuit switched networks on common channel signaling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The performance of grid topology circuit switched networks using DAR (dynamic adaptive routing) or FR (flood routing) are compared in order to select an adequate routing protocol. The call setup time, which is the key measurement of performance evaluation in circuit switched networks, has been obtained based on estimated voice traffic. In the grid topology network, the common channel signaling method, is used to establish the path from the source to the destination. The performance of FR is better than that of DAR, under light traffic load. However, the performance of DAR is better than that of FR, under heavy traffic load or in a large network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A control system with the computer used on 35t/h fluidized bed utility boiler
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A real-time closed loop control system using microcomputer, which has been used for the control of two 35t/h fluidized bed boilers in practice, is introduced in this paper. The overall control scheme, including eighteen loops i.e. level of steam drum, temperature of superheat steam, steam pressure, bed temperature, vacuum of combustion chamber, rest of fluidizing air and bed height, are presented. Its main features are that the boiler load is adjusted by the bed temperature associating with the bed height, while water supply and steam temperature adjustment are decoupled. The hardware and the software of the system as well as the anti-interference measures are introduced, and some plots of experimental results are also given. The techniques developed in the paper can be spread in the field of fluidized bed boiler, and also have application to other control systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust control algorithms for robot manipulators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A robust computed torque problem is considered in this paper. By representing the error model as a block structured uncertainty model, the problem is formulated as a robust feedback controller design problem for systems with parameter uncertainties and an optimal input/ouput scaled H/sub /spl infin// stabilization approach is presented for synthesizing controllers which robustly stabilizes the linear system with the structured uncertainties. An application example for a two-link manipulator is given, and the simulation results of the proposed method for the uncertain dynamics are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Abductive networks applied to synthetical evaluation of complex systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We introduce the concept and method of the abductive network and discuss the characteristic of the economic system. Based on this, we use a special kind of abductive network, ie., neural networks to construct a model of evaluation for local economic development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Studies on the flight performance optimization of commercial aircrafts
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A thorough research on the flight trajectory optimization techniques with energy-state approach is conducted in this paper. The point-mass energy-state approximation model and the trajectory optimization principle and algorithms based on this model are first summarized. The fixed-time 4D trajectory optimization is then discussed, and the associated iteration algorithm is developed. The step-climb mode optimization principle and method are considered and discussed. An algorithm simplification approach based on modelling the optimized results for specific aircraft model is presented and discussed, aimed to reduce the computation requirement amount so as to enhance its on-board real-time implementation property. Digital simulations and some specific modelling results for a Boeing-707 transport aircraft model are presented and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Extended rendezvous mechanism of Ada to improve the level of parallelism
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Rendezvous in Ada is a synchronous communication mechanism between tasks that are executed concurrently. It is a useful concept for task interaction. This paper proposes the extended rendezvous mechanism using the agent task to reduce the suspended time of tasks at the point of rendezvous and to improve the level of parallelism. The agent task is an intermediate task as an interface between two tasks carrying out the rendezvous. It receives the message needed in a rendezvous from a calling task, and makes an accepting task to perform the rendezvous. The extended rendezvous mechanism executes the rendezvous using this agent task. In spite of increment of the agent tasks and the complexity of programs it shows that the extended rendezvous is efficient than the standard rendezvous stated in ALRM (Ada Language Reference Manual).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robustness of signal correlation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The robustness of signal correlation is of paramount importance if signal correlation is to be used effectively in the real world. The paper examines the robustness of speech correlation based on the average correlation between adjacent speech frames. The effects of the speech frame size, the amount of amplitude distortion and the amount of gaussian noise on the correlation property are studied. Simulation results show that the optimum speech analysis frame size is in the region of 15 to 20 msec. The speech correlation property is found to be robust even when the amplitude of the speech signal is infinitely clipped. It can also withstand fairly high gaussian noise and has numerous applications in the field of speech coding, speech enhancement and speech analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive multi-thresholds detection algorithms for finding little targets of maritime ship
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A serious degradation of detection probability(P/sub d/) in a conventional cell-averaging constant alarm rate (CA-CFAR) detector is known to be caused by the presence of interfering targets in the set of reference cells. A new CFAR detection algorithm of multithreshold in which three tentative estimates of the noise level in the test cell are obtained by independently processing output of the leading and the lagging cells is proposed and studied. The performance of multi-threshold CFAR detector is analyzed in both a benign environment and in an environment of an arbitrary number of interferers in the sample set. A Rayleigh fluctuation target mode (Swerling Case I) is used as a model for the received signal. The results have been applied in Radar Station. The practical testing results show that the multi-thresholds detector has good performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systolizing the covariance analysis of linear predictive coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A systolic array for the covariance analysis of linear predictive coding is developed in this paper. The covariance analysis of linear predictive coding can be computed with a large set of irregular and nested recurrence equations. Systolizing the algorithm is a difficulty task. The task is first decomposed and then mapped onto several interconnected systolic arrays.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to improve the accuracy of the angle measured in multi-target situation for OTH radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The sum and difference amplitude comparison method of a secondary surveillance radar is conventional in azimuthal direction indication but is effected by much azimuthal errors, especially by the multiple-targets situation. After a discussion of azimuthal estimation techniques and performance, with special reference to the OTH HF radar applications, a novel estimation, which is called MSMWSA (method of symbol maximum and weighted sidelobe averaging), for this radar is described. The proposed technique is a close approximation of the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) taking into account the receiver characteristics as well as the multiple-targets situation. The performances, obtained by analysis and computer simulation, are compared with those of a traditional estimator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of robustness theory in the analysis of subsynchronous oscillation [of power systems]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the applicability of the recently developed frequency-domain, matrix-norm robustness theory for the analysis of subsynchronous oscillations in a power system is explored. Based upon structure preserving multivariable feedback model, a set of new robustness theorems are developed. These theorems can be used to analyse the effects of parameter perturbations on the stability of subsynchronous oscillations in a power system and can provide useful measures for evaluating the tolerance of the system to modeling errors. An example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of these theorems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of stability of an optical phase-locked loop
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on an improved model of an optical phase-locked loop (OPLL) and the rate equations of an external cavity semiconductor laser, the effects of OPLL feedback on the stability of the external cavity semiconductor laser are discussed. The conditions for the local laser working stably with the phase-locking feedback are established.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New functions of cellular neural network: image restoration and symmetrization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Two new functions of the cellular neural network (CNN), image restoration and image symmetrization, are introduced. When the feedback operator, control operator and bias current of the CNN have been chosen properly, the image information is processed by the CNN under the control of these templates, resulting in the restoration or symmetrization of the image. Some examples of image restoration and symmetrization are given in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On evaluating the performance of error-correcting codes in lasercom PPM systems with direct detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A simple method of evaluating the maximum likelihood (ML) decoding performance in coded pulse position modulation (PPM) laser communication (lasercom) systems with direct detection is given for both shot-noise limited Poisson and thermal-noise limited avalanche photodetection (APD) receivers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust adaptive controller for nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The basic concept of the design of a dynamic neural controller is discussed with emphasis on the control problem. A general neural network is used to design the controller motivated by the robust linear controller design method. The method unifies the nonlinear components in the controller and the plant. This scheme simplifies the structure of the dynamic neural controller and modeling. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the new method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical implementation of 3-phase and 3-level microprocessor sampled PWM techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Two methods for practically implementing 3-level PWM sampling schemes for a 12-device inverter bridge are presented. They offer advantages of reducing the computational requirements for implementing them, as well as the ability of programming wider PWM pulses into a microprocessor. Wider PWM pulses result in a more accurate practical representation of the PWM waveform. One scheme offers the additional advantage of reduced potential shift between system neutral and load star points. The benefits gained are at the expense of an error introduced to the harmonic spectra. Graphical and tabulated results are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Continuous time performance analysis for a hierarchical routing algorithm in Manhattan street networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The Manhattan street network (MSN) is a directed network with a link topology that resembles the one-way system of streets and avenues in midtown Manhattan. It is designed for packet communications in a local or metropolitan area. In order to improve on the delay-throughput performance of the random routing algorithm yet keep its properties of simplicity and flexibility, a hierarchical deflection routing algorithm is proposed. We conduct theoretical analyses of this routing algorithm in continuous time for both the store and forward model and the virtual cut-through model, and compare the results for both models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transaction management in multi-user CAD environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We analyse engineering design process and point out its three properties of long duration, exploration and cooperation. We survey related work of concurrency control for advanced database applications and describe our transaction management system aimed to meet the demands of design process involving many users, which contains three simple and kernel mechanisms that is, checkout/checkin, savepoint/rollback and notification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Security management on mobile-phone communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The cellular mobile-phone system has developed over a quarter of a century, and most features are mature, but not the security management. The security problem arises due to the popularity of the mobile-phone, and the advanced technology, because of the disclosure of information. However, the disclosure of information cannot be avoided, so, the information must be encoded before transmission. In order to distinguish between the encrypted and the original message; the extended-message field in the overhead message can be used as an indicator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic motion compensated video coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The performance of the dynamic motion compensation (DMC) for video compression is evaluated using test sequences, in comparison with what is recommended in the MPEG coding algorithm. The DMC method is introduced to minimize the redundancy in motion vectors of block matching motion compensation. The DMC can be divided into two categories: spatial dynamic motion compensation (SDMC) and temporal dynamic motion compensation (TDMC). The spatial dynamic compensation algorithms are described. A very efficient modified full search algorithm for blocking matching motion compensation is then presented. The run-length and variable length coding (VLC) are applied to code dynamic motion information to further the reduction of the side information required for the coding. The effectiveness of these algorithms is examined and evaluated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive implementation of the MPEG encoder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Due to the huge amount of data contained in digital video signals, the compression of video signals becomes crucial and important when the storage and transmission of digital video information are required. Most compression algorithms use motion compensated predictive coding to remove temporal redundancy and transformation coding to remove spatial redundancy. Additional entropy coding algorithms are also used to further reduce the amount of data in representing the compressed video information. With such a structure, a MPEG standard for video compression has been established by the International Standard Organization (ISO). The same compression techniques can be easily generalized to encode high definition (HD) video. In the paper, the authors propose a novel structure for encoding HD video, which provides an adaptive coding structure without any additional computations than those conventionally used. Since the temporal correlation is utilized during the encoding process to remove temporal redundancy, it is expected to produce a savings of bit rate in the reconstructed HD video.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real-time neural computation of the eigenvectors of a matrix
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper proposes a neural network approach for computing in real-time the eigenvectors corresponding to all the eigenvalues of a matrix. We show that the proposed neural network is guaranteed to be stable and to provide the desired eigenvectors with arbitrarily small error during an elapsed time of only a few characteristic time constants of the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear connections of a feedback neural network and its associative ability analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A feedback neural network, of which input elements are connected nonlinearly, is studied. The network's associative characteristics and ability are discussed, and the learning algorithms are derived. We propose the idea of the equivalent weight subset of the neural network, and by means of this concept, the nonlinearly connected network is made much simpler and the complexity of the weight matrix is lowered. Furthermore, when a pattern is learned by the network, not only the pattern itself but also its shift variance can be recognized by the network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Knowledge-level modeling based on TRSA method
