publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper proposes a knowledge-level modeling method, called TRSA, which describes a task structure (i.e. the abstract structure for a problem-solving task) by means of task reduction and describes the reasoning activities for the subtasks included in the task structure by means of subtask association. As conceptual models of problem-solving processes, task structures can be constructed dynamically according to the features of application domains and the requirement of problem solving tasks. Hence, they can become the constraints and guide for acquiring reasoning knowledge and maintaining knowledge bases. In addition, a visual, interactive, structural modeling language and a symbol-level functional architecture are provided to support TRSA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the optimality of decentralized filtering systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: For the multisensor systems, the decentralized information structure can improve the fault-tolerant ability and increase the processing speed. This paper presents the necessary and sufficient condition for the optimality of decentralized linear dynamic filters, i.e., the decentralized filter is equal to the centralized filters. It is pointed out that this condition is satisfied only in rare case. However, by analyzing federated filter presented by Carlson (1990), we show that it is possible to obtain optimal decentralized filters with the modified information structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of the Alliant FX/2800
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes the Alliant FX/2800, a shared-memory multiprocessor system based on Intel i860. Up to four processors are used, so the system has a peak performance of 160 MFlops. This paper presents some performance results and characteristics of the parallelising C compiler.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integration of LD-CELP and echo canceller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new scheme to handle the echo canceller as an on-side job of a LD-CELP codec is studied in the paper. The authors give a novel approach to integrate the echo canceller (CCITT G.165) into the LD-CELP codec, such as CCITT G.728 "Coding of speech at 16 kbps using low-delay code-excited linear prediction" codec.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Solving equations and inequations in term algebras with selectors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We address the problem of handling selector functions in solving equations and inequations over trees. We introduce a selector elimination transform and show how Colmerauer's method (1984) can be used with this transform.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new algorithm for vector quantizer design based on multi-codebook
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An efficient algorithm for the design of a vector quantizer (VQ) is developed for use on a long training sequence of data in the paper. The algorithm is based on multiple codebooks, and a multi-codebook vector quantizer (MCVQ) can be obtained. With microcomputer simulation, it shows that the algorithm for VQ design based on the multi-codebook is able to reduce the computational complexity of the VQ. In addition, the storage requirements of the MCVQ is not increased compared with the conventional fully search vector quantizer (FSVQ) based on single codebook.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High performance fiber-coupled Fabry-Perot interferometers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new type of fiber-coupled Fabry-Perot (FCFP) interferometers have been designed out, by which a much larger range of cavity lengths has been obtained. FCFPs, which contain free spectral range (FSR) from 20 GHz to 10000 GHz, Finesse up to 250 and insertion loss as low as 2.5 dB, have been built. The devices are piezoelectrically tuned.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallelising image processing algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Multiprocessor machines provide increased computational power and memory capacity that can be used to achieve tasks involving large amounts of data, such as imaging. With multiprocessor machines, many sophisticated operations on image data can be accomplished within reasonable time constraints. In order to efficiently utilize multiprocessor machines, conventional image processing algorithms have to be parallelised. The design of parallel algorithms takes into account many considerations, e.g. interprocessor communication, load balancing, task division, task placement, scalability, network topology, etc. In this paper, the performance of some image processing algorithms running on a loosely-coupled multiprocessor machine is evaluated. The machine consists of a PC host computer and a multiprocessor network consisting of a number of transputers. The configuration of this transputer network is under software control and so different parallelisations of a particular algorithm can be tested on a particular network topology. Three image processing algorithms were selected for parallelisation. They are the Sobel edge operation, the fast Fourier transform and the Hough transform. Parallelism is achieved in various approaches, such as partitioning of tasks or partitioning of data. For a particular network configuration, the performance of different parallelisation approaches for each algorithm was assessed, based on the parallel processing time, overhead time, communication-to-computation ratio, efficiency, etc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Variational approach to soliton propagation in long fibers with lumped amplifiers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The premphasis method in long distance soliton transmission is investigated by means of variational approach. The results agree well with that of the direct numerical method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of self-tuning controller to an air heating process
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Extended horizon and k-incremental self-tuning controllers were implemented using a microcomputer on a laboratory scale air heating process. The performance of these controllers is evaluated and compared with a digital PID controller. The results obtained indicate that the self-tuning controllers could improve the performance of the process significantly compared to the digital PID controller.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quantum series resonant inverter for a DC motor drive
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a quantum series resonant inverter (QSRI) is utilized as a DC motor drive. A sampled data dynamic modeling including a QSRI and a DC motor is newly proposed to obtain an effective analytical tool for the analysis. Based on this model, an optimal predictive resonant current (OPRC) control technique minimizing the current error is developed and its advantages over the other types of current control techniques are comparatively discussed. In view of the current ripple and offset current, near optimum operational mode patterns can be obtained using the proposed OPRC control technique. The usefulness of an OPRC controlled QSRI for a DC motor drive with 4 quadrant operation is verified by employing the motor current and speed controllers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer processing and pattern recognition of radar remote sensing images of the Huai River basin
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Introduces remote sensing image processing and recognition. Because the radar remote sensing and image processing system makes errors and the image has distortion, the authors adopt gradient and linear regression to correct the grey distortion and use the multinomial warping method to rectify geometric distortion. The authors use a supervised classification and recognition method to analyze the remotely sensed images and to provide flooding distribution maps and data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robustness and stability margin of dynamical systems with structured uncertainties
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, robustness and stability margin of linear or nonlinear systems are discussed. First, the robustness in linear or nonlinear dynamical systems with structured uncertainties is argued through the simultaneous Lyapunov inequalities. In order to find the common positive definite matrix P of the inequalities or to solve the so-called common Lyapunov problem, the P-region method proposed by the authors is roughly explained. Next, it is shown that the P-region corresponds to the robustness of systems, and the limit of the stability margin can be determined by the limit of the P-region. Also, as an example, the algebraic solution for the stability margin is compared with the numerical one.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of the amplified spontaneous emission in erbium-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A computer model for the evolution of the amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) spectrum of the erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs) is presented. In particular, the temperature dependence of the ASE at the important wavelengths of 1.535 /spl mu/m and 1.552 /spl mu/m are evaluated. The results are then compared with the experimental ones to verify the validity of the theoretical ASE model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple robust self-tuning controller in the presence of unmodeled dynamics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A modified self-tuning control algorithm is proposed in the paper. The proposed algorithm assures global robust stability of the system with an invertable stable plant in the presence of unmodeled dynamics of the plant. Simulation results have shown the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Arden - Architecture Development Environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes Arden, which is being developed to help architecture design. Arden includes a retargetable compiler and a back-end simulation tool that uses the concepts of object-oriented programming (OOP) to achieve model reusability. The code generator in the Arden compiler uses a tree pattern matching method for instruction selection. An experimental bottom-up matching algorithm that reduces the pattern matching to a numerical computation problem can reduce the space complexity and the search time. A useful instruction description language has been proposed to simplify the architecture specifications. We have implemented the DLX architecture with only 49 rules. Arden has been able to output DLX assembly code and has the same performance as GNU cc output.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PQ-coupled difference equation model for power system load
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a second order PQ-coupled difference equation load model (PQ-DELM) is derived, which takes the interrelation between active and reactive currents into account. Load modeling is revealed to be a closed loop identification problem, and for the parameter estimation of the PQ-DELM an instrumental variable (IV) algorithm is put forward. The field test of actual load and the test in the laboratory validate the PQ-DELM and the IV algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Visualization techniques for various programming paradigms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper illustrates the variety of visualization techniques that are employed for various programming paradigms, examining the type of information required and the advantages that the information provides the programmer. We examine the specific visualization requirements for each paradigm and the general requirements of visualization systems which depict the flow of control for both sequential and parallel program execution. We find that many of the visualization systems currently available tend to focus on only one aspect of the visualization requirements rather than the broad base of needs of the programmer. The need to integrate these visualization systems in the future is highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Decision support system for thermal power plant siting (SDSS)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: On the basis of new technologies such as fuzzy sets, analytic hierarchy process and expert systems etc., a practical decision support system for thermal power plant siting (SDSS) has been set up and is presented in this paper. SDSS, as displayed on the PC screen, consists of ten parts: introduction, system maintenance, individual decision, clear database, consultation, auxiliary operation, multiple decision, sensitivity analysis, graph system and exit. SDSS can help decision makers to make individual decisions and multiple decisions on the site alternatives, in the preliminary feasibility study stage for thermal power plant siting, then it outputs the decision results and their certainty factors. SDSS not only can explain its reasoning process, decision results and rules in detail but also provide some expert conclusions in special fields for users. Guided by the domain experts SDSS can modify or enlarge its knowledge base easily. Through changing the weights of the criteria SDSS can do a sensitivity analysis on any site alternative if the users want. SDSS has good flexibility and can be used as a frame structure to form the expert systems in other fields. The man-machine interface in SDSS is clear and audio-visual, the decision results can be shown in all kinds of displays. SDSS can be applied to the other domains and the designing institutes throughout the country. Application of SDSS to the site selection of Wu Shashan, Ying Longshan, Qiang Jiao along the Zhe Jiang coast obtained a good result.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real time data compression for power system monitoring using programmable gate array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The importance of real-time monitoring and evaluation of power supply quality is not over emphasised. Nowadays, almost all modern power system control centres are equipped with computer based data-acquisition systems. A new implementation using a programmable gate array for compression and restoration of digitised signals is presented in this paper. The proposed methodology offers various merits such as low effectiveness, high speed, high compression ratio and full accuracy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and implementation of the application layer protocol for real time data communications in electric power system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper introduces the national industry standard "DL-476-92 the application layer protocol for real time data communications in electric power system ", issued by the Ministry of Energy, People's Republic of China, in April of 1992. The authors are members of the protocol development working group.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A debugging tool for distributed systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes parts of the design of a debugger for a distributed real-time multimedia system. Emphasis lies on the distributed aspect of debugging, which means that attention is paid to the external behaviour of the processes. This type of debugging is useful to find communication or synchronization errors. However, experience shows that this is not enough: the debugger must also provide hooks for the user to use traditional sequential debuggers. This type of debugging focuses on the internal behaviour - or internal logic - of processes. For the sequential debugging part a normal debugger like GDB can be taken. Three key elements of the debugger are events, filters and recognizers. By definition events are the lowest level of system activity that may be observed by the event debugger. Filters are applied to remove events from the stream of events produced by the debuggee that are of no interest for the programmer. Recognizers are used to recognize behaviour -right or wrong- of the system. By combining events, different levels of abstraction are introduced, thus alleviating the task of the programmer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A backward protocol verification method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Using the formal Communication Finite State Machine (CFSM) model, a communication protocol consists of several communicating entities which can be represented in some CFSMs. Global state reachability analysis is one of the most straightforward ways to automatically detect logical errors in a communication protocol specified in the CFSM model. Global state reachability analysis generates all of the reachable global states and checks the correctness one by one. Even though communication protocols are error free, global state reachability analysis still needs to be executed completely. We propose a new verification method which is called the backward protocol verification method, to detect logical errors. By analyzing the properties of deadlock error, unspecified reception error, and channel overflow error, some candidate erroneous global states are generated. Then, each candidate global state is checked whether there is a path, i.e., a global state sequence connects to the original initial global state. If there is a path, then the candidate global state is really an erroneous global state and the communication protocol does have some logical errors. Otherwise, if there is no candidate global state or none of the candidate global state has a path, then the communication protocol is error free.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A statistical circuit simulator for designing tunable circuits
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a statistical circuit simulator for the selection of tuning components is described. Using this simulator, a circuit designer can make an appropriate solution on the selection of tuning component as well as an estimate of the yield for manufacturing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct segmentation for 3D medical images
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new algorithm for direct 3D segmentation is presented. The algorithm combines region growing, edge detection and a new edge preserving smoothing method. The combined method helps to avoid characteristic segmentation errors which occur when using region growing or edge detection separately. Boundary modification is also introduced to overcome noise in the boundary location and ensure more realistic region boundaries. The algorithm has been validated through application to medical image visualisation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Catastrophe theory model of multimachine power systems for transient stability studies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A catastrophe theory model of interconnected multimachine power systems is proposed for the study of transient stability problems. The swing equations are put in the form of one of the elementary catastrophes-the swallowtail catastrophe. The manifold of the catastrophe defines the boundary between transient stability and instability in terms of three control variables, which are functions of the parameters and operating conditions of the power system. Thus stability is easily assessed from the system parameters and operating conditions; no solution of the swing equations is required. The catastrophe model is used to check the transient stability of the system by considering that one or more generators are critical. Results are given for the simplified WSCC system of three generators and for the seven-machine CIGRE system. The catastrophe theory results compare favourably with the time-solution results for the systems for the same three-phase short-circuit disturbances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of simplified adaptive control to position control of a 3-axis robot
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper examines the applicability of simplified adaptive control (SAC) technique to an actual system, that is, position control of a 3-axis robot, and verifies that experimental results illustrate satisfactory control performance. In the algorithm, a feedforward gain is proposed to be inserted in parallel to a reference model as well as to the controlled system in order to decrease steady-state error, and this proposition is theoretically analyzed. In the experiments, control performances are compared between the SAC and a conventional PID control. The comparison shows superiority of the SAC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural network controller for queueing in packet switch networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Packet switching is an important technology in broadband ISDN (B-ISDN). The authors propose neural networks architecture for two kinds of queueing in packet switch networks to gain maximum throughput. First they introduce a new energy function for the input queueing. Then they propose a modified input smoothing scheme, which can obtain higher throughput than the standard input smoothing scheme, and its control by neural network. Finally, computer simulation results are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An architecture for a distributed deductive database system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a three level architecture for a distributed deductive database system which extends the power of distributed database systems to include deductive capabilities. It allows both knowledge-based and data-based information to be shared by the sites of a computer network in order to process user queries. The benefits and the possible ways of segregating the rule base into different clusters are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach to digital control implementation of continuous-time systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A transformation method which is based on block-pulse functions (BPF) expansion is proposed. Using this transformation method, an approximate solution of the continuous-time system under consideration can be obtained, and the control laws of the continuous-time system can also be discretized to get digital control algorithms. A case study of a model reference adaptive control system is described and the problem of how to reduce the amount of computations for a high order system is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural-network-based model reference adaptive control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents the learning algorithm of a neural network being applied to identification of affine nonlinear systems, and proposes a neural-network-based model reference adaptive control approach. The theorems on exponential stability of the system are proven. Simulation results show that this method is feasible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of remote procedure call based on ISO/OSI reference model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Describes a client-server distributed computing model which is established on an Ethernet-based LAN. Simple PCs are used as clients, and a high-performance i486 CICS processor workstation with an i860 RISC coprocessor is used as the server. Remote procedure call (RPC) facilities are designed and implemented for the above distributed processing system, to support remote compilation and remote program execution. An i860 RISC networked compiler is also designed to facilitate the use of the RISC server. The system is designed under the ISO/OSI reference model with modularization. It is also kept small and simple in its development, testing and debugging. The use of the RPC mechanism facilitate a high degree of programmer transparency. The client-server model is successfully built and its performance is evaluated. It is found that systems using the powerful RISC servers have superior performance compared to a PC running local applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A computer vision system for measurement of pedestrian volume
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This study applies image sequence analysis techniques to perform pedestrian volume measurement. A new algorithm, which consists of four steps, was proposed. The algorithm was capable of extracting pedestrian information from consecutive video images while eliminating vehicle information. The volume of the pedestrians crossing a detection area can be automatically derived by the algorithm. A computer vision system, called the Pedestrian Volume Measurement (PVM), was developed based on the algorithm. The significant advantage of the PVM system to previous systems was that the new system can be used at intersections where vehicle presence makes the previous systems not practicable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An integrated method for transient security assessment of power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new technique of determining the first swing stability limit of power systems by combining the equal area criterion (EEAC) method, the roots evaluation method and a fast numerical integration method is presented. The proposed method consists of two phases: prediction and correction. In the first phase, the EEAC method is adopted for critical clearing time (CCT) estimation considering that the EEAC method is extremely fast. In the second, the fast numerical integration method and roots evaluation method are combined and used for CCT correction. The method has been tested and practically implemented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of transient stability limits using artificial neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the nonlinear mapping relation between the transient energy margin and the generator power at different fault clearing time was established by using the multi-layer feedforward neural network of the perceptron type, Lyapunov's direct method based on the system dynamic equivalents was used as a fast method to obtain the training set of the artificial neural network (ANN), the transient stability power limits of the generator at different fault clearing time were estimated very quickly by ANN. The proposed approach has been tested on a practical 59-generator power system, and the results were found to be quite accurate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of silicon guided-wave electro-optic modulators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Presents both electrical and optical simulations of Si guided-wave electro-optic modulators. The simulation starts with design of modulators using a 2D semiconductor process simulator. The electrical properties of the modulators are analyzed by a 2D device simulator. Thereafter, the simulated electrical parameters are converted into optical parameters by proper electro-optic coefficients. The optical simulations are performed with both finite-difference-time-domain (FDTD) and mode-propagation-by-Fourier-expansion (MPFE) methods. The advantages of combining and using these two algorithms together are better accuracy and capability of analyzing arbitrarily shaped and optically large structures. The technique is illustrated by simulation and analysis of a series of Si guided-wave electro-optic modulators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Restoration of noisy images by the adaptive average differential iterative and the improved median filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In the literature there are many methods to restore noisy images. An adaptive differential iterative filter (AADIF) and an improved median filter (IMF) which suppress impulsive noise and Gaussian noise while preserving the image edges and details successfully, are analysed and evaluated in terms of their filtering performances under practical noise conditions. The signal-to-noise ratios in this experiment are from 0 dB to 17 dB. Besides the description of their algorithms, a great deal of experimental data are shown to support their efficacy. It is concluded that these two filters are highly competitive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new algorithm for computing optimal control of discrete-time systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents simple algorithm for solving the optimal control problems of discrete-time systems with constraints on control. In this algorithm, monotonous reduction of cost values at each iteration is guaranteed. It is proved that the converged control satisfies the Pontryagin type necessary conditions for optimality under some conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the design of a local switch for heterogenous multi-subsystem interconnect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Before heterogenous networks evolve to all-ATM, multimedia communications are likely to cross over different networks operated at various speeds and protocols. An effective multimedia interconnection network or the so called switching hub must be able to handle various traffic patterns such as continuous, isochronous and connectionless data. Due to the limitations of current implementation such as backplane bus and shared memory the authors present a new platform, multi-subsystem interconnect (MSI) model which is based on a parallel and fast packet switching technique. The main part of MSI is a time-multiplexed space division switching fabric with the capability of simultaneous path resolution and packet transfer. The whole structure consists of a set of reusable building blocks. In realization the interface hardware can be implemented with a few ASICs applicable for different subsystems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple method for studying the influence of bus loads on power system transient stability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Transient stability is an important problem in power systems. The influence of bus loads on power system transient stability is one of the main concerns by operators. This problem is studied and a simple method for studying the influence of bus loads on transient stability is presented in this paper. It can avoid recomputing the new power flow and reforming the reduced admittance matrices. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis can be used to speed up transient stability assessment. Some simulation results and comparisons are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An on-line diagnosis system integrates model-based and rule-based reasoning for manufacturing organization management
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an architecture of an on-line diagnosis system for manufacturing organization management. This diagnosis system consists of five component parts: a model base, a rule base, a diagnosis unit, and two interfaces. The functions of each part in this diagnosis system are described. An example about quality diagnosis in production management is given at the end of this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On LQ optimal control: a frequency approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to long-range predictive control based on a quadratic cost function. The controlled system is always described by an input-output, discrete time model, and the output predictions of the system which are required in the solution of the problem, are expressed in a new form which allows one to minimize the quadratic cost function in a way similar to in LQ optimal control. Then the resulting control law computes the control gain matrix via the solution of the standard Riccati equation. It is shown that quadratic predictive control synthesis from a input-output representation of systems can be viewed as a particular case of the general linear quadratic optimal control (LQG).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A combined neural network and hidden Markov model approach to speaker recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Presents a combination approach to text-independent speaker identification. The approach makes use of the strong classification power of an artificial neural network and the hidden Markov model's ability to handle the sequential character of speech. The combination approach is superior to both the neural network approach and the hidden Markov model approach in identification accuracy and computational complexity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Speed control of induction motor using fuzzy algorithm with hierarchical structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes a fuzzy logic controller for the speed control of induction motors. For changes of load inertia moment and load torque, the performance of speed controllers using a fuzzy algorithms with hierarchical structure and using conventional PI controllers is investigated. These controllers are applied to a laboratory model drive system with a 2.2 kW induction motor. Simulation and experimental results show that speed controllers using fuzzy algorithms are more robust than conventional PI controllers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive subsampling for image data compression
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Describes a two-to-one subsampler which allows an image to be transmitted in a layered format. Subsampling can be made adaptive to local activities of the image by using gradient measurements. Simulation results show that, for a typical outdoor scene, the picture quality in terms of the PSNR ranges from about 50 dB at 10% to 30 dB at 95% of the blocks of the image being subsampled. The DCT coefficients of the low-pass subsampled output remain highly compacted, so that further data reduction is possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On an amplitude constrained controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper investigates the stability of a closed-loop system when a one-step predictive control which is subject to a saturation constraint on the control variable, is applied to a stable system with an integrator. Then, generalization of a result of Chang and Evens (1987) is achieved by showing that stability in the sense of BIBO can be assured for the system with any kind of non-minimum phase behaviour.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct shape reconstruction of 3-D object from monocular shading image
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The method described in this paper for reconstructing the shape of Lambertain surfaces from the shading information inherent in a monocular image can deal with a surface whose image (a smooth and non-self-occluding one) is produced by orthographic projection with a parallel light source from a known direction. By dividing the image area into serial triangles, the intensity function I(x,y) on each triangle can be linearized. With the help of a support function and a transformation, it is proved that each triangle represents a cylinder in new X-Y coordinates with (s,t) as its surface gradient components. So, the ill-posed image brightness constraint equation in Cartesian coordinates can be solved in X-Y coordinates with only one variable (either s or t). It is necessary to find out, firstly, the pixel which has the maximal intensity, and then assign its depth leads for the direct recovery of the shape at each point, without the necessity of integration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a fuzzy learning controller and its application to robot manipulators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Fuzzy logic control schemes related by linguistic control rules have been gaining much attention as a method of intelligent control in recent years. However, a fuzzy controller is, in itself, a nonlinear controller having several parameters to be properly determined. In this paper, the authors propose a fuzzy learning controller which has an ability of generating and modifying the control rule-base, and tuning input/output gains for the iterative task. Through simulation studies on a linear time-invariant (LTI) single-input single-output (SISO) system, and a 2-link robot manipulator, the authors evaluate the performance of the proposed controller.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Steady-state stability criterion and uniqueness of load flow solutions for distribution systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The study of load flow solutions is one of the most important topics for power system research. For a distribution system, radial-type networks have been proven to have unique load flow solutions. In this paper, the Jacobian matrix determinant for a 2-bus system is developed to analyze the properties of its voltage solution. The 2-bus based analysis is then extended to distribution systems of fundamental radial and loop types. A method of checking the feasibility of the voltage solution is proposed. Numerical tests are also included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuzzy control of group elevators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new fuzzy control method for control of group elevators is proposed. An expert system that is used to realize the fuzzy control with a fuzzy control rule is built. It consists of a knowledge database whose rules are divided into production rules and fuzzy rules, inference decision part, traffic situation database, control commands and control equipment. Knowledge and experience of an expert about elevator group supervisory control are memorized and dispatched for the system in order to bring about control commands and to finish organization and monitoring. A new fuzzy rule that is the key to describe the dynamic features is studied. The fuzzy control is used to describe dynamic performances of group elevators. Based on the data stored in the expert knowledge database and the traffic process database, waiting time and distance time are calculated so that control commands for each elevator are sent out. Control format and use of fuzzy control are discussed. A fuzzy inference decision method that is the heart of fuzzy control is described. An optimum algorithm of car distribution of the elevator is obtained by the process of fuzzy inference decision. The control results, for an AI 2100 elevator, are examined. It has been shown that transfer ability of the elevator is increased greatly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The real-time measurement of non-sinusoidal AC electrical parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Recently, some monitoring projects, by means of embedded systems, have been carried out on AC machines . They all relate to the problem of real-time measurement of nonsinusoidal signals. This article gives the general principles of real-time measurement of nonsinusoidal AC electrical parameters and lays emphasis on some technical problems which occur in practice such as interruptions, real-time calculation, elimination of phase errors and smoothing filters for current signals. The discussion of these problems is of great importance both in theory and in practice.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrate CAD to CAPP/CAM with object oriented engineering database using STEP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We present an object-oriented engineering DBMS (OOEDBMS), named OSCAR-3, to support product data model in CAD/CAPP/CAM integration system. We introduce the characteristics of OSCAR-3, which are also indispensable for general OOEDBMS. Finally our future research directions are outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A three-phase linear systolic array SVD algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Singular value decomposition (SVD), one of the most basic and important tools of numerical linear algebra, is finding increasing application in digital signal processing. In this paper, a novel systolic array SVD algorithm is presented. It is suitable for implementing on a versatile one-dimensional array processor and has been implemented on the Linear Systolic Array Processor, LiSAP.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: D-stability for perturbed discrete systems with time delay
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the D-pole placement problem for perturbed discrete time delay systems. We propose a criterion which guarantees robust pole location of perturbed discrete time delay systems within a specified circular region. The explicit element bounds on linear time-invariant perturbations with highly structured information are obtained. An example is given to demonstrate the result.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Suppression of subsynchronous resonance using phase shifter controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a study on the application of static phase shifters to stabilize subsynchronous torsional oscillations in the IEEE Second Benchmark Model, system-1. In order to effectively suppress the unstable torsional modes in different operating conditions, a unified approach based on modal control theory is proposed and a set of static phase shifter controllers (SPSC) are designed. The effectiveness of the proposed damping scheme is demonstrated by using the frequency-domain approach based on eigenvalue analyses and the time-domain approach based on dynamic response simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new means of "TX-to-RX" control in mobile radio-to-telephone interconnect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: With the development of mobile communication, mobile networks must connect with the telephone network and mobile radio-to-telephone interconnect is used more and more. When it operates in a simplex mode, the control of transmitter to receiver (TX-to-RX) link is difficult. The current radio-to-telephone interconnects are almost all using VOX (voice operated transmitter) and COR (carrier operated relay). Because that mode is not very reliable, a new means of mobile control is given. It is especially useful in a mobile communication system without a control center.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Givens rotation based multichannel least squares adaptive lattice algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: By combining the spatial lattice filter with a single channel hybrid lattice/QR least squares (LS) algorithm, a multichannel LS lattice algorithm based completely on QR decomposition of the multichannel data matrix directly is presented in the paper. The parameter vector to be estimated in each channel can be obtained directly from internal variables in the present algorithm without a backsolve operation. The parameter identification problem to a multichannel autoregressive model is solved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural network approach for communication network routing problem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A description of the Hopfield/Tank model used for the communication network routing problem is given. Then, through "static" (i.e. the eigenvalue and the eigenspace of the connection matrix) and the dynamic analyses of the model, it is found that the model has the fastest rate to converge to the optimal or near-optimal solutions from an initial value. Therefore the quality of the final solutions can be guaranteed. The influence of the initial value on the final solutions is also considered. Simulation results are given at the end of the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A variable structure neural network model and its applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a neural network model called variable structure neural network model (VSNNM), also named improved multilayer perceptron (IMLP). In view of the back propagation algorithm (BPA), it is a time-consuming algorithm and its learning time is about O(n/sup 3/). In contrast to BPA, the speed of the learning algorithm proposed is much faster. Taking XOR for example, the speed of the learning algorithm is about 30 times faster than BPA. Moreover, hard limiters as the activation functions of neurons and only integer connection weights are used in VSNNM. Both the number of hidden layers and the number of hidden neurons in each hidden layer are variable, along with the demands of problems, but they are always kept minimum. Thus, this will greatly facilitate actual hardware implementation of training VSNNM. Hence, considering its speed and the number of neurons, the VSNNM is a successful attempt.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On communication patterns of parallel objects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Object-oriented programming is proving to be quite useful in many areas which have not been served well by more conventional approaches. Object-oriented systems show great potential for exploiting concurrence/parallelism. But many object-oriented languages currently in use are sequential. How to implement object-oriented languages on parallel systems is still a promising research topic. A parallel object-oriented system is a single-user system which is implemented on multi-processors. Objects can be active concurrently in one processor or do things on different processors in parallel. There are two communication patterns: synchronous and asynchronous communication. We put emphasis on communication patterns of parallel objects. We also discuss several ways to achieve performance in object-oriented languages and how to implement communication patterns on transputer-based multicomputer systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multifunctional directional transversal difference protection device by microcomputer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes the first successful power system device with multifunctional directional transversal difference protection in China. It realized some protection action performances which are difficult for conventional relay protection. Especially, eliminating both the voltage dead-zone and increasing action sensitivity and selectability are important improvements over conventional relay protection. By using the advantages of microcomputers, this device has created some new functions which are impossible for conventional protection, and has progressed toward the direction of multifunctionality and automation. It has been successfully in field operation in a 66 kV substation in Liaoning Province since May of 1992.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An integrated approach towards robotic modular fixture assembly
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A prototype twin-arm robot workcell has been developed for modular fixture assembly. Model-based robot programming plans collision free robot path, and generates an off-line program. A six-component force/torque sensor detects local frames in the real world. Automatic framing compensates the discrepancy between the ideal world in the CAD model and the real world. By means of active force control, automatic error recovery can be incorporated to enhance the reliability of robot operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High quality speech coding based on hybrid CELPC and VELPC techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Code-excited linear predictive coding (CELPC) is now the main technique used to produce good quality speech at bit rates around 4.8 kbps. However, the original CELPC is impractical in most cases due to its heavy computational load. A hybrid CELPC and voice excited linear predictive coding (VELPC) scheme is presented in the paper for speech coding with lower complexity. In the algorithm, the speech signal is firstly divided into two parts, the base-band and the high-band respectively, in frequency domain, and then the base-band and the high-band signal are coded with CELPC and VELPC techniques respectively. The test experiments showed this new coder could produce synthesized speech with good quality at bit rates around 4.0 kbps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A statistical method for building macromodels of circuits in tolerance design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A method for building macromodels based on factorial experimental design and regression analysis is studied. It employs a step-wise experimental design method needing least number of circuit simulation. The variable screening technique is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Research on the technology of microcomputer-controlled video frequency testing and signal processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a video-frequency area measuring system is presented. The principles of the system, the hardware diagram and the corresponding software are discussed in detail. Satisfactory results have been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical fiber temperature sensor based on phase shift by aluminum thermal expansion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The method of using aluminum tube wound by single-mode fiber as a temperature sensor is proposed. The optical source of this temperature sensing system is a 2-frequency He-Ne laser. When the temperature of fiber on aluminum is changed, a phase shift in optical signal will appear. By using electronic circuits, this phase shift can be detected and compared with a reference signal which is obtained directly from the laser source. Then one can obtain information on temperature according to the difference of phases between these two signals. Two experiments have been performed in the laboratory. In the first experiment the aluminum tube is 12 cm in diameter, 8 cm in height, and 2 mm in thickness, with a fiber length about 60 m wounded 155 turns. The sensitivity is 2.1/spl times/10/sup -2/ rad//spl deg/C-m. In the second experiment, the tube is 7.5 cm in diameter and height, and 2 mm in thickness, with a fiber about 10 m length wounded in 21 turns. The sensitivity is 4.9/spl times/10/sup -2/ rad//spl deg/C-m. The temperature from 5/spl deg/C to 80/spl deg/C is measured with this design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stochastic motion estimation and its applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Motion is an important clue used in human vision to extract objects of interest from background with irrelevant details. In image analysis, motion stems from the relative displacement between sensor and scene under observation. In this paper, a posteriori probabilistic approach is used to define this problem of the motion estimation. The motion vector is estimated by maximizing the a posteriori probability distribution of the relation intensity distributions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: H/sup /spl infin// control of inverted pendulum
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This note is concerned with the control of a double inverted pendulum. The control system is based on robust H/sup /spl infin// state feedback control theory and is designed by using the computer aided design software developed by the authors. The resulting controller is a robust H/sup /spl infin// controller for a linearized model in the neighbourhood of the upright position of double inverted pendulum. Simulation results show that the designed controller works satisfactorily.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An operation efficiency analysis on breadth first quadtree
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper proposes the method which traverses and codes the quadtree by breadth first. Quadtree coded by breadth first (breadth first quadtree) has the same compression ratio with the quadtree coded by depth first (depth first quadtree). In breadth first quadtree, nodes in high level and low level appear in level by level, not at random. This makes it better for operation efficiency, especially in geometric property operation (perimeter calculation, area calculation, search, object labelling, neighbor finding) which needs long operation time. In this paper we show the advantage of breadth first quadtree by the worst case analysis and the general case analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multiprocessor communication architecture for high speed networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Over the years, communication speed of networks has increased from a few Kbps to several Mbps, as also has the bandwidth demand. Communication protocols, however, have not improved to that extent. With the advent of Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM), it is now possible to "tune" protocols to current and future demands. This paper, develops a High Speed Network architecture, which caters to the needs of bandwidth-consuming applications such as voice, video and high definition image transmission.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuzzy control system and it's application in chlorine alkali production
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The chlorine alkali industry plays important role in whole industry. The process is complex and power consumption is enormous, so how to raise the level of automation in the production has become an important subject. This paper discusses the design and implementation of the chlorine hydrogenium subsystem's DDC level of a hierarchical-distributed microcomputer control system. After debugging and operating, the system has achieved control requirements and the effect is comparatively good. An important step has been taken in the field of optimisation of the chlorine alkali control system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A visual tool for C++ program development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Proposes a visual programming environment framework for C++ program development. With the evolution of microelectronic technology, we are able to directly represent and manipulate programs, tables, icons and other representations on computer systems. Visual and graphical representations offer programmers new abilities to gain deeper insights about programs and software systems than is possible by plain text. This study aims at the construction of a computer-aided software engineering toolkit to aid in the creation of an object-oriented C++ program in a programmer-friendly manner, with enhanced productivity. For this purpose, we introduce the concept of a table which can represent real objects or classes and plays the role of a kind of icon.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multi-level hybrid model for very-large-set pattern recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A multi-level hybrid model for pattern recognition with a very large set of classes is proposed. The model involves traditional classification methods, knowledge-based methods and neural network methods, employs the advantages of all three methods, and is more characteristic of human perception.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robustness of pole-assignment in a specified circular region
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A sufficient condition is proposed to guarantee robust pole location within a specified circular region for a linear uncertain system. The explicit bound on linear time-invariant perturbations with highly structured information is obtained. Under these allowable highly structured perturbations, both stability robustness and certain performance robustness will thus be ensured. The merit of the proposed new approach is demonstrated by a example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of turbine-generator torsional oscillations with particular reference to adaptive autoreclosure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Adaptive autoreclosure techniques can offer many advantages over conventional schemes in improving power system stability and reliability. Previously (1993), the authors developed a novel autoreclosure scheme by using a neural network approach. The results show that the proposed scheme can distinguish between permanent and transient faults, and can precisely define the arc extinction time in the case of transient faults. In this paper, studies of turbine-generator torsional oscillations are conducted. The outcome of the studies offers a better understanding in the development and applications of adaptive autoreclosure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The least-conflict code grouping algorithm for CDMA wireless information networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In code division multiple access (CDMA) wireless information networks, it is important to find an efficient algorithm for assigning as few codes to the stations as possible. We propose the least-conflict code grouping algorithm for selecting which stations should share the same code to reduce the number of codes needed. The simulation result shows that only a few codes are required to drive a throughput-delay performance, of the coded tone sense (CTS) protocol, very close to the case where each station has a unique code.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Arithmetic coding data compression codec for newspaper facsimile
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An arithmetic coding data compression codec for transmitting newspapers is reported. By using a limited accuracy algorithm to Chinese words and a rastered photograph newspaper page with resolution of 24 Pels/mm, a compression ratio about 10 has been obtained. This codec was put into use in May 1992 in the national transmission network of China.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Protocol for a slotted ring network as an integrated voice and data carrier
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper proposes a protocol for integrating voice and data traffic onto a slotted ring network. The performance of the protocol is investigated through simulations by modeling voice traffic as having alternating talkspurts and silence periods. Voice traffic is also given priority over data traffic because of real-time delivery requirement. The simulation shows that the network can effectively handle both traffic without deteriorating data transmission excessively. The scheme proposed uses only one bit for acknowledgement of data packets which is allowed to ride on the voice packet. This method thus prevents the data acknowledgement process from being severely interrupted by voice transmission.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: M-correlated dynamic Huffman code
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The compression results of traditional variable length coding (VLC) are limited by the global entropy bound calculated from the statistics of entire source. Many entropy coder have been proposed for the purpose of approaching this compression bound as close as possible. In this paper, the local entropy (LE) coding principle is given to reduce the coding bound by partitioning the source into parts while it still can be exactly recovered. In addition, the LE theorem is also developed for the purpose of realizing the above principle for practical applications. The M-correlated DHC (MDHC), which is a realization of the LE theorem, is proposed for image compression. The compression result of MDHC shows higher compression ratios than adaptive Huffman code (HC) in every case of our experiment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using neural networks to solve Steiner Tree Problem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on neural computing theory, we propose an algorithm to solve the Steiner Tree Problem, an NP-complete problem. The algorithm proposed is parallel and its efficiency is verified through examples. However, two problems remain unsolved: the determination of parameters in the algorithm; and the optimal solution cannot always be found.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional information encoding and holo-spectrum display of two-dimensional image
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The multi-dimensional information encoding is introduced as a means of displaying Fourier spectrums of signal, and an information encoding and displaying algorithm is proposed in this paper. It can be used in Fourier spectrum display and analysis of two-dimensional (2-D) image, and a 4-D hole-spectrum, i.e. first spatial frequency, second spatial frequency, magnitude and phase plot, of 2-D image is obtained. An experimental display system is developed, and the hole-spectrums of the 2-D images based on the multi-dimensional information encoding are analyzed. The results show that the hole-spectrum of the 2-D image based on the multi-dimensional information encoding are able to represent the details of the 2-D image magnitude and phase characteristics in the spatial frequency domain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of artificial neural networks to the classification of Australian wheat varieties
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Reports results obtained from the application of artificial neural networks to an Australian wheat variety classification problem. A 'HyperSAB' (Hyper-Self-Adaptive Backpropagation) network with a self-adaptive acceleration strategy for the error backpropagation learning algorithm has been developed. This has been applied to six different Australian wheat varieties with 200 samples in each case. The results indicate that the artificial neural network has some potential to be used as an identification tool in this problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal estimation of distances between holes precision by Kalman filter theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents that using Kalman filter theory optimally estimates precision of distances between holes in parts that are to be assembled into batch-finished products. It has mainly solved two aspects of problems. (1) How to write out state equations. (2) The state results obtained by applying Kalman filter theory to error theory are superior to those by classical error theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A developing program for test and evaluation of digital relaying algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a development program for evaluating microprocessor based relaying algorithms. Execution of the program creates a real-time environment which a digital relay would encounter under service. Prefault and fault conditions can be selected to test real-time performance of relaying algorithms under various fault situations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Visualising coordination languages for parallel processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes a graphical programming interface for Linda-coordinated languages. To support visual editing of programs written in an ordinary computation language (e.g. C) coordinated through Linda, two separate graphical notations are proposed, one for representing Linda's tuple space templates, the other for the ordinary (or host) language. The text program automatically generated from the program graphs can be compiled and executed on either a shared-memory MIMD machine or a loosely coupled network of workstations. The tuple space communication structure can be visualised after the program construction. The animation of the dynamic behaviour of templates within the tuple space is integrated into the environment, so that the program execution can be monitored and the program modified, if necessary, for the next iteration of the program development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A distributed intelligent robot system based on microcomputers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An intelligent robot system based on a distributed microcomputer system with five microprocessors is described. The improvement and extension of each processor are performed to build a real-time, but inexpensive intelligent robot system. Main efforts focus on the implementation of the system, system information classification and exchange, and function modules in each CPU. Shared information is divided into data base, knowledge base command area and status area. System functions are allocated to different processors to be executed in parallel. Experimental results show that the system is designed and implemented successfully and can be extended for further researches and practical applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The simulation and experiment of an Advanced Static Var Generator using GTO inverters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes an advanced static VAr generator (ASVG) using gate-turn-off (GTO) thyristor inverters which is designed for power system applications. Special emphasis is placed on the system principle, computer simulation analysis, general construction and experimental results.
