The operating results achieved by the prototype in the laboratory show that the ASVG has the feature of flexible regulation, fast response and promising development future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: M-net: a proposed high speed local area network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: M-net is a local area network (LAN) based on unidirectional bus system (UBS) architecture consisting of two outbound channels and one inbound channel. The network provides reverse round robin scheduling. The medium access control (MAC) protocol of M-net utilizes implicit token passing scheme with attempt-and-defer mechanism, achieving conflict-free transmissions among stations. In this paper, architecture and MAC of M-net is described. Then bounds on the performance measures of M-net are reported. Finally its performance is compared with other contemporary LAN systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Embedded ADPCM for variable bit rate coding in ATM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper introduces a variable bit rate coding algorithm combining silence detection and embedded ADPCM. The bit rate controlling method are discussed in the paper. The result shows that the bit rate of this coding algorithm method can be effectively reduced to below 20 kb/s, at the same time, the quality is practically equal to PCM. When the network is congested, we can either discard the LSB (the least significant bit) to reduce the average bit rate to 13 kb/s with a fairly good quality or store cells in a buffer, it can be output when the channel is free. The quality of speech coding is satisfactory if delay compensation is added.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance evaluation model for CSMA/CD bus under heavy load
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The performance evaluation model for CSMA/CD bus under heavy load is presented. Based on the definition of the critical point of heavy load and the description of difference between the average collision times of users and the system, a Markov transfer matrix of the system state is provided and the mathematical model which is suitable for evaluating the performance of CSMA/CD protocol under heavy load is established. After a comparison with the simulation results, an analytical approximation of the new method is presented and the results show that our model is close to the real system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new approach for implementing SMI algorithm with a linear systolic array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new approach for implementing SMI algorithm with a linear systolic array is presented. The systolic array only performs fast Givens rotations and has only one working state. That makes the systolic array design, implementation and control simple.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study on radiation pattern of H-plane microstrip array antenna directly coupled to nonradiating edges
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In order to improve directivity, a microstrip array antenna directly coupled to nonradiating edges is analysed. The equivalent circuit of the array antenna is obtained by the equivalent transmission line model and the radiation admittance parameters derived from the analysis method for the slotted parallel-plate waveguide filled with homogeneous dielectric. The calculated values of the return loss and the radiation pattern are presented and compared with the measured values. The calculated values are observed to be in fairly good agreement with the measured values.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A power LAN for telecommunication power supply equipment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of a distributed control LAN for linking microcontroller-based power rectifiers that are specifically developed for telecommunication purposes. The LAN is based on a RS485 multidrop serial line, using a PC as the master station for monitoring and controlling the rectifiers through the power network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of polarimetric fiber-optic interferometric temperature sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Among the various fiber-optic sensors, the sensor based on interference technique has the highest sensitivity. However, the range of temperature measurement is limited by their periodic nature. The purpose of this research is to improve this situation, and still keep their high sensitivities. We use two interferometers with slightly different sensitivities simultaneously, and the relative phase differences between two fundamental modes in the fibers are measured to determine the temperature. The purpose of extending measurable temperature range is achieved by combining the output signals of those two interferometers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust stability for finite wordlength implementation of two-dimensional recursive digital systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents criteria for robust stability of 2-D recursive digital systems under finite wordlength implementations. Based on the criteria, the stabilities of digital systems under various complex nonlinear cases can be analysed and tested. The stable work regions of the systems' coefficients also can be found. The test and analysis procedure is simpler than those of Bauer and Jury (1988) and Basu (1990), especially for high order 2-D digital systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gray-level-based corner detection by using wavelet transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Corners are very attractive features for many applications in computer vision. In this paper, a novel gray-level corner detection algorithm based on the wavelet transform is presented. First, we derived several properties of the corner and the edge embedded in the wavelet domain. Next, we apply these similar properties between the corner and the edge to extract the edge image. Then we employed these different properties between the corner and the edge to locate corners. Experiments have shown that our algorithm can detect corners accurately and effectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Photo-switch array and its applications in position detecting and imaging
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a new optical position sensor called the photo-switch array which can be used to detect the shadow position of an object. Another application of the photo-switch array is to detect the shadow image of an object, even if it is moving with a very high speed. Analytical results for system transfer function are presented and verified experimentally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simplifying discrete-time H/sup /spl infin// control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper deals with the mixed-sensitivity problem in the discrete-time case. It is proved if the plant is stable, only one Riccati equation need to be solved. If the plant is unstable, only one full dimension Riccati equation and a lower dimension Riccati equation need to be solved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast and reliable algorithm for railway train routing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The concept of discrete coordinates for railway nodes (signals, switches, sections, etc.) and the concept of local areas of railway switches in a railway network are proposed. A very fast and reliable algorithm based on these concepts are given for railway train routing. The time delay model of the algorithm is developed. It is shown that the delay time can be reduced tremendously by using the switch selecting rules proposed in the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An automatic circuit extractor from a photomicrograph of integrated circuits
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Investigates the problem of extracting a circuit from the photomicrograph of integrated circuits. It involves processing of the high resolution gray-level image of an integrated circuit layout captured using a high power optical microscope and a CCD camera. The final output is a Netlist Description of the circuit. The possible applications of the result are in the area of design verification, simulation, fault diagnosis and failure analysis, where a full circuit description in terms of Netlist is required. The circuit description of the layout follows the SPICE circuit simulation format. The approach consists of first processing the image captured to translate the gray-scale image of the layout circuit into Caltech Intermediate Form (CIF) code. These CIF codes are then processed to obtain the Reflist description of the circuits. The results have been very good and are reported in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The research of partial discharge measurements at ultra high frequency in GIS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Internal partial discharges (PD) may be very harmful to gas insulated substations (GIS) and should be detected and eliminated. Measuring the ultra high frequency (UHF) signals from partial discharges in GIS is a sensitive, effective method to detect the intensity of the discharge. The equivalent models of analysing the UHF resonances in GIS chambers are presented. Calculation results are obtained by using the EMTP program. The PD resonances in both the time and frequency domains are picked up by a coupler built on to the hatch cover plate and an embedded electrode and spacer. These results are also obtained theoretically through Fast Fourier transforms (FFT) and Wigner transforms (WGT). The results of experiments and theoretical analyses fairly agree. The measurement at UHF is free from external electric interference and is very useful and practicable for online monitoring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The object-oriented distributed transaction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Distributed transactions are an important programming paradigm for simplifying the construction of reliable and available distributed applications. We have implemented an object-oriented distributed transaction in the HDOOM model. This model is built on the base of a Novell LAN. The transaction facilities are provided as a routine library in C++. This adds parallel and atomic features to the C++ language. This paper presents the object model HDOOM, and describes the transaction structure and implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct lightning stroke protection technique by combining rejection with attraction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper illustrates the existing problems of power system lightning rods and dissipation arrays. It illustrates lightning protection techniques that have been advanced by rejection and combining rejection with attraction. The effectiveness of lightning rejection and a combination of rejection with attraction is shown using photographs taken from discharges in simulation experiments. The paper also introduces the structure and protective range of lightning rejectors and analyses the mechanism of lightning rejection. It gives some practical examples of lightning rejection and the combination of rejection with attraction. If the protected objects are higher than the critical height of the rejecting device, it is necessary that a combination of rejection with attraction be used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SIM: a Korean signature extraction method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The signature file method has been recently thought as a useful text retrieval method when inverted file method is not available. However, traditional word-oriented signature file methods cannot retrieve all the relevant text items in the variable-spacing environment such as Korean text. This paper describes the Space Ignoring Method (SIM) that can retrieve all the relevant text items irrespective of the word-spacing forms of the compound noun queries. The advantages of this method are presented by mathematical analysis and experimental performance comparison with a word-oriented method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modified time delay control for nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper proposes a modified scheme of time delay control for nonlinear systems. Time delay control is useful because its structure is simple and it does not need to know full knowledge of uncertainties. But it still requires knowing the range of uncertainties. The modified scheme is to adjust a controller parameter, and does not have to know the range of uncertainties. Therefore it can be applied to less known nonlinear systems. The adjustment of controller parameter is performed by estimating the convergency ratio of output derivative whose order is the same as the relative degree of a system. The scheme may be sensitive to noise because it uses the output derivative. This problem is solved by replacing the output derivative by the corresponding input which converges to the derivative as time goes on. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme is effective and it can be applied to systems subject to noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of handwritten digit recognition system on multitransputer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We propose an off-line digit recognition algorithm through stroke classification and implement it on a multitransputer for parallel processing. We classify possible strokes in the digit into 6 strokes and make a decision tree for recognition. To enhance the performance of the recognition system the whole task is partitioned into parallel subtasks considering best trade-off between parallelism and overhead. Though parallel tasks were executed concurrently in a processor on star-networked multitransputer because of resource limits, a model of parallel recognition system is presented. By increasing the number of processors to allocate the internal parallel processes privately, parallel recognition system may be put into practical use.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cluster model for optimal double-loop connected network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper investigates the solution of the optimization problem that appears in the design of double loop structured local area computer networks or interconnection networks. Double loop structure is a regular, two-connected network, designed for packet communications. The studies of degree two network connection schemes is based on the circular graphs of degree four. These graphs are regular, vertex-symmetric, and maximally connected, and such optimal graph exists for any given number of nodes. Every four of two-connected nodes consists a cluster, so cluster is a component with four input and four output link in the network. The proposed cluster network forms the optimal connection of a circular graph. We demonstrate how to construct one such network for any number of nodes and examine their network properties. The problem of routing is also addressed, and two routing rules are investigated that take advantage of the network regular structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated voice/data on a centralized switch node architecture for LAN with free round robin service strategy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The integration of voice and data traffic in our proposed centralized switch node architecture is considered. Specifically, the unfairness of the free round robin (FRR) scheduling strategy towards low priority traffic types is demonstrated by a comparison with a restricted bandwidth strategy called reserved round robin (RRR). The simulation results show that under heavy load conditions, RRR provides a more balanced scheduling of traffic types than the FRR, with only a moderate increase in the delay times of higher priority traffic types.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a V.29 data modem using digital signal processing technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The modem market can be classified into two categories. They are the commondity and professional products. The professional products at the high end of the market are mainly for corporate network. This type of modem is mainly designed around DSP devices. This paper presents the design and the implementation, using digital signal processors, of a CCITT V.29 9600 bps modem. The whole transmitter and the receiver that are described were all implemented using the TMS32010 and the TMS32025 DSP respectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An automatic coding technique for the image editing of a videotex system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on the principles of the image processing, pattern recognition and morphology, an automatic coding technique for the image editing of a videotex system which could greatly improve the editing efficiency is presented. The scheme and function of a videotex editor with high performance will also be given. The result we got is rather satisfactory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power system protection based on personal computer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This investigation centres on the practical advantages of microcomputer based replacements for parts of the conventional electromechanical and static protective relays used in power system protection. Incremental instantaneous protection, in which a trip decision is made on the basis of the rate of change of current, has only become a practical proposition with the advent of fast microcomputers. With the correct choice of current transformer ratio, and preset values in the software, a 12 bit analog-to-digital system is shown to be adequate. Software is also developed to implement the inverse definite minimum time trip function, with satisfactory results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An introduction to heterogeneous optimal selection theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, an approach for selecting an optimal suite of computers for solving problems with diverse computational requirements, called Heterogeneous Optimal Selection Theory (HOST), is presented. HOST is an extension to Augmented Optimal Selection Theory in two ways: It incorporates heterogeneous parallelism embedded in the tasks, and it reflects the costs associated in using various fine grain mapping strategies at individual machine level. Some related issues are discussed in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust PD control of unmanned land vehicles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: For the velocity-following problem of an unmanned land vehicle, the classical PD control law is shown to be robust with respect to highly nonlinear dynamics by properly choosing the control gains. The tracking error system is shown to be uniformly and ultimately bounded. The choices for the gains depend only on the bound of the nonlinear dynamics. Even though the coefficients of the polynomial bounding function are unknown, the robustness PD law can be guaranteed by simply increasing the gains that satisfy certain inequalities. Experiment results are presented to validate the conclusions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Software system for ABC-90jr.-an array based computer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The software system for ABC-90jr., an array based computer with a state-of-the-art architecture is described. This includes the design of the programming language, the run-time software, the debugger and the software emulator for the machine. A way to expend MS-FORTRAN for mixed-language programming with low-level assembly language of the machine is introduced. A method to fully exploit the parallelism between the host and the attached processor is discussed. Examples illustrating the features of the hardware and software of ABC-90jr. are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of intelligent controller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new artificial intelligent controller (AIC) is proposed for control of complex systems. This controller incorporates various approaches of artificial intelligence including central mechanism, fuzzy decision, and neural networks. Numerical simulations show the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive control design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical power system state forecasting and estimation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper discusses the concept of state forecasting and estimation in power systems. A method of forecasting bus injective power and line flow power which makes use of the current information and the historical data from run patterns is presented and the results of state forecasting and estimation are compared with those of static state estimation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Block systolic computations in digital filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Many efficient systolic algorithms in the block computation of digital filters have been derived. Highly concurrent structures can be implemented from these block systolic computation algorithms. All the performances of these highly concurrent structures can be described using the total computation times and the total processor numbers needed for each algorithm. A comparison with sequential algorithms using tables of speedup rates is presented, and the efficiency for each block algorithm is summarized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improvement of synchronous machine saturation simulation in the EMTP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an improved synchronous machine saturation model in the EMTP. It is based on the machine-reduction method interface. Simulation results are used to demonstrate the improvements in simulation accuracy of the saturated synchronous machine and the reduction in the number of iterations between the mechanical and electrical parts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple polyphase signals for access system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We present several theorems which are very attractive in designing multiple signals for an access system. The designed signals are all derived from the orthogonality of the Frank code matrix, and they are associated with complementary codes or perfect periodic codes. The co-interference between any two signals in a certain set can be reduced to satisfy the needs of a multiple access system. We also discuss the Doppler property of the designing codes and propose an architecture for their implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic mapping technique for adaptive Huffman code
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new adaptive Huffman code which has low hardware cost and high compression efficiency is proposed. The adaptation principle of this code is to dynamically change the mapping relationship between symbols and codewords while keeping all codewords unchanged. The proposed code is applied to the coding of "macroblock types" of MPEG and the experimental results show that it can achieve a 20%/spl sim/28% more savings of coded bits than MPEG. The hardware cost and operations of the proposed hardware architecture for the new code are significantly less when compared to conventional adaptive VLC. Hence, it is suitable for real-time coding systems, especially the video codec.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Complex neural networks constructed by different kinds of neuron network models and neurocontrol
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A novel concept of a neuron network model is submitted and a new method for constructing a type of complex neural network using different kinds of neuron network models is offered. The method is derived from the discovery of neurobiology and considered from the angles of reliability or robustness, topology, bionics and synagetics. The architecture and the corresponding property of this kind of neural network are in conformity with that of the human nervous system. This method can also be used in neurocontrol systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New classified vector quantization of images
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this work, a new coding scheme called predictive classified address vector quantization (PCAVQ) is proposed for image compression. In this scheme, a new two-stage classification method based on the three-level block truncation coding technique is first developed to efficient classify blocks of an image into different classes having similar characteristics. The predictive mean removal VQ technique is applied to reduce the blocking effect in decoded images. On the other hand, a new simplified address VQ method is also developed to increase the compression ratio of the overall system. Simulations using real images show that the proposed PCAVQ scheme has about 1.7 to 4 dB improvement in peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) over the JPEG baseline system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tracing evacuation route using parallel algorithm in the case of fire in coal mines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Fire in coal mines is quite common and the hazard of fire always looms large. The paper deals with the situation of accidental fire breaking out in a board and pillar working. Although board and pillar has been taken as a particular instance, the idea can be applied to any working district having a different method of extraction. The paper highlights the capabilities of a parallel algorithm, executing in a message-passing multi-processing environment in real-time. The idea appears to be superior to the ordinary procedural algorithm using record type data structures and employing arrays and pointers for search methods as suggested by S. Kozielski (1980).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal control of PWM harmonics by pulse width reduction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: PWM sampling techniques are widely used in converting DC-AC power. The PWM waveform consists of a fundamental and harmonics. In many applications harmonics control is desirable. Output PWM harmonics can be controlled by reducing the width and the position of the edges of the PWM pulses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital power system simulator for relay testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A digital simulator dedicated to power system relay testing purposes is presented. It is used as a testing device for relay panels. The paper introduces the primary power system being simulated and its mathematical model and describes the software and hardware implementation of the simulator. The simulator has been in operation for two years. Its performance has been exemplary.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SIMD algorithms on a novel image data structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper we introduce an image data structure which is named 'boxcode' and present parallel algorithms for the basic geometrical operations, namely translation, scale, and rotation on boxcoded images. The algorithms are designed to exploit SIMD computers. They utilize SIMD machines that have a few thousands of elementary processors, interconnected with a linear interconnection network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: GKD-1 RRC real-time robot controller and its application in force/position hybrid compliance control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The new type of real-time robot controller, GKD-1 RRC, designed for robot force/position hybrid control is based on a multilevel bus mode MIMD tightly-coupled multiprocessor structure which can dynamically distribute load to maintain dynamic load balance by the management of the kernel of multiprocessor concurrent operation system and can meet the need of task-based parallel processing. The paper presents the hardware and software structure of the robot controller and its main features. Then some typical experiments on force/position hybrid control schemes and their results are explained. The experimental results show that computer structure of GKD-1 RRC is efficient and applicable, with 4.88 ms force/ position hybrid control cycle, less than 100 gram average force control steady state error, and the accuracy of the position control is same as the original accuracy of the manipulator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Handling expressions with side effects within an axiomatic semantics framework
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper shows how expressions with side effects can be treated in an axiomatic framework. The first problem is defining an appropriate valuation function. This is done by defining evaluation orders and showing how this can be used to define appropriate valuation functions. A syntactic transformation that eliminates all expressions with side effects is then presented. This transformation yields a program that is equivalent to the original program but has no expressions with side effects. This new program can be then handled with the standard axioms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wideband ambiguity function of South-China FM bat sonar signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Echolocating insectivorous bats, such as the South-China FM bats Pipitrellus Abramus Temmink, detect and track their moving prey by means of echolocation. Despite a series of papers published on bat signal analysis, their discussion concentrated on the 1D FFT spectrum. The wideband ambiguity function (WAF) is developed to describe the range-velocity estimation performance of the bats' sonar signals. Twenty-one signals emitted by the South-China FM bat, during natural hunting of an insect were analyzed via time, frequency and the 3D wideband ambiguity diagram (WAD). The evolution of the main signal parameters (pulse interval, pulse duration, bandwidth, dominant frequency, WAD, and the elliptical contours of ambiguity) from a search to a capture of an insect are summarized. The result suggests that the search signal emitted by the FM bat are best used to extract coarse and fine information from different frequency components of one echo. In a number of hunting sequences the authors found that the terminal signals contained 2nd and 3rd harmonics. The dominant frequency of the terminal signals in almost all the sequences went down suddenly from 50 kHz to 30 kHz. This is to reduce the delay error caused by Doppler velocity coupling. In the terminal phase, using shorter duration combining with depressing frequency, enables bats to reduce the coupling delay error to zero and the long axis of ellipse coincidence with the velocity axis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systolic algorithms for generalized predicative control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Discusses the systolic implementation of generalized predicative self tuning control for a single input single ouput system. The original generalized predicative control problem is first changed into a stochastic linear quadratic problem by a general realization, and then the dynamic programming method is used to the resultant problem. Since no requirement is placed on the realization, we choose a special realization and incorporate the matrix decomposition in the algorithm. Due to the special structure of the problem, the trapezoidal systolic array is used. The derived algorithm is numerically stable since the Givens or modified Givens rotations are employed in the algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hybrid UTD-MM analysis of electromagnetic scattering by a perfectly conducting semi-elliptical cylinder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: When an electric or magnetic line source is located in the presence of an semi-elliptical cylinder, the far field pattern is analysed by the hybrid UTD (uniform geometric theory of diffraction)-MM (moment method) technique developed in this paper. By the reciprocity theorem and the UTD, the known currents are obtained. The basis function for the unknown current in the smooth convex region of the scatterer is assumed and used in solving this problem by the MM. Because of reduced number of basis function employed in the present method, the computing time is considerably reduced in the analysis of large scatterers. Whereas the UTD solution is invalid in the grazing incidence case, the hybrid method can be applied in this case. The numerical results are compared with those of the MM.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bit error rate of optical soliton communication systems with lumped amplifiers and guiding-frequency filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new Gordon-Haus limit of a soliton-based system with lumped amplifiers and guiding-frequency filters is discussed. The exact bit error rate expression of such system considering the combined effects of the timing jitter and the energy jitter is presented. Some numerical results are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust D-stability analysis for discrete uncertain systems with multiple time delays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The problem of assigning all poles of a closed-loop system in a specified disk by dynamic output feedback is considered for discrete systems with multiple non-commensurate time delays. This kind of pole assignment problem is called D-pole placement, and its relation to robustness properties is discussed. Thus, the robust D-pole placement is subsequently proposed and a robust criterion is derived to ensure D-stability of the discrete multiple time-delay systems subject to parametric uncertainties. Furthermore, with this robust criterion, the bounds can also be estimated for allowable parametric uncertainties that guarantee all the poles of the discrete uncertain multiple time-delay systems to remain inside the specified disk. Finally, an example is given to illustrate obtained results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high speed and high reliability drive-protection circuit for power transistor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a high speed and high reliability drive-protection circuit for the GTR power transistor, based on the characteristics of GTR. The circuit keeps the GTR working in the optimum state. With the protection circuit a military research subject has been completed successfully.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Conjugation and H/sup /spl infin// control of discrete-time systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper concerns the H/sup /spl infin// model-matching problem of discrete-time systems using the conjugation method. The restriction on T/sub 2//sup -1/(z) and T/sub 3//sup -1/(z) which must be antistable is removed in this paper. The result can be used to solve more general H/sup /spl infin// model-matching problems of discrete-time systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Defuzzification method for a faster and more accurate control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Fuzzy control is achieved by formulating a rule-base which is based on experience gathered by human operators. Those systems which cannot be modeled mathematically benefit most from a fuzzy control strategy since the imprecise data can he captured using linguistic variables in the rule-base. Fuzzy logic has certain disadvantages. The number of computations required for arriving at a certain output response for given inputs is very large and thus the system response is sluggish. Therefore to adapt fuzzy systems to real-time applications one needs to use faster algorithms and/or parallel processing. Also the process of defuzzification required to produce a single output value may lead to errors which can undo the advantages of fine control normally achievable using fuzzy logic. Special analytical techniques ensure that the complications of the defuzzification process are simplified; the method used retains the desirable features of fuzzy control. This paper aims to present a comparison between the conventional fuzzy controller and a fuzzy logic controller based on the techniques mentioned above.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of MIS subsystem of the production and technology division of Northeast China Electric Power Administration Bureau-SMIS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: With the vast applications of computers in electric power systems and the development of computer systems in Electric Power Administration Bureau, electric power system management information systems (MIS) are now required. In order to achieve data sharing and office automation, Northeast China Electric Power Administration Bureau (NCEPAB) has designed and developed its own MIS. On this basis, The Production and Technology Division of Northeast China Electric Power Administration Bureau and Tsinghua University decided to develop a MIS subsystem-SMIS. The ideas and methodology of the SMIS system design are presented. It employs existing structures and data communication conditions and personal computers to develop and implement MIS on the basis of Dbase III and Foxbase/sup +/. The SMIS is renewed by means of harnessing an Oracle relational database to achieve better results. The SMIS is made up of an IBM4381, a PC486 and 8 PC386s. The 4381 serves as network center, the PC486 serves as working terminal, and the PC386s serve as terminals in each office (TMOF). Besides these, each important message in the divisions is allocated to a TMOF. A dull terminal for officer use will also be allocated in each department to find relevant data. Data communication adopts the Novell network and its protocol.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SMULA, an O-O knowledge representation language in OOKSDE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents SMULA, an object-oriented (O-O) knowledge representation language in an O-O knowledge-base system development environment (OOKSDE). While presenting the programming structure of SMULA, it focuses the discussion on some unique features adopted in the language. Finally, the reasoning mechanism of the knowledge object base represented by SMULA is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transient calculation of networks with ferromagnetic elements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an efficient method for transient calculation of power networks with ferromagnetic elements. A hysteresis model is developed to represent the magnetizing characteristics, in which the multi-valued hysteresis behaviour is simulated by a given major loop and the minor loop trajectories within it. Based on the model, a set of nonlinear differential equations are obtained to describe the magnetizing branches, which are solved by a semi-explicit Runge-Kutta description method. Thus, network transients can be calculated in terms of the solutions to magnetizing branches. The result calculated by the algorithm is compared with experiments, and good agreement is shown between them.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new parallel computation model on synchronous wireless interconnection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We propose the study of a new parallel computation model based on synchronous wireless interconnection. The new computation model takes advantage of the radio technology instead of the conventional processor-processor links to communicate. To show the power of the new model, we first show that the new model can simulate the concurrent-read concurrent-write parallel access machine (CRCW PRAM) easily, then we derive an algorithm that can simulate the binary tree to perform the semigroup computation in O(log n) time by using O(n) processors. In addition, we design O(l) time algorithms on maximum finding and sorting problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of echo canceller during start-up for high-speed data transmission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Echo cancellers that use the spectral estimation approach for the fastest possible starting-up time need to know the approximate delay and duration of the echo, and require a cyclic input of a pseudo-noise (PN) sequence. This paper describes the effects of an inaccurate estimate of the echo duration by the initial sounding of the echo path. It also compares the performance of the well-known Barker sequences, the Relaxed-Barker sequences, and the arbitrarily constructed PN sequences when used for the starting up process. It offers an explanation and gives the necessary characteristics of the PN sequences that ensure the successful operation of the echo canceller. Finally the paper gives a guideline for the choice of a suitable PN sequence for the estimation of an unknown echo path of any but roughly-known duration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hierarchical control structure for multisensor object recognition system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Multisensors can be used to overcome problems associated with intelligent object recognition systems. The introduction of multisensors into such a system emphasizes the need for an effective method for combining sensor outputs, and a complicated system requires intelligent control. We propose a hierarchical control structure (HCS) to build a recognition system and introduce a fuzzy neural net (FNN) method to fuse multisensor information. This paper describes the concept of HCS, the derivation of fuzzy rules, the FNN's construction and training, etc. Then, experimental results involving parts recognition in the application of an assembly robot are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low bit rate image coding technique using human visual system model and homomorphic processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A low bit rate image coding scheme which incorporates the homomorphic property of an image, transform coding, vector quantization and the human visual system model is described. Experimental results indicate that reasonably good reconstructed images are obtained at around 0.2 to 0.25 bits per pixel dependent on the nature of the images.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An artificial neural network approach to radar target identification in polarization domain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The state-of-the-art of radar target identification (RTI) in the polarization domain is reviewed first, then the possibility of using an artificial neural network to solve the problem of directly extracting the polarization-invariant features is discussed. A modified backpropagation algorithm for a multilayer feedforward neural network is proposed for the case of large training samples. A new method for RTI in the polarization domain using single-frequency multipolarization is proposed. By using a dumbbell target as a simulation model, an experiment is performed which shows that the proposed method in this paper is practicable and effective, and it has a high correct classification rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple scheme of nonlinear decoupling control for robotic manipulators with flexible joints
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Control of robotic manipulators with flexible joints is considered in this paper. Without using sophisticated mathematical tools, a simple yet rigorous algorithm is derived to decouple and linearize the highly nonlinear and strongly cross-coupled robotic dynamics. It is shown that the concise handcrafted algorithm can be used with great ease. A numerical example is presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed scheme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operating speed and reach accuracy study for a digital distance relaying algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A finite transform based algorithm has been developed for digital distance protection of power system transmission lines. This paper presents the investigation results of performance affected by sampling rate and window length. Improved performance of both operating speed and reach accuracy can be achieved by optimum selection of these parameters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Six-joint industrial robot controller software system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the software system of a six-joint industrial robot controller based on intel 8086+intel 8087 is described. The system was designed and implemented successfully. The main features of the system are its real-time operating system and motion-orientated language TRL.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient method for optimizing dispatch of voltage and reactive power in large scale power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an efficient method for solving the optimizing dispatch of voltage and reactive power in large scale power systems. In the proposed method, a large system is decomposed into a series of subsystems based on the effective control range of voltage and reactive power regulating devices. A primal problem with high dimension is solved by optimizing alternately a series of subproblems with much low dimension, and the complex coordination process used in other decomposition optimization methods is effectively avoided. The proposed decomposition technique is very well suited for various systems with different size, structure and complexity. Numerical results of applying the proposed method to two power system examples verify the efficiency of the method in terms of convergence and computation time. There are significant improvements compared with the centralization optimization methods in which optimization is directly carried out on the original system model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The evolution of network-based corporate networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper reviews the evolution of the business services that provide corporate networking from the public network. Specific phases that are described are: Nodal Centrex, Networked Centrex, Private Virtual Networking, and Global Virtual Network Services. From within this context, the benefits of AIN-based Virtual Network Services are examined, highlighting some challenges for the future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data structure for segmenting binary image
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Descriptions for binary images are important in image processing systems. In this paper, we design many data structures to describe image features and realize an algorithm using connectivity analysis (some similar to labeling algorithm) to extract these features. In practice,these methods are applied in robot's peg-in-hole assembly. Vision here is used for analyzing images of parts (some holes in them). It proves that these data structures are very useful in binary image processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using dataflow principle to exploit restricted AND-parallelism in logic programs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: To improve the execution speed of logic programs, exploiting parallelism has proved promising. The paper presents a scheme supporting Restricted AND-parallelism improved over a previous scheme by exploiting more parallelism. The scheme is based on dataflow computation and implemented in a non-shared execution model, and thus taking advantages of distributed binding results. Comparison with the previous scheme is discussed and some examples given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A segment-based speech recognition system for isolated Mandarin syllables
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A segment-based speech recognition scheme is proposed. The basic idea is to explicitly model the correlations between successive frames of an acoustic segment by using features representing the contours of spectral parameters. These segmental features are several lower-order coefficients of discrete orthonormal polynomial expansions. The performance of the proposed scheme was examined by simulations on multi-speaker speech recognition for all 408 highly confusing first-tone Mandarin syllables. A recognition rate of 77.4% was achieved for the case, using five 6-segment reference templates per syllable. This is 13.0% and 6.6% higher than those obtained by a conventional dynamic time warping (DTW) method and a conventional hidden Markov model (CHMM) method, respectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of the throughput and delay performance of MP-CSMA/CD using an adaptive algorithm with 2 levels of priorities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An approach to implementing two levels of priorities in an MP-CSMA/CD local area network is presented. Our method a different probability of transmission for different priorities. Our simulation results show that it is possible to implement two levels of priority if the bus has 10 percent of high priority stations and the overall load does not exceed 0.5.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The systolic array implementation of DCT-4
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The type-4 discrete cosine transform matrix can be permuted into an imitative cyclic matrix with imitative constant /spl lambda/=-1. The matrix-vector multiplication can be implemented by systolic array. This paper presents two systolic array implementation of type-4 discrete cosine transform (DCT-4). Because of the relationship between type-2 discrete cosine transform (DCT-2) and DCT-4, the proposed systolic array implementation can be used to compute DCT-2 and two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (2D-DCT).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Speech recognition using dynamic recognition neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper proposes a dynamic recognition neural network model (DRNN), which has the advantages of some neural networks, so it is learns fast, calculates simply, and constructs flexibly. The model is suitable for dynamic recognition, such as speech recognition. Experiments on the Chinese isolated digital recognition were carried out. The results show that the model has potential.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SNR performance of various discrete ADM systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The performance of various discrete adaptive delta modulation (ADM) systems in the presence of random signal input is analyzed. The ADM systems considered are (a) Winkler system, (b) Abate (1967) system, (c) Bosworth and Candy (1968) system, and (d) Tazaki system (1977). It is assumed that the input random signal has a slope which varies randomly having Gaussian, Rayleigh and exponential probability density function (PDF) and has rectangular and triangular power spectral density (PSD). For an input random signal with specific PSD and PDF of its slope, the SNR has been calculated and plotted against the signal power. A performance evaluation has been made and summarized for the four systems above.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effects of random polarization dispersion on soliton propagation in optical fibers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The effects of random polarization dispersion on soliton propagation in optical fibers are investigated numerically by considering the random rotation of the birefringence axes and the random fluctuation of the magnitude of the polarization dispersion. It is shown that with the correlation length of the random polarization dispersion increases, the effects on soliton propagation become more serious.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Color image sequence coding with variable block size motion compensation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a new color image sequence coding method based on variable block size motion compensation is proposed. A multiresolution tree structure is used to organize the blocks with various sizes. At the bottom level, the quadtree is used to code the resultant motion compensated prediction error. The spatiotemporal characteristics of the human eyes are embedded into the tree structure to achieve high compression. For transmission of color information in the scenery, the color pixel is first transformed into Y-U-V color space, and then a color quadtree structure is constructed to transmit the full color information. Massive experiments have been done with the CLAIRE image sequence. Results show quite promising.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gallium arsenide photoconductive switch in high-voltage analogue application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to demonstrate the unique features of jitter-free response and bilateral conduction of photoconductive switches made from gallium arsenide as high-voltage devices optically modulated by high-power illuminators in HV analogue applications. The experimental results show that analogue waveforms, sinusoid and triangle, can be generated with peak-to-peak voltages up to 15 kV in a frequency range from 0.01 Hz to 1250 Hz. The theoretical model suggests that when the maximum modulating frequency of an irradiance is smaller than 1/2/spl pi//spl tau/ (/spl tau/: the effective free carrier recombination time) the peak amplitude of the modulated dynamic conductance of the switch will be constant within the modulating frequency range, which is in good agreement with the experimental result.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust mixed-norm H/sub 2//H/sub /spl infin// regulation for uncertain discrete-time systems via state feedback
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of robust H/sub /spl infin//-constrained H/sub 2/ state feedback control for uncertain discrete-time linear systems. The uncertainty considered is time-invariant norm-bounded and exists in both the state and input matrices. The results lead to a static state feedback controller which not only stabilizes the system but also minimizes a guaranteed cost bound on a quadratic cost function (an H/sub 2/ performance) subject to a prespecified H/sub /spl infin// constraint on the level of disturbance attenuation. It is shown that the problem addressed can be converted to the usual mixed H/sub 2//H/sub /spl infin// regulation problem for which there is no parameter uncertainty. This observation leads to a complete solution in terms of the existing results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An active edge detection approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, an active edge detection approach is proposed. It at first locates the discontinuity neighborhoods in the image with a simple error analysis algorithm. To suppress the noise and interpolate the missing points included in the edge neighborhoods, an improved relaxation labeling algorithm is then applied. The sizes of the spatial extent of the discontinuity neighborhoods can be estimated from the resultant images. Based on these measures, the optimal difference operators are than applied to the corresponding neighborhoods in the original image to extract the edge points exactly. As the new method can concentrate the major calculation on where the edges may be and extract the edgepoints adaptively, it works with high precision and low computational cost. Experimental results show the good quality and high speed of the proposed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Enhancement knowledge on uncertainty exceptions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Our exception handling approach uses enhancement knowledge in a class or instance definition instead of constructing a new subclass for the specific class. One direct associative link between normal and exceptional cases is built. The size of class hierarchy will shrink to the manageable range and the efficiency and rationality of reasoning will also increase. During reasoning period, the conditional trigger meta-knowledge mechanism can dynamically use the limited knowledge to induce or retract practical conclusions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new learning control strategy for robots in constrained manipulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, an iterative learning control strategy is presented for a class of constrained robots. The controller design is based on the reduced form of the robot model. The strategy guarantees the perfect motion tracking of the robot with its end-effector moving on a linear and frictionless constrained surface in the presence of unknown bounded disturbances. The bounded and adjustable force tracking error is obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The power characteristic of 500 kV large power compact over head transmission line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Aiming at the power supply quality of 500 kV large power compact transmission lines, their transmission ability is discussed in detail when different kinds of conductor bundle are used. Based on this discussion, the best model and number of subconductors are also put forward in this paper which points out that 500 kV large power compact overhead transmission lines will contribute to tremendous economic gains in the Three Gorges power station project.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a Chinese full-text retrieval system based on a probabilistic model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Full-text retrieval has the advantages of searching documents over a wide range of words and accessing original text directly. However, because of the inadequate processing speed and insufficient memory capacity, there has been little work done on full text retrieval systems in the past. With the emergence of very large capacity compact disk ROM (CD ROM), research in full-text retrieval systems is becoming increasingly important. Practical systems based on Boolean retrieval models have appeared. However, in spite of its ability to process structured queries, the Boolean model has been criticised for its inability to provide ranked output as all retrieved documents are considered equally important. Probabilistic models have been proposed by some scholars to solve this problem and have successfully been implemented on a small scale trial basis in indexing retrieval systems. This paper focuses on applying the probabilistic model into the full-text retrieval system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stabilization of discrete-time constrained systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A great deal of attention has been paid to stabilization of constrained systems. This paper investigates the stabilization of discrete-time constrained systems. The explicit element bounds on linear time-invariant perturbations with highly structured information are obtained. The state feedback controller is designed to satisfy the requirement of stability under the nonlinear saturation. An example is given to illustrate the application of our result.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation study of video transmission over FDDI
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Fiber distributed data interface (FDDI) is a 100 Mbps local area network. This paper reports the results of a simulation study of variable bit rate video transmission across a FDDI network. The mean delay of the video image transmissions is investigated using the synchronous and asynchronous service modes and under various network load.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic sort checking by sorting constraint consistency checking
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Integrating sorts (types) into logic programming languages increases expressiveness and evaluation efficiency. To support richer sort structures such as parametric and inclusion polymorphism, static sort checking is insufficient. Therefore efficient dynamic sort checking is an important issue in sorted logic programming. We first compare existing techniques for dynamic sort checking in the literature. Aiming to achieve more efficient dynamic sort checking, we propose a new evaluation procedure, based on constraint consistency checking, for sorted logic programs and goals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the implementation of an optimal polarimetric detection algorithm (PWF) with DSP56001
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: It is known that the polarimetric whitening filter (PWF) approaches the optimal detector (OPD) in the detection performance under both Gaussian and non-Gaussian clutter environments. A digital signal processor that consists of a four channel-high-speed A/D convertor, a real time double FFT processor (using the TMC2310 FFT processor) and a DSP56001-based CFAR detector. The hardware for the control of the TMC2310 with the DSP56001 and the software implementation of the motion compensation for binary integration are described in detail. A simple DSP56001 development system architecture is also configured.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive compression for image sequence recording and analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Medical thermography employs imaging techniques in the infrared spectrum for medical diagnosis. Very often, the cooling or warming course of human skin has to be studied, resulting in huge piles of image files that occupy lots of memory space. A new compression technique, with predictive ability, has therefore been devised for storing the files more economically to upgrade the effectiveness and efficiency of medical thermography. This method has also been found to be universally applicable to optical image-sequence recording in optical flow analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prefix computation on faulty hypercubes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In a parallel computer system, fault-tolerance is more obtainable since there is more than one processor cooperating in the system. For solving parallel prefix computation, we need not use all processors all the time. Thus, we propose a fault-tolerant mechanism by solving the prefix computation problem on faulty hypercube computers. By this mechanism, prefix computation can be done in O(log n) time on a faulty hypercube computer if there exists a fault-free subcube with size of at least a half of the hypercube, and in O(log/sup 2/n) time in the worst case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new design for autonomous land vehicle architecture
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Having analyzed the fundamental requirements of autonomous land vehicle (ALV) architecture designing, we find that the contradiction between the requirements of real-time and reliability is crucial. From our research, it can be shown that there are problems in solving this contradiction in the existing architectures. In order to solve such problems, we put forward a new design of ALV architecture, called the communication pipeline hierarchy system, and present some improvements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculation of the critical point of voltage collapse of power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a tracking method is proposed for calculating the critical point of voltage collapse of a power system. The new method has very promising numerical convergence characteristics and is easy to implement. It can provide arbitrary accuracy and can be applied for any load growth pattern. Its theoretical basis and some numerical examples are given in this context to demonstrate the effectiveness.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a file server operating system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes the design of a file server operating system called Cypress. The design of Cypress is aimed at improving the file server response time through exploiting latest hardware advances. Cypress is distinctive in its caching and management strategies that take advantage of the large-capacity disk caches, tens to hundreds megabytes, and the powerful processors in contemporary file servers. If compared with general-purpose operating systems that are installed to perform file server operations, Cypress enjoys another advantage of featuring more predictable response time for real-time applications. Based on our measurement on our first version of implementation, the average hit response times of Cypress when running on a Intel 80486 CPU based PC with 32-megabyte memory are 1.38 ms and 1.39 ms for read and write requests, respectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A stochastic parallel algorithm and its applications to VLSI layout
