publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: There are some problems that can be reduced to combinatorial optimization in VLSI layout. Using traditional methods, it could not escape from local extrema and often could not find valid solutions. We use a stochastic parallel algorithm to obtain valid and optimal result, through formalizing VLSI layout problems, choosing appropriate annealing schedule and parameters. The algorithm we used has low time and space complexity, high parallelism, and it is easy to be implemented using VLSI circuits. The results we obtained show the effectiveness and universality of the algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A natural language modeling for Chinese: phonetic flow to text
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper introduces a kind of phonetic text transcription language modeling used for the fields of speech recognition, Chinese character inputting etc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new fast decoding algorithm for the Golay code
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new effective algorithm for decoding the binary [24, 12, 8] Golay code is presented. The decoding algorithm is based on the "structure" properties of the parity-check matrix of the code. The algorithm available is fast, and simple in structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing jitter in high speed telecommunication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The most vexing problem for digital communication system designers and testing engineers is the control and measurement of jitter. The paper first introduces the concept of modulation domain and the principle of phase progression digitization as well as the modulation domain measurement method of jitter. Secondly, the authors give the structure of the jitter measurement system design using zero-dead-time (ZDT) counters. At last they give a simulation experiment of jitter measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient parallel algorithm for edge-coloring of graphs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Given G=(V,E) is a simple planar graph, and it doesn't contain any odd loops, |V|=n, |E|=m. We propose an efficient parallel algorithm for edge-coloring by using /spl Delta/ colors, based on SIMD-CRCW PRAM, a kind of shared memory model that many processors can read and write a unit simultaneously. Here, /spl Delta/ is the maximum degree of vertices of G. If /spl Delta/ is an even number, the algorithm requires O(log/spl Deltaspl middot/log/sup 2/n) time and O(n/spl Delta/) processors; otherwise it requires O(log/spl Deltaspl middot/log/sup 2/n+/spl Deltasup 2/n) time and O(n/spl Delta/) processors. When /spl Delta/=O(log/sup O(1/)n), the algorithm is an efficient algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the fast algorithms of multi-dimensional DCT and DST with input/output in normal orders
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Fast algorithms for multidimensional DCT are given. The algorithms is based on the successive order reduction of Tchebycheff polynomial, but with input and output in normal order. It is shown that the algorithms with input/output in normal order have more simple structure and require less time than ones with input/output in Hadamard order, and need fewer arithmetic operations than other multidimensional algorithms. The algorithms for DCT may be generalized to the computation for multidimensional DST. A C language program for computing two-dimensional DCT-IV is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new simplified method to design a robust position controller for a DC servomotor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a new method to design a robust position controller for a DC servomotor is proposed. The robust position-controller will ensure the closed-loop control system achieves the asymptotic tracking for a reference input of certain type p/sub 1/ and the complete rejection for a disturbance signal of certain type p/sub 2/. The proposed method has the following advantages: (1) proposing a systematic procedure for synthesizing the robust position controller, and (2) presenting a closed-form solution to the control law. Furthermore, an example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The analysis of mathematical morphological structuring element decomposition and its lower bound
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Mathematical morphology, which is a set theoretical methodology for image analysis, can rigorously quantify many aspects of the geometrical structure of signals in a way that agrees with human intuition and perception. The paper, which is based on the synthetical idea, analyzes the decomposition of a morphological structuring element. For any N-point structuring element, it concludes that the correct lower bound of decomposition is e/spl middot/lnN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RTDAMS: a real-time diagnosis and maintenance system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Rule-based systems are most important knowledge representation techniques and have been widely used to build large expert systems, but their deficiencies make them unsuitable for real-time application. The ideal space production has real-time requirements. This paper discusses the design and implementation of a real-time rule-based diagnosis and maintenance system (RTDAMS), which can be used in the automatic GaAs production line on the space station.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An object-oriented user interface management system NPUUIMS: design and development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: It is very time-consuming and expensive to create highly-interactive graphical styles of user interface. User interface management systems (UIMSs) attempt to make the creation of user interfaces easier, but most existing UIMSs have many problems. This paper describes the Northwestern Polytechnical University UIMS (NPUUIMS), a UIMS that adopts object-oriented methods and direct manipulation techniques that are used to create direct manipulation interfaces. In addition, we introduce a form-independent concept, which allows the presentation components of user interfaces to be generated automatically.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of dynamic programming theory for optimization of transmission line tower spotting
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The quality of tower siting of a transmission line determines directly the cost of the power line. Until now, all tower siting has been done by hand. It is impossible for a designer to choose a best plan from thousands of plans in practical work. In recent years, some of the problems described have had the possibility of being solved by the development of computation methods and the rapid progress of computers. Here, the authors describe how dynamic programming is the best way to solve the above problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On optimization of update propagation in multidatabase systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We consider the problem of update propagation in a multidatabase environment. Initially, the update propagation strategy is discussed in terms of minimization of the total communication cost of such operation. We indicate that the Steiner Tree is a more suitable model of update propagation than a minimum spanning tree approach. Since the Steiner Tree problem is NP-hard, the update propagation require an application of heuristic method. Subsequently, further optimization in respect of system response time is considered and an algorithm for computation of a propagation strategy, optimal with respect to this criterion is presented and analyzed. The update propagation response time can be improved by selecting a propagation center in the network; an appropriate algorithm is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Eigen analysis method for stability evaluation of linear constant-coefficient RDDE and its application to power system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A quantitative analysis method for stability evaluation of linear constant-coefficient retarded differential difference equations (RDDE) is presented in this paper. The method is used to investigate the effects of both distributed parameters in AC transmission lines and time-lags in static VAr compensator (SVC) controllers on the subsynchronous resonance modes. Results of a sample system show that the proposed method is very effective to study the stability of power systems with time-lags.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A voice input word processor system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: With the advent of note-book and hand-held computers in the consumer market, voice-input systems will gain prominence in the future over keyboard and pen-based systems. In this paper, we propose an intelligent voice-based word recognition and processing system using natural language processing techniques. The results have been very encouraging and the system has been tested extensively in WordPerfect 5.1 environment using a vocabulary of about 1000 words.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of feedback supervisor for controlled Petri nets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an effective synthesis algorithm for the state feedback supervisor by which the closed-loop system accepts the supremal controllable sublanguage of a given Petri net language.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Throughput analysis of an FDDI network under frequent renegotiation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The fiber data distributed interface (FDDI) standard refers to a 100 megabits-per second token ring network that supports synchronous and asynchronous data transmission. The media access protocol is based on the timed token access protocol which provides adjustment of the load offered to the ring by setting the target token rotation time (TTRT). The present paper describes an analytical model of a homogeneous FDDI network under the assumption of heavy load, which allows the TTRT to be frequently bid for and adjusted as and when the access time requirements of synchronous traffic changes. An algorithm to calculate the mean throughput of the network under frequent renegotiation has been derived. The behaviour of the FDDI network under frequent renegotiation is analysed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coordinative control of excitation and fast valving using artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A cooperative control scheme of power system generation excitation and fast valving based on artificial neural networks is proposed in this paper. Two neural networks are used to coordinate excitation and fast valving control. Digital simulation and physical laboratory experiments of a simple neural network controller are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-transputer video coding (MTVC) system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A novel approach for the parallel implementation of a CCITT H.261 video coding algorithm on a multiprocessor network is presented. One of the prominent bottlenecks of parallel implementation of a video coding algorithm is the sequential operation of the bit rate control in the coding algorithm. An a priori buffer-fullness estimator is proposed to circumvent this sequential operation which involves changing the quantisation step-size at fixed intervals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power spectrum estimation via neural-type structured network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We emphasise the learning algorithm and the convergence capability of the structured network for solving linear equations (Wang et al., 1990). Based on this structured network, a new autoregressive (AR) modeling method is presented. Its basic idea is to solve Yule-Walker type matrix equations for model coefficients by the structured network. The advantages of this AR modeling method over other AR modeling methods are: a parallel architecture and algorithm, suitable for VLSI hardware realization; and no divisions are involved in the calculations, so that the method still works for ill-conditioned Yule-Walker type matrix equations. Simulation results illustrating the performance of the method are given for both narrow-band sources and combinations of narrow-band and broad-band sources subjected to various levels of Gaussian white noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image sub-band coding with inter-band predictions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Subband coding (SBC) method has become an attractive strategy on image coding because it allows more flexibility in the design of coding schemes. A method which considers the intra-band correlation properties in the design of an optimal quadrature mirror filters (QMFs) bank tree is presented. It uses the entropy value of each band to determine if this band is to be further decomposed. The correlation properties between two neighbor high band signals are studied and discussed. It is found that the inter-band correlations are very high between two neighbor high band signals. In particular, more than 61% of samples in the higher band signals need not be encoded and transmitted. A new subband coder for image data is presented. Experimental results are presented in terms of bit rates and the quality of the reconstructed images. The signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) performance of our subband coder is compared to those of other subband coding techniques. Under the same data rate, our subband coder achieves the best SNR performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design automation for a 2 /spl mu/m CMOS gate array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents specific technical information on the development of a design automation system for a 2 /spl mu/m double-metal CMOS gate array. It highlights the physical database requirements of a workstation-based design system and focuses on the features that facilitate the development of the design system and enhance the system's performance efficiency. Some possible pitfalls that should be avoided are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Impacts of static and dynamic models on solutions of voltage stability simulations-case studies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Power system voltage stability has been paid much attention for many years. To investigate the voltage stability problem, a static model is used to examine the feasibility of power flow equations, while differential equations are employed to study the dynamic effectiveness of system components. In this paper, both dynamic and static models are used to study the phenomenon of voltage stability. A 2-bus and a practical systems, namely the Puget Sound power system, are used to serve as samples in the test results. The results pinpoint and classify the difference between these two kinds of models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Task assignment and scheduling in fault-tolerant distributed real-time systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Task assignment and scheduling are two important problems for the design of distributed systems. However, due to system complexity and large task numbers, finding optimal solutions is usually very difficult. In this paper, we develop a heuristic algorithm to perform task assignment and scheduling in fault-tolerant distributed real-time systems. In static, the algorithm computes task assignment quickly to find sub-optimal solutions satisfying all requirements. During system operation, the periods of tasks under different fault conditions are dynamically adjusted to adapt to the loss of system resources. Our goal aims at improving system performance by fully utilizing computing resources, including all spare units. Analytical and simulation results are provided to evaluate the efficiency of this algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new lower bound for channel routing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Channel routing is a key problem in the physical design of VLSI chips. It is known that max(d/sub max/, /spl upsi//sub max/) is a lower bound on the number of tracks required in the reserved two-layer Manhattan routing model, where d/sub max/ is the channel density and v/sub max/ is the length of the longest path in the vertical constraint graph. We propose a polynomial time algorithm that computes a better lower bound on the number of tracks required for routing. This algorithm is also applicable for computing a lower bound on the number of tracks in the three-layer HVH routing model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Circuit partitioning for multiprocessor SPICE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Circuit partitioning issues for circuit simulation on distributed multiprocessors are discussed in this paper. An efficient three level partitioning algorithm for large-scale circuit is proposed. Using this algorithm, we can partition a large-scale circuit into r sub-circuits of similar size while keeping the interconnect set to a minimum. This algorithm may also be implemented in parallel. An example is provided to show the performance of the algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wavelet analysis based multiband excited vocoder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The multiband excitation (MBE) vocoder is a high quality and low complexity speech coder, which is a pitch sensitive speech coder. The authors present a new pitch period estimation method, which is based an wavelet analysis theory. In this method each frame of speech is processed by wavelet transform (WT), then the pitch period is estimated in the frequency domain by a rational interpolation. The results of experiments show that the accuracy of the pitch period can reach the 1/16 sample point and that the method suits different speakers. Computation in this method is time saving and easy to apply in real time implementation. The authors also present improved algorithms for decisions on parameters of the spectrum envelope A/sub m/ and voiced/unvoiced V/UV decision. Based on this, they completed a 4.2 kbps MBE vocoder by computer simulation. The results show that this MBE vocoder is better than the normal transform vocoder both in speech quality and complexity, and easy to realize on a single DSP chip TMS320C25.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated medical practitioner network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes the design and development of an integrated medical practitioner network. The network consists of two major system components: the user interface screen for viewing X-ray images, and the organization of the network. The integrated medical practitioner network provides physicians with access to medical records of the patient through a personal computer. The user interface allows physicians to navigate through patient files, select images, access reports, and perform remote consultations. The patient's records and X-ray images are stored in a database either at a local or a remote side. If the patients' records or X-ray images are not in the local database, the system automatically dials up the external database connected via Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) to retrieve the data. The system also provides a conferencing facility for physicians to discuss patients' cases over the ISDN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving the performance of optimum parallel algorithms on SIMD array processors: programming techniques and methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We describe parallel programming techniques and methods applied to the implementation of two parallel algorithms on an SIMD array processor. These programming techniques and methods can be employed to parallel numerical algorithms for improving their performance and efficiency. First we implemented the column sweep algorithm to solve a lower triangular system of linear equations and then we implemented an algorithm based on Given's rotations for reducing a rectangular matrix into lower triangular form. The estimated execution time of all algorithms has been obtained and analyzed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and realization of DSC equipment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In domestic communication networks, there exist analog and digital telecommunication systems at the same time. Signalling transformation equipment is needed for the interface of these two kind of systems. Digital line signalling conversion equipment (DSC) is used for the transformation between digital 2600 Hz line signalling carried by voice channels and digital type ABCD line signalling carried by TS16 in PCM. That is, the digitalized single frequency 2600 Hz line signalling carried by voice channels is on one side of the 2048 kbits/s digital trunk, and digital type ABCD line signalling carried by timeslot 16 is on the other side of the PCM trunk interface. The DSC interface equipment transforms the two sides associated signalling. DSC equipment may be built independently for PCM terminal equipment or TDM/FDM 60 channels TMUX, and installed in SPC rooms or other suitable places. It may be put together with PCM terminal equipment or TDM/FDM 60 channels TMUX. The DSC equipment consists of the following parts: digital trunk interface, filter and detector for signalling, microprocessor, alarm and display. The block diagram of the DSC equipment is shown. The authors adopt a series of MITEL chips to realize the trunk interface, system control and digital switch.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new blind equalization algorithm for multi-level QAM systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We put forward a new blind equalization algorithm to erase the influence of the random start-up phase offset between the transmitter and the receiver. This algorithm can give an accurate estimation of such a phase offset, and its convergency and stability are better than any other algorithms presented so far. Computer simulation confirms that it works very well with a large phase offset, especially in multi-level QAM systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spectral estimation of two-dimensional, NMR signals by matrix pencil method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Presents a new method based on the matrix pencil approach for estimating the parameters of two dimensional (2D) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) signals in noise. This method is capable of locating frequencies anywhere in the 2D plane, along with their decay rates. Simulation results are given to show the performance of this algorithm and its applicability to the practical 2D NMR problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust pole-assignment design for perturbed discrete time-delay systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The sufficient condition to guarantee robust pole location within a prescribed circular region for perturbed discrete time-delay systems via a state feedback controller is introduced. By the sufficient condition, the tolerable parametric perturbation bounds that ensure all the poles of perturbed discrete time-delay systems to remain inside the desired disk D(e, f), centered at (e, 0) with radius f<1 and |e|+f<1, can be estimated. The stability radius of matrix is employed to investigate the problem, and the result obtained by the presented sufficient condition is a significant improvement over the method reported by Lee et al. Finally, our result is demonstrated by an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Handprinted character recognition system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A handprinted character recognition system is used for inputting unconstrained handprinted characters in a common data table to a computer. In this paper each section of system is described, and the new methods of table segmentation and character recognition are put forward.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new contour coherence based thinning algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new contour-coherence based thinning algorithm is proposed in this paper. In the algorithm, the connectivity template is improved to avoid abnormal broken points. This algorithm only requires one time pre-scanning and all the pixels to be processed are determined by the contour-coherence criterion. The searching time and judgement time, therefore, is shortened by the algorithm so that the processing speed increases considerably. The topological property preservation of this algorithm is better than that of the classical thinning algorithm. This algorithm can guarantee that all the extracted skeletons are single-pixel wide which is very important for the automatic recognition of paper-map.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The function of a design problem solver
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an object oriented design model and discusses the structure and functions of the design problem solver. The class in this model is used to represent the particular problem solver. The relation between classes is represented by the field used by and the compound attributes of the class, and the real connections of the design object can be established only during the solving process. The knowledge of reasoning is separated into two parts: the explicit defined queue of solving action and the constraint satisfying set. If a constraint is violated, the system will try to remove it by modifying the existing solution instead of backtracking. All of these features are useful for design problem solving.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An object-oriented language and its implementation issues on multiprocessors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Object-oriented programming languages show great potential for exploiting concurrency and parallelism. This paper presents a parallel object-oriented language called ParaObject, and its implementation issues on multiprocessors. First, an overview of the language ParaObject is given. Then, the most challenging implementation problems are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hybrid concurrency control approach in heterogeneous distributed database systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We present an integrated concurrency control approach for a multidatabase system that overcomes some weaknesses of previous approaches by A. K. Elmagarmid and Y. Leo (1987) and D. Georgakopoulos et al. (1991). The presented method allows local schedulers, based on different strategies and with different requirements, to be efficiently and effectively integrated into one interoperable structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A machine-description table based instruction scheduler for improving pipeline execution parallelism on QHRC RISC system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a parameterized instruction scheduling algorithm based on machine description table for QHRC RISC system, having a 3-5 stage pipeline structure. It would provide considerable flexibility for instruction scheduling, improving execution efficiency for rapidly upgrading RISC machines. And, using this instruction scheduler as a tool, the effect of several methods for solving instruction interlock problem has been analysed. Finally, a high performance approach combining the hardware feasibility and software effectiveness for solving instruction interlock problem and enhancing pipeline execution parallelism is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A design methodology of knowledge-based and object-oriented for CIMS information model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the features of data are analysed and some design methods of information model are researched in the CIMS environment. A knowledge-based and object-oriented design methodology for the CIMS information model is introduced. It is based on the ideas of artificial intelligence and object-oriented paradigm. The requirement analysis is represented by the knowledge-based techniques and the information structure is represented by the object-oriented techniques in the conceptual schema of the information model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analytical method for solving reactive optimization in power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on the decoupling principle, a quadratic programming model with "nonincrement" variables for evaluating an optimal scheme for reactive power compensation in power systems is presented in this paper. In the model, the reactive power flows on all lines are regarded as the variables to be evaluated and the objective is to maximize the present worth of revenue savings associated with reactive power compensation and energy loss reductions resulting from the application of VAr compensation. In order to completely resolve the convergence problem, the Lagrange multipliers method and the method of "setting the violating quantity equal to its bound" are employed. The proposed model is suitable for resolving the reactive optimization in 35/spl sim/110 kV power networks. This paper concludes with the results of some numerical studies performed on the IEEE 6-bus sample system and a practical 35 kV power network with 21 buses. The method is easy to use and the results are satisfactory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Circuit placement in arbitrarily shaped regions using neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Circuit placement is a very important step in the physical VLSI circuit design, since it has a pronounced affect on the final chip layout. In this paper, a new neural network based on Kohonen's self-organization algorithm is introduced to solve the placement of arbitrarily sized cells in an arbitrarily shaped region. Experimental results show that the proposed method is better than the previous.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel processing system for the computations of wave scattering
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An algorithm based on the moment method for wave scattering analysis is decomposed for parallel computation in a customer designed computer network. The network comprises of transputers and 80486 single processor boards. It is configured in a modified processor farm architecture. Softwares are written for handling low level tasks and special techniques are developed to alleviate the bottleneck imposed by RS422 communication differential links. As reduction of communication between various processing units is one of the key objectives, nearly all computational power of each processing unit in the system is expended in solving the wave scattering problem instead of communication and synchronization. Satisfactory computational speedup is observed. The system is not restrictive to algorithms used in wave scattering or antenna analysis; it is applicable to a class of algorithms which is relatively short yet extremely time consuming.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An all-digital code conversion technique between 32 kbps CVSD and 64 kbps PCM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An all-digital technique for mutual conversion between 32 kbps CVSD encoded signals and 64 kbps standard PCM encoded signals has been proposed. Compared with the existing code conversion schemes, our proposed technique overall eliminates cumulative distortion regardless of the number of the tandem transcodings in the steady state mode (i.e., in the absence of transmission errors). Thus, the algorithm can enhance the performance of the telephone networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The computer image analysis for the 2-D coronary arteriograms
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new method for the automatic identification of coronary border is presented. It mainly utilizes mathematical morphology to segment the blood vessels and derive a refined skeleton for tracking. Finally, a tracking algorithm incorporated with a branching-point model, match filter, skeletons of blood vessels is applied to detect the arterial border and estimate the lumen width of blood vessels. Experiments reveal that the authors' approach can not only eliminate background variations and noise, but accurately define the boundary of coronary angiograms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A pipelined systolic architecture for 2-D discrete Fourier transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new systolic preprocessor is proposed for the two-dimensional discrete Fourier transform (2-D DFT) using an even-odd decomposition algorithm. According to the even-odd decomposition algorithm, a 16-point systolic preprocessor is created for a direct square 2-D DFT implementation. So, the square postprocessor is decreased by a 16 in size and therefore it is very suitable for large 2-D DFTs. The entire architecture is connected in a full pipeline and the pre- and postprocessors can be run simultaneously.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new algorithm for criticizing robust D stability of uncertain control systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a new algorithm of robust D stability analysis based on engineering application. The algorithm has apparent superiority in the field of computation comparing with other methods as far as the perturbed parameters increase. It is not only suitable for the robust D stability analysis of interval polynomial family but also for the polytopic polynomials, and it has also been extended into the robust D stability analysis of the polytopic polynomials with time delays. It is suitable for both continuous-time and discrete-time systems and makes the robust theory take a step towards the engineering application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Preprocessing algorithms for automatic DNA sequence reading
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Image processing algorithms for DNA sequence reading from DNA sequence gel autoradiographs are presented. Background normalization, contrast enhancement, boundary extraction and DNA sequence detection algorithms are respectively described in individual sections. The background normalization algorithm removes the variation of the background. The contrast enhancement algorithm extends the readable range of the captured DNA sequence image and increases the reliability of the DNA sequence reading system. The boundary extraction algorithm detects the boundaries of each lane set which are then used to correct geometric distortions. DNA sequence detection algorithm selects only the bands, determines the order of the bands in the sequence and joins different parts of the sequence. Version 4 of VIPS is used as the image processing algorithm development environment for this project.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An extraction method of analogical information for efficient knowledge processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Case-based reasoning is to solve new problems by adapting previous solutions to old problems. As an alternative to rule-based reasoning, the extraction of similar examples from previous knowledge is very important for solving practical problems. In this paper, we propose a method to extract analogical information for efficient knowledge processing in an intelligent information system supported by relational database technology. At first, the method incrementally retrieves candidate analogical cases from the case base. Then, it selects more similar cases, based on the similarity between the problem and the candidate. The approach substantially reduces the computational complexity in knowledge processing of intelligent information systems such as expert systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adopting line surge arresters to increase lightning-withstand levels of transmission-lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Line surge arresters are applied to increase the lightning-withstand levels of power transmission lines. Here, the lightning-withstand levels, lightning discharge currents and absorbed discharge energies of power line surge arresters are analyzed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient management of object-oriented software development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Object-oriented software development has become popular in recent years because it encourages the use of modern software engineering technology and promotes and facilitates software reuse. It also provides a consistent and natural decomposition of the problem domain, and a structured knowledge representation that enhances software extension, modification and maintenance. In this paper, the key concepts that describe object-oriented software development are data abstraction, information hiding, encapsulation and inheritance. In an object-oriented software development environment using C++, the basic unit is the class which is the realization of data abstraction and information hiding. When the number of classes increases to a certain amount in a multi-user distributed software development environment, there is an urgent need for the central management of classes in a class library system. Current techniques for managing large class libraries make use of browsers. However, these tend to impose severe limitations when the size of the libraries reaches the order of thousands. This paper presents a method for the efficient management of object-oriented development using a relational data dictionary approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of CAD in structure design for power transmission line tower
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The authors apply modern design thought to the structural design of the transmission line towers and compare this approach with traditional design ideas. Such designs use the great advances made in technology and achieve remarkable economic profit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hangul recognition on multi-transputer system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We propose a printed Hangul recognition algorithm on multitransputer system. The vowels in a printed Hangul have very outstanding features and are relatively easy to locate and recognize. We developed subpattern separation algorithm which is based on the vowel. After subpattern separation, the system extracts stroke codes for each subpattern and recognizes them. To get higher recognition speed, we allocated each processing step on a multitransputer system. We tested the validity of the recognition system for 7,000 printed characters from an ordinary text. It showed good result in both speed as well as recognition rates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architecture and operating system design of the M/sup 2/ Database Machine
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper discusses the architecture and operating system design of the M/sup 2/ Database Machine. The primary design goal of the M/sup 2/ is to provide a cost-effective solution to large database processing. The M/sup 2/ architecture is essentially a bus-based two-level hierarchical multiprocesser with a shared-memory multiprocessor structure at the lower level and a shared-disk structure at the higher level. The main distinction of the M/sup 2/ architecture is the high-bandwidth message-passing bus that forms the backbone of the second level, the higher level, of the hierarchy. The high bandwidth of the message-passing bus extends the scalability of the M/sup 2/ architecture to more than one hundred CPUs. Another distinction of the M/sup 2/ Database Machine is its system software. The M/sup 2/ incorporates a directory-base coherence protocol in its distributed file system. The directory-based coherence protocol allows efficient file sharing at the page or file block level.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved maximum likelihood estimation for nonlinear continuous-discrete system and its application to aircraft flight data compatibility checking
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Evans-Goodwin et al. (1985) presented a maximum likelihood algorithm for nonlinear continuous-discrete systems. Accounting for both the process and measurement noises, its filtering process is often numerical unstable and the calculation of sensitivities by using the finite-difference method needs to select the size of perturbation, these limit its validity in practical application. This paper gives a improved maximum likelihood method; an algorithm is given to determine the best perturbation. At the same time, a fast triangular formulation of square-root filter is used to replace the conventional one or the so called stabilized extended Kalman filter to improve the numerical stability of the algorithm given. A practical application to compatibility checking of flight test data indicate that the improved ML algorithm is more efficient.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A knowledge-based system for Chinese NLP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a knowledge-based system for Chinese natural language processing (NLP). The information in the knowledge base consists of static and dynamic knowledge. The process supported by the system involves morphology, syntax and semantic operation. The model is applied to analyze Chinese phonetic alphabet (CPA) sentences and converts them to the corresponding Chinese character sentences.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analyzing cache performance on multi-stream execution processor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, effect of multi-stream (or multithreaded) execution on the performance of cache system is presented. Parameters considered include cache size, line size, set associativity, and unification of instruction/data. The results presented in this paper can be used when designing a multithreaded processor system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of synchronous and asynchronous traffic in an FDDI network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Earlier work on the analysis of the FDDI protocol separately analyzed either synchronous traffic or asynchronous traffic because of the analytical complexity. However, both synchronous and asynchronous traffic are actually correlated; the independent analysis of either one would lose some correctness. The present authors present an approach to analyze all the traffic simultaneously. Within the approach, they still analyze both queues separately, but correlate them by a pseudo ring latency to reflect the dependencies between the traffic. An iterative method is used to numerically obtain the state probabilities for both traffic. Also, by a pseudo conservation law, the mean waiting times of both traffic are obtained. The results show very good agreement with simulation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An extension of SQL to capture more information from objects with many-many relationship
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Many decision support applications such as task assignment, truck deliveries, airline crew scheduling problems usually need to get information from objects with many-many relationship. However, with current relational operators including the complete set of relational algebra it is difficult to get required information from objects with a many-many relationship. We extend SQL so that users can capture more information from objects with a many-many relationship by using the query language directly. The relational operators were extended with six operators, namely, match, maxmatch, cover, mincover, partition, and minpartition.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of service control point in the intelligent network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The overall performance of the service control point (SCP), an element which is a part of the network information control system (NICS), an intelligent network architecture being developed by ETRI, is evaluated by simulation in order to check whether the system satisfies the real time requirements. The multithread scheme is presented for improvement of system performance and its effect is also analyzed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Daily reliability dispatch of generating units
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In accordance with a new viewpoint of operating risk, probabilistic power system unit commitment is studied in this paper. The proposed approach takes the unit stochastic failure characteristics and uncertainty of load forecasts into account. With the prediction of operating risk, a dynamic programming model for daily unit commitment is established to minimize the objective function of spinning reserve throughout a day, and an algorithm is also proposed. A numerical example is given to illustrate the application of the proposed approach, and the results show that the approach and algorithm are both feasible and efficient.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A videotex system under network environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An information service system of a two layer topological architecture, based on a LAN, under a network environment is presented. The upper network is used to implement the sharing of resources by the workstations. The lower one is used for mutual communication and the management of user terminals. The system is designed to the videotex technical standard and is compatible with both Chinese and English.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A knowledge-based cell controller for flexible manufacturing systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The cell control level is often the integral part in the implementation of computer integrated manufacturing (CIM) for the control of shop floor production. However, the conventional cell controllers operate with little intelligence and are often unable to adapt to different manufacturing environment and requirements. This paper introduces a framework for a knowledge-based cell controller that is currently being develop for GINTIC's flexible manufacturing systems. The cell controller is designed with a knowledge-base system embedded in an object-oriented control system. Changes in the production environment and operation rules can be easily reflected by modifying the rule sets embedded. The functionality of a cell controller, in the context of GINTIC's control model for flexible manufacturing system, is carefully studied and mapped to the knowledge-based framework.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ownership-based cache consistency model in a distributed file system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Write-sharing of files in a distributed file system is considered as an obstacle to caching files on clients' site. We are specially concerned with cacheability of write-shared files, and propose an ownership-based cache consistency model. With our model the server CPU loads can potentially be reduced without violating data consistency in the case of file write-sharing. We show the validity of our model with a simulation method, in terms of server utilization and network traffic.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interworkstation Reference: a new approach to LAN application development
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Resource-sharing and communication among workstations are main purposes of networking of computers. Based on characters and visual volume concepts of LANs, we present a new approach to applications of LANs-Interworkstation Reference (IWR), which combines two kinds of the applications above into one form. In this paper, the basic concepts about IWR are introduced and then methods of design and implementation and security strategies of IWR are given in details.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simplified multistage decoding method using threshold technique for multilevel coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A simplified multistage decoding method using threshold technique for multilevel coding is presented. It can decrease the time delay of the multistage decoding greatly without the loss of the decoding performance and therefore make the real-time decoding for multilevel codes possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The implementation of X.400 P3
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Since the CCITT published in 1984 a set of Recommendations on MHSs-X.400(84), the research and development of MHSs have been extensively deployed. Some utility systems which support the X.400 standard have been widely used. But in these systems, the UA and MTA reside in the same system where P2 and P1 are included, but not P3 and P7. The implementation of P3 and P7 is still at the research stage. This paper gives a method of implementing P3, a protocol defined in the CCITT X.400(84) standard and improved in the X.400(88) standard, which is used to enable the MTS-user (UA or MS) to access the MTS Abstract Service remotely. Based on the ISODE7.0 and PP6.0, we have implemented P3 according to the CCITT X.400(88) in UNIX systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Edge detection using scale space knowledge
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Edge detection has acquired enormous importance in computer vision research: gaussian filter has been widely used in the past to accomplish this task. Although the gaussian filter has nice scaling behaviour and is computationally elegant, it suffers from the disadvantage of delocalisation of edges when operated at higher scales. Multi-scale processing of an image is thus required. In this paper, the process of edge detection has been looked upon as a reasoning problem. In the past, knowledge handling and reasoning have been attributed to high level vision routines, but from the results presented here, it can be argued that reasoning does play an important role in the process of edge detection. The knowledge base required for this is formed out of the theory of scale space. Particular emphasis is laid on the behaviour of delocalised, missing and false or spurious edges in the scale space. The scale space is formed by operating the LoG filter of different sizes on the input image. The dissimilarity among the zero crossings is measured across the scales. It is useful in the removal of false edges. A compatibility measure relates the zero-crossing contour with the current scale parameter, /spl sigma/. The rules are coded in NEXPERT OBJECT 2.0. The results are compared with Canny's multiple edge detection algorithm (J.F. Canny, 1986).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A research on fast Hadamard transform (FHT) digital systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A 2/sup m//spl times/2/sup m/ standard Hadamard matrix can be written as the mth power of one matrix. Based on this principle, the paper presents a digital system to carry out the fast Hadamard transform (FHT), which is composed of one arithmetic unit, four random-access memories, two address generators, /spl pi//sub 1/, and /spl pi//sub 2/, and a control unit. Experiments show that the hardware system can finish the FHT within 20 ms for a picture of 4095 elements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust stability analysis by transformation of Youla parametrization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper addresses an alternative approach to analyse nominal and robust stability via Youla parametrization (1976). The parameter, Q, which is used to form all nominally stabilizing controllers, can then be interpreted as a feedback compensator in the transformed framework of this method. Thus, we can purposefully design the parameter Q to achieve H/sub /spl infin// optimal performance. In addition, the constructive procedure is provided to form the standard plant in the presence of uncertainties. The condition of robust stability is also obtained for the uncertain systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of asynchronized synchronous generators on the transient stability of power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on the simulation of a typical power system, the effect of asynchronized synchronous generators on the transient stability of power systems is investigated. The comparison of transient performances between asynchronized synchronous generators and conventional synchronous generators is presented. The transient processes of power systems with different structure under different operation states are calculated and the critical clearing times of sudden short-circuit faults are given. The discussions show that the transient performances of asynchronized synchronous generators are much better than conventional synchronous generators and it is effective to install asynchronized synchronous generators in power stations for improving the transient stability of power systems, especially under the case of surplus reactive power on transmission lines connected to power stations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An experimental electrical impedance tomography system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The design of an experimental electrical impedance tomography (EIT) system is presented. The aim of EIT is to reconstruct the internal resistance distribution of a test object (region). The project involves building a data acquisition system that applies current to the test object and measures the induced voltage responses on the boundary of that object. The measured responses are then processed using the back-projection image reconstruction algorithm to acquire an approximated image of the test object's internal resistance distribution. The laboratory experimental results showed that recognizable images can be achieved on both open and closed boundary conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of fuzzy grammar to handwritten character recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The main disadvantage of formal language theory applied to syntactic pattern recognition is that it is often too rigid to handle real patterns which are usually distorted or noisy. However, it is well known that the concept of vagueness can provide a convenient way for describing ill-defined patterns. In this paper, using handwritten character recognition as an example, we show that fuzzy language can be an effective tool for syntactic pattern recognition.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polynomial approximation based learning search
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, polynomial approximation method and theory are introduced into the research of learning search of artificial intelligence. By so doing, a learning search algorithm can, after sufficient number of problem-solving, construct a heuristic estimate function h(.) which uniformly approximates to the optimal estimate function h*(.) by arbitrary precision. One of these learning search algorithms, A-B/sub n/, is described and it is shown that, when the number of the previous problem-solving becomes large enough, the worst-case complexity of A-B/sub n/ can be reduced to O(poly(N)), where N is the length of the optimal solution path, poly(N) is a polynomial function of N.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model of the knowledge compilation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The authors explain their knowledge compilation model and discuss its implementation. The most important issues are examined. Despite the immaturity of the model, knowledge compilation has proven to be a useful tool. Research into the model continues.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculation of transient parameters and overvoltages in cable/GIS power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, the present different calculation methods of cable/GIS parameters, including analytical methods, the finite element method, and the subdivision method, are analyzed and compared. With example calculations, suitable methods are recommended. The surface subdivision method is presented for the first time to calculate parameters at high frequencies and is shown to be both simple and convenient. This paper presents the pathological problem that exists at high frequency in the modal transformation of cable/GIS systems. This pathological problem is solved in this paper by removing the pathological elements in modal transformation. With the transient parameters calculated, the influence of the earth on the surge propagation along the cable is also analyzed. The cable sheath is considered as one conductor to reflect the strong effect of the earth. The results of calculations for lightning surge overvoltages in urban cable/GIS systems show that three-phase models should be used instead of one-phase.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TempIS: interfacing system for graphical display of temporal databases
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents an interfacing between a temporal database management system (DBMS) and a graphical display system. This integrated system, is called TempIS and consists of a temporal DBMS, a graphical display system, and an interface control system. The temporal DBMS supports time, but conventional DBMS's do not. Therefore, TempIS shows graphical animation with time factor by using a graphical knowledge base. We describe how to interface them as well as the structure of the temporal DBMS and graphical display system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Next generation of Chinese text-to-speech system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The author presents a concept of speech characteristic database of Chinese text-to-speech conversion. The database gives a complete description from Chinese characters to speech. The speech characteristic database is composed of basic speech database and rules. The basic speech database includes tone syllables, neutral tone syllables and everyday expressions. The rules include pronunciation, tales of words, grammatical rules and semantic feature rules. Based on basic speech database, the description from Chinese characters to speech can be completed by the tales. Perfecting the database is the basis of realizing high qualitative Chinese text-to-speech conversion. According to the speech characteristic database, a Chinese text-to-speech system is developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Petri net tools for analysis and verification of task scheduling algorithm in real time distributed process control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper first show by formalism that a task scheduling algorithm can be equivalently specified by a set of rules, that is, a set of specification rules can constitute a task scheduling algorithm; and then show that these rules can be translated into a marked Petri net model involving the Petri net place,transitions and arcs that correspond to the states and state transition of the running procedure of the task scheduling algorithm so that reachability graph can be generated in terms of the model. From the reachability graph, we can see if there are livelock, deadlock and other faults of the task scheduling algorithm. In the last part, we illustrate an example to explain the detail process of rules' equivalent specification, rules' translation, and reachability graph generation in terms of a task scheduling algorithm, to analyse and verify its correctness and completeness.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of variable structure control techniques for improving power system dynamic stability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a study on the application of variable structure control techniques for improving power system dynamic stability. The basic concepts of variable structure control are discussed. The procedure of designing a variable structure controller for the linearized model obtained by linearizing the nonlinear characteristics of a synchronous machine connected to infinite busbar is explained. The possibility of a controller which would guarantee proper operation irrespective of machine output power, transmission line reactance and infinite bus voltage is discussed. The results of the simulation studies show that with the proposed controller, the stability of the synchronous machine is improved significantly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architecture for VLSI implementation of discrete cosine transform processor for video codec
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A VLSI chip having a small number of arithmetic components to implement the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) in real time is desirable. In this paper various fast algorithms are taken into considerations to find the minimum necessary arithmetic components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Buffering schemes for ATM switches
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The ATM switch, which is the most promising approach for the new switching technology in B ISDN, can be grouped into two major types: blocking and nonblocking switches. Even in nonblocking switches, it is still possible for the output collision to occur. To avoid cell loss due to collision, it is necessary to use buffers. Three buffering strategies for ATM switches are described in the paper. Their performances are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prolog vs procedural backtracking
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Backtracking algorithms try to solve problems by generating and testing a set of possible solutions. Typically, there are some points in the execution of a backtracking algorithm where execution can proceed in more than one way. Such points are called choice points. Backtrack technique has been incorporated into variants of many high level languages, mostly procedural languages, such as Pascal, Fortran and LISP. Also, backtracking is one of the major features of Prolog. A programming language with has built-in support for backtracking algorithms is called a backtracking language. Typically its semantics recognise success or failure of execution, and it supports programming of choice points. It hides details about how choices are made at choice points, how to backtrack, and how to resume the previous state. Backtracking languages find wide application in artificial intelligence algorithms. We compare the backtracking mechanisms of Prolog and other backtracking programming languages, and present a new backtracking language.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interconnection of existing LANs with B-ISDN using simple router function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In order to support the interconnection of distant LANs (Local Area Networks) via B-ISDN, we present main issues posed by interworking and suggest efficient methods for resolving these issues. This paper also describes the functions and organization of the high speed B-LTA (Broadband-LAN Terminal Adaptor) which can interconnect existing Ethernet or FDDI LAN. Our proposed B-LTA system is a simple router which supports direct and indirect LAN interconnection method. The simple router uses only network address of LAN for address filtering, address resolution and connection establishment function.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An approach of object oriented database for open energy management system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper an approach of object oriented database for an open energy management system is introduced. The requirement of an open system and the merit of the object oriented programming technique are briefly described. An example of object oriented database design is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel hybrid coding scheme based on wavelet transform
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A hybrid image coding scheme using the wavelet transform (WT) is presented. The advantages of the wavelet representation are utilized to decorrelate the high information redundancy between the adjacent image lines. The coding of the resulting multiresolution difference signals takes into account the human visual system (HVS). This paper analyses the statistical characteristics of the difference information. The quantization and coding techniques incorporating the human visual characteristics and the probability distribution of the difference signals are also discussed. The experimental results demonstrate the better performance of the proposed hybrid coding system compared with the results achieved previously.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Knowledge-based design support system for radar system design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The radar system design is the most important part of the design process during which alternative design solutions are generated.
