In this paper we present and develop the knowledge-based design support system (KBDSS) for radar system scheme design. The KBDSS consists of five parts: user interface, knowledge base, expert system, inference engine, design case base and model base for radar system analysis. Two models of design process are: decomposition and case-based reasoning. The knowledge representation in KBDSS is based on an object-oriented paradigm. Frames combining with production rules and procedures design methods are used to represent the knowledge of design objects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of source reactance on power transfer limited by voltage instability in compensated transmission systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The effect of generator reactance on power transfer limits of EHV lines operating on the verge of voltage instability and having different series and shunt compensation schemes is investigated. Numerical results for maximum power transfer, critical angular separation and critical voltage are given with respect to five different compensation schemes considering different line length, power factors and degrees of series and shunt compensation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust control systems with disturbance observers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: It is shown that the control system with disturbance observers has a nice property of disturbance rejection even without an integral action in the controller if the controlled process has an integration. This paper is concerned with a robust control design using H/sub /spl infin// optimality theory when the controlled process is subject to model uncertainties, in which the conditions of robust stability and stability guaranteed control system are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A DCME frame structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Digital circuit multiplication equipment (DCME) permits the concentration of a number of 64kbit/s PCM encoded input trunk channels on a reduced number of transmission channels. It has two basic techniques; one is digital speech interpolation (DSI), the other is adaptive differential pulse code modulation (ADPCM). Essential facilities, interface conditions and overall performance requirements are given by recommendation G.763, 1988. However, frame structure didn't detail assignment. Many corporations such as ECI, NEC and AT and T have produced products. They have used different DCME frame structures. NEC'S NCM-501 DCME fully complies with INTELSAT IESS-501, DCME multiframe length is is longer than new DCME frame length. This new DCME frame structure is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The blind equalization technique for MPSK modulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper discusses one new blind equalization technique for MPSK signal. The blind equalization algorithm based on the technique has been presented and analysed. Computer simulation indicates that the blind equalization algorithm has a better convergence and error performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Split-radix DET algorithms and the computation of DCT and DST
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Split-radix direct algorithms for four types of discrete exponent transforms (DETs) are introduced. The DCT and DST may be directly computed using the split-radix DET algorithms. It is shown that the direct computations of DCT and DST have simple structure and in-place implementation. Their output is in bit-reserved order, rather than Hadamard order or other complex order. The direct computations can be implemented using the software or hardware of split-radix DFT algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hybrid model for handwritten Chinese characters recognition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid model is presented for handwritten Chinese characters recognition. First, a new and reliable stroke extraction method is proposed. Based on the extracted strokes, the cross-points can also be determined. The characters with the same numbers of strokes and cross-points are grouped together in rough classification stage. Second, a Bayesian neural network for fine classification is presented. The experimental results show that the commonly used 1000 characters can be partitioned into 70 groups and each group contains 23 characters on the average and the average recognition rates of 95% and 85% for recognizing the characters written by two specified persons and selected from the CCL/HCCR1 database had been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image segmentation for measurement of particulate contamination in hydraulic fluid
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An image segmentation method is proposed to identify the particulate contamination in hydraulic fluid. The procedure of segmentation consists of three steps. First, a partial contour of the interest object is derived by an adaptive edge focusing algorithm. Second, the derived edge points are considered as seedpoints of the threshold surface, then a special surface interpolating technique is employed to generate the threshold surface. In the last step, the image is segmented by the threshold surface. The experimental results show that when background noise and objects are very similar in both shape and gray level, the proposed algorithm can get better results than the other segmentation methods studied. Thus, the algorithm has been used in many kinds of particulate contamination measurement in hydraulic fluid as a very important image preprocessing step.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multisensor multiframe change detection via optimal likelihood ratio test
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on the likelihood ratio test with the maximum likelihood estimation, optimal multi-sensor data fusion is addressed for the detection of changing scene in consecutive multiple image frames. It is shown that the information necessary for the sensors to transmit to the fusion center is the estimation of the correlation coefficients. The optimal threshold of the testing is obtained from the criterion of a constant false alarm. The experimental results illustrate that the performance of the detection scheme is improved when the number of the sensors and/or the frames increased. Furthermore, the changing areas of interest can be extracted accurately from the change detection algorithm combined with preprocessing and mask techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An expert system for recognizing hand-written Chinese characters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Chinese characters are highly structural such that a syntactical approach for recognition is suitable. For hand-written characters, such an approach experiences problems because of writing style variability. An expert system with machine learning is proposed for the recognition of Chinese characters. The authors adopted concept learning in their system which is intended to tackle the problems such as mutual similarities of characters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: KBCOPS: a knowledge-based co-ordinated problem solver
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Thinking, conflict avoidance and planning results optimization are the key for co-ordinated robot problem solving. The paper presents a knowledge-based, robot co-ordinated problem solver (KBCOPS). It also illustrates the planning power of the KBCOPS system by solving and analyzing some typical planning problems in the simulated double robots world.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer network and data communications for power system real time control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Computer networks and data communications for (nonlinear, distributed) power system real time control are discussed in this paper through the analysis of a newly designed power system computer control network with redundantly structured network hardware and software. A new concept of the computer control network is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prototyping database functions using type theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Database researchers have viewed prototyping as an effective method of investigating new concepts and techniques. However most well known prototypes have been substantial software development projects that involve several man years of effort. We discuss a relatively inexpensive method of prototyping database structures and concepts using the sound formal system of constructive logic and type theory. The method is illustrated by first describing the database structure of a generic data model, and then defining one of the algebraic operators for it. Specific data models can be derived from this generic model as illustrated by the authors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A scheme of experimental research environment for ILP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Advanced uniprocessor research concentrates on exploiting instruction level parallelism (ILP) to improve computational performance. This article introduces experimental research in certain programs looking at the above questions. The design of an experimental research environment is introduced in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The heuristic approach in IDSS for project planning and scheduling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Classical project planning and scheduling techniques have been successful in project management. At the present, intelligent decision support systems (IDSS) have been proposed and applied in real world. We propose a heuristic approach in IDSS for project planning and scheduling and developed a synthesis system of project management and control decision support system (PMCDSS), which is an intelligent interactive computer-based system. In this paper we discuss the heuristic approach based on PMCDSS. The main ideas are: (1) Building an adaptive model (e.g. object-oriented modeling) to represent the multiobjective problem in project management. (2) The core of such model is resources allocation. (3) Domain knowledge representation and inference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonblocking conditions for self-routing Benes network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A Benes network is a rearrangeable interconnection network. To implement self-routing in Benes network, head-bits should be added before the destination address bits. A set nonblocking conditions for self-routing Benes network are presented in the paper, based on which the head-bits can be computed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing the dynamic performance of video ADC in the HDTV system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper first presents a testing method by designing a fast in and slow out (FISO) memory system. Secondly, the authors use the bispectrum to test the harmonic distortion of video ADCs in high definition TV (HDTV) systems. The result shows that this method has the advantages of low cost and high detective resolution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the design of hyper-ellipsoidal pattern classifier and its application to power system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new approach to the design of a hyper-ellipsoidal pattern classifier is derived. In comparison with previous works, non-linear mapping and the dimensional problem are avoided. The approach is based on a programming technique and, therefore, it is of low complexity. The design approach is applied to transient security assessment (TSA) in a power system. The performance of the pattern classifier is shown to be satisfactory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital HDTV system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Both European and Japanese have shown interest in HDTV broadcasting by satellite while USA was interested in HDTV terrestrial broadcasting using digital image compression techniques. This was possible by latest VLSI developments in digital image compression for HDTV applications. Some of the digital HDTV systems developed in US and Europe are reviewed and compared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of an artificial intelligence controller for effective control of engine speed and pump flow according to working condition of an excavator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper explores advanced controller design concepts by combining the fields of artificial intelligence (AI) and automatic control. To accomplish this, the effective AI controller for the working mode control of excavator is designed. The knowledge bases for the controller are established from the human operator's experience and basic engineering knowledge and the operating curves of the engine and pump. And a new gain self-tuning algorithm is proposed for closed loop gain control. The excavator with the controller shows to drive more effectively and efficiently in each working mode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel planar lattice architecture for competitively inhibited neural network simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Competitively inhibited neural network (CINN) appears to be promising in adaptive parameter estimation and pattern classification for its intelligent information processing potential. A neurocomputer of the parallel planar lattice architecture (PPLA) based on transputers for large scale, high speed simulations of the CINN is proposed in this paper. It has an even greater expandability of parallelism and exhibits sufficient flexibility to simulate the CINN of various network configurations and parameters. The experiments demonstrate that the performance of this neurocomputer is almost proportional to the number of processors by using a load balancing algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Continuous output sliding control design and alleviation of the state observation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A schematic design methodology for sliding mode control is presented. State observation is not necessary. When the sliding mode is achieved, the output tracking error decays in an exponential rate. An alternative approach is also proposed which retains the positive features of classical sliding mode control methods but uses a continuous control law so that the inherent control chattering due to high frequency switching in the controller is eliminated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Portable controlling software package for parallel fault-tolerant computer system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A portable software system to support distributed parallel and fault tolerant computing in a PC network environment is described. It facilitates better utilization of system resources and provides a platform for fault tolerant computing. The software system consists of a concurrent control library and a program translator. The design is dedicated for a master-slave, loosely coupled and Tandem-model configuration. The implementation of slave system management, communication protocol and fault tolerance is discussed. Some performance analysis using networked PC's is also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling and robust control system design of a type of missile
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, linearized mathematical models of a type of missile are established on a series of representative points chosen from a typical trajectory of a missile. Upon a tremendous amount of numerical calculation and analysis of the obtained data, some facts are discovered which are important to robust control system design. A knowledge base for the design of non-minimal phase control systems is built on the basis of calculation and analysis of one thousand non-minimal phase systems. A new approach is then presented to the design of robust control system. It inherits the advantages of the "optimization of parametrized desired eigenloci" method, but is applicable to non-minimal phase plants. The controller designed by this method not only guarantees system stability, dynamic performance, robustness and controller stability, but also has a structure much simpler than what the H/sub /spl infin// approach and /spl mu/- approach might give.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analysis for power transmission technology from large energy resources
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The authors present and discuss the possible alternatives of future bulk power transmissions to meet the Chinese state policy of "Transmitting Power from West to East" with a synthetical consideration both of large transmitting power from the giant energy resources and the new technical progress in the next century, taking Southwest hydropower resources as an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The studies of stability for dynamic routing in packet switching network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The problem concerning the dynamic stability for routing decision under dynamically varying load conditions in a packet switching network is studied. From a system control point of view, the control-oriented space state model describing the process of packets transmitted throughout the network and routing variables in a multiple traffic and multiple link network are established. A definition of the stability of the routing decision is given and some constraints and conditions about the network link average utilization function G(. ) and the routing diversion matrix R/sup d/ ensuring the stability of the network are developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Artificial neural networks for transient stability assessment of power system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper explores the suitability of using two artificial neural network models (ANN) as tools for power system transient security assessment (TSA). Firstly, a TSA problem of a local power net is changed into a pattern recognition problem suitable for an ANN, and sample data are preprocessed. Then BPN and KNN models are used respectively for this TSA problem. The suitability and advantages of the two models are discussed and compared on mapping capability of the problem, estimation of certainty factor of interpolating results and ANN size. The results show that from the point of view of TSA application, the KNN model is better than BPN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The transmission of facsimile file via radio channel using packet method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper examines a method of transmission of facsimile (FAX) files via radio channels using the HDLC format (packet method) during step C. Thus, one can control the the error using all the methods known, such as ARQ, change rate, FEC and hybrid ARQ. In the paper the authors used ARQ, change rate (rate adaptable) to control the error first. The results of the experiment show that one can transmit FAX files without any error.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: GA approach to invariant matching: under noise and geometric transformations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper proposes a new approach to solve the matching problem, in which the genetic algorithm is used as the search strategy to find the optimal matching between the features of the object and those of the model. Feature points matching is used as an example to discuss this kind of approach. Firstly the invariant relative attributes of features are discussed. With the invariant attributes, we analyse the expression of matching points. Secondly by using the genetic algorithm's schema we design the new approach to the invariant matching. The experiments show that the algorithm is indeed invariant to the geometric transformations and it can work in the noise case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systolic algorithms for power series manipulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Linear time systolic algorithms are given for computation of product, quotient and power of power series using triangular networks having unit pipelining period.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Introduction and solutions to NOE path planning with incomplete information
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper addresses the nap-of-the-Earth (NOE) path planning with incomplete information. We first define the path planning for NOE flight. Then we discuss how to divide the problem into several subproblems. For each of the subproblems, we propose a clear definition along with a brief description of the solutions to the subproblem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fast intelligent target detection algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new algorithm used to automatically detect targets in a complicated background is presented. Based on a knowledge base and prior experimental data, the multi-double-gate filter which uses the features of the target to separate targets from clutter background, is a very useful algorithm. It has a higher detection rate and a smaller amount of computation than other similar algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intelligent design versus solving artificial problems-artificial intelligence research at the cross-roads
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The major hypothesis of the paper is that artificial intelligence research has reached a point where two diverging future paths could be followed. On the one hand, one could take the development of technical possibilities and try to find problems that fit to existing technical solutions. We call this route "solving artificial problems". On the other hand we propose an attractive field of future AI research, which concentrates on the design of empirically relevant solutions for man-machine interactions by splitting decisions in an intelligent way, into those taken by machines and those taken by human groups. Using the notion of intelligent design we give some examples to illuminate our case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lighting power supply line characteristics and performance of an FSK discrimination detector
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on experiment and measurement in a typical situation, the statistical analysis on transmission characteristics of a lighting power supply line is performed in this paper. The paper also discusses the design and performance of an FSK discrimination detector in some detail. The modems based on the detector have been successfully used for computer networking by using the lighting power supply line.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A priority-driven concurrency control protocol based on data contention rates for distributed real-time database systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a priority-driven concurrency control protocol to schedule active transactions accessing distributed real-time databases based on priority information. This protocol controls real-time transactions with different priority more effectively. By combining flexible synchronization techniques for desirable real-time conflict resolution, it intends to avoid unnecessary aborts or blocking of conflicting transactions. Thus, flexible priority-driven scheduling enables this protocol to interleave and complete as many transactions as possible without sacrificing data or timing constraints. Performance is achieved by increasing the number of transactions, especially with higher priority.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The implementation of automatic monitoring network system for trains
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents the implementation of Automatic Monitoring Network System for Trains (AMNST), and describes the dynamically remote real time network monitoring method for the safe running of trains, and discusses the configuration of network hardware, the design and implementation of the network software. The method has been used in the Da-Qin railway monitoring system and the results are satisfied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some practices of analyzing power system transient stability with the trajectory analysis method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A recently proposed method for analyzing the output data of a traditional transient stability program, which is known as the trajectory analysis method, has been applied to a real world power system. The results are presented in this paper and they show that for the most disturbed generators, the value of the stability index (S/sub i/) is monotonically decreased with the deterioration of stability, by any mode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of the expert system for train dispatching
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In the TDES (Train Dispatching Expert System), a hierarchical train dispatching knowledge base is built. The inference engine of the TDES is designed with a three-level structure so that the TDES is a dynamic production system with multiple levels, which can automatically select the rule sets and inference control strategies according to the information produced by the TMSS (Train Movement Simulation System). Consequently, the resolution process of problems is self-adapting and closer to the complicated and quick-witted thinking process of train dispatchers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault tolerance and pipelining of VLSI combinational logic networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: On the basis of alternating logic and complementary logic, a new fault-tolerant design method named as alternate complementary logic is proposed. Some properties of this logic are analyzed and a scheme of the combinational network realizing an arbitrary alternate complementary logic function is proposed. Under the assumption of the stuck-fault model, the network has the capabilities of on-line self-testing and fault-masking, and its time-delay can be reduced by pipelining.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Globally stable adaptive controller of robot manipulators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper addresses an adaptive inverse dynamics robotic control algorithm. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, the theorems on the global stability of robotic system are proven. The proposed algorithm is easy to implement and the robotic system is robust to parameter uncertainty and payload variation. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the scheme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The simulation of machine-network interaction in multi-machine power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a newly developed machine-network interaction transient simulation program. This program is especially useful in calculation of the transient shaft torque of turbine-generating units caused by various kinds of faults and switching operations. It can also be used for other purposes such as calculation of transient voltages and currents for harmonic analysis. In the program, most of the important power system elements such as generators, transmission lines, circuit breakers, transformers, shunt/series compensators, infinite buses, shafts of turbine generating units, excitation systems and power system stabilizers are modeled. Great efforts have been made to enhance the simulation speed. The implicit trapezoidal rule of integration is adopted to solve the differential equations and the critical damping method is used to eliminate the numerical oscillations caused by switching operations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: I: an integrated programming language
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an integrated programming language I which incorporates the logic and the functional paradigms in an object-oriented framework. Our integration technique is based on dividing objects as either logic or functional objects. Methods in logic objects are modified Horn clauses which can invoke methods in functional objects. Methods in functional objects are applicative functions and are permitted to invoke methods in logic objects. The object-oriented nature makes methods be inheritable and have distributed execution environment (object). In addition, different levels of parallelism can be exploited in I.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Congestion control in B-ISDN based on a fluid flow dynamic model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We propose a dynamic feedback flow control method for reactive congestion control in B-ISDN (Broadband Integrated Service Digital Network) based on ATM (Asynchronous Transfer Mode) switching and multiplexing technology. Our approach adopts a fluid flow model to represent the dynamic behaviour of the queue length in a bottle-neck link. Based on this model a forecast of the future state of the buffer is used to predict congestion. A feedback control scheme avoids or reduces cell loss by warning the controllable source to reduce its traffic delivery rate. An intelligent controller proposed for the controllable source can intelligently adjust its delivery rate according to feedback information and local delivery history. Comparison of our feedback control scheme with normal open-loop flow control methods using simulation results show that cell loss is controlled over a wide range of traffic flow, and that the simple scheme is robust.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Subband DCT coding of HDTV signal in intraframe under a bit rate of 140 Mbits/s
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A subband coding scheme based on the DCT of the intraframe is demonstrated, which compresses the bit rate of an HDTV signal from about 1.2 Gbits/s to less than 140 Mbits/s. The HDTV signal is split up into four subbands by a separable 2D quadrature mirror filter bank (QMF). The DCT transform and quantization, considering the property of human vision are applied to the baseband. The other high bands are quantized by a quantizer with a center deadzone. To further reduce the information bit rates, variable length coding (VLC) and run-length coding (RLC) are applied to the quantized signal in each band. The buffer adaptive control on the bit rate of subbands makes the data steam in the channel uniform. Computer simulation results are presented in terms of the bit-per-pel and SNR of the reconstructed pictures. The objective and subjective quality of the reconstructed pictures are excellent.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Attribute-based recognition and association
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper discusses attribute-based recognition and association. An object has different attributes with it, according to different notices, so it can be recognised through these attributes. Association is an important psychological phenomenon and can also be demonstrated with attributes. An attribute is a set of features of an object. The connection between two attributes can be measured by similarity. Thus, recognition and association can be processed by computing the similarity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On sensitivity improvement by a stable controller in SISO digital control systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In Hera and Sung (1989), it is shown that for a SISO digital control system, sensitivity improvement is possible by a two-delay output controller. In this paper, it is shown that the result is restricted to a limited class of SISO plants only. To help circumvent the problem, the author provides an approach towards sensitivity improvement using a generalized sampled-data hold function (GSHF) based two-delay output controller. The proposed controller is able to attain the infimum of the H/sup /spl infin//-norm sensitivity optimization problem for a two-delay digital control system irrespective of whether the continuous-time plant has zeros at the origin or not.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust performance control and analysis of ill-conditioned plants
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Ill-conditioned plants with delays are generally difficult to control. Motivated by the work of Skogestad, Morari, and Doyle (1988), this paper deeply investigates the robust control of ill-conditioned plants, and provides some new results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DGPSL: a distributed graphics processing support library for graphics and image
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Presents DGPSL (distributed graphics processing support library) which is one of major components of the authors' distributed graphics processing support environment. It is a facility for implementing graphics applications which require expensive computing power that is not available on single workstation. The paper describes in detail the techniques in designing and implementing DGPSL.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of a neural network controller for robotic applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Computer simulations have been performed for analysing the learning behaviour of a neural network when it is used as a controller in a robotic control system. Specifically, the effect of the backpropagation parameters on the convergence and stability of the network have been investigated. The neural network is configured as a feedforward inverse controller. Results indicated that increasing the number of neurons in the hidden layer will improve the convergence speed. However, beyond a certain limit additional neurons will cause system oscillations and finally instability. The main contribution of this paper is the derivation of a relationship between the rms error and the number of iterations used in the training of the neural network. Guidelines for selecting the neural network parameters are also given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Index-predicted vector quantizer for image coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new structure of the index-predicted sector quantizer (IPVQ) is proposed for image coding. The IPVQ can exploit the correlation among inter-sectors through prediction. Compared with the general sector quantizer (GVQ), the IPVQ may obtain a higher compression ratio, while keeping the same picture quality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Timer management in X.25 layer 2-an interpretation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The X.25 layer 2 protocol describes three timers for error recovery and efficient data transfer. Timer management in any protocol requires heavy processing and can cause excessive overheads if not implemented intelligently. This paper discusses some techniques to be followed to reduce these overheads. The number of timers running at any instant, and the number of times that timers need to be set or reset, can be controlled. The piggyback timer, if used intelligently, can lead to efficient data transfers. The current research done in this area assumes Poisson and deterministic traffic types to decide the timer value. Our study of the layer 2 protocol in relation to the higher layers revealed that the traffic pattern can be predicted in some cases. A piggyback scheme was devised that is dependent on the traffic pattern to ensure high performance of the protocol. This scheme is discussed in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some new results on correlation properties of sequences used in CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Some new upper bounds on family size of sequences used in code division multiple access (CDMA) applications are presented in the paper to provide more insight into the tradeoffs between correlation parameters. Results searched by computer are also given in comparison with Gold sequences to illustrate the properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Single-tone HF high speed data modem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on the selection of a two-dimensional signal constellation in the presence of phase jitter and Gaussian noise and the estimation of the characteristics of several fast speed equalization algorithm, the project of a single-tone HF high speed data modem using two Texas Instruments TMS320C25 digital signal processors is proposed. The project selects the 16QAM signaling format and a receiver employing a baseband decision feedback square root Kalman equaliser. A different function can be completed by loading a different software, making the modem multifunctional.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Construction of 3-D fracture based on fractal theory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A new method of construction of 3D fracture based on fractal theory is proposed. The fractal model of metal fracture has been developed, and the surface of fracture has been constructed by using fractal iteration. Metal fracture inspected by scan electron microscope (SEM) is the meet common method in studying fracture. We prove that the average error of estimating the surface and volume of fractures using this method, is the best.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wavelet transform and multi-resolution synthesis of texture images
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Based on the principle of the wavelet transform, the paper introduces the wavelet transform theory into the synthesis of texture images and proposes an efficient multi-resolution synthesis method. Simulations by computer are carried out. Two natural texture images are generated from the multi-resolution synthesis model and the effect of the methods is presented by examples, The experimental results indicate that with the present method not only the microtextures or macrotextures can be modeled and synthesized, but also both together, and the synthesized texture images have visual and analytical characteristics similar to those of the natural texture images.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant duplex logical systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents, first of all, a definition of failure logical functions and an extention of boolean functions by defined failure logical functions. Then, asymmetrically failure logical circuits having only "0" failure and only "1" failure feature are assumed as fail-safe logical circuits. An architecture of the fail-safe logical system, which consisted of said logical circuits is depicted. And then, a structural principle and the practical example of fault-tolerant logical systems composed of duplex fail-safe logical systems having detectable functions of fault systems with fail-safe features are specified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementing Manufacturing Message Specification services and protocol using ISO Development Environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The Manufacturing Message Specification (MMS) is an OSI application layer standard designed to support messaging communications to and from programmable devices in a computer integrated manufacturing (CIM) environment. This paper describes how the ISO Development Environment (ISODE) can be employed to implement MMS. ISODE is a non-proprietary implementation of the upper layers of the OSI protocol suite. The experience should be useful to those contemplating using ISODE to implement OSI application entities and application programs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hybrid-ARQ protocol with adaptive rate error control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive rate error control scheme for digital communication over time-varying channels. The cyclic code with majority-logic decoding is used in a cascaded way as an inner code to create a simple and powerful hybrid-ARQ error control scheme. Inner code is used only for error correction and the outer code is used for both error correction and error detection. When an error is detected, retransmission is required. The unsuccessful packets are not discarded as with conventional schemes, but are combined with their retransmitted copies. Approximations for the throughput efficiency and the undetectable error probability are given. A high reliability coupled with a simple high-speed implementation makes it suitable for high data rate error control over both stationary and non-stationary channels. Adaptive error control scheme becomes the best solution for time-varying channels when the optimum code is selected according to the actual channel conditions to enhance the system performance. The main feature of this system is that the basic structure of the encoder and decoder need not be modified while the error-correction capability of the code increases. Results of a comparative analysis show that the proposed scheme outperforms other similar ARQ protocols.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An economic three-phase current-forced reversible AC to DC converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: An economic three-phase AC/DC power converter is proposed. The proposed converter uses only four active switches to simplify the hardware circuit and reduce the cost. In addition to the characteristics of unity power factor and sinusoidal input current waveform, the proposed power converter also possesses bidirectional power flow capability. A mathematical model of the power converter and a critical inductance condition are derived in this context for simulation and design. Finally some simulated and experimental results are presented for verification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Unified framework of adaptive forgetting identification algorithms for time-varying systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a unified framework including adaptive forgetting identification algorithms (AFIA) for time-varying systems. This helps in distinguishing between different algorithms and suggests ways in which algorithms might be improved. Through some transformation, this paper gives a complete convergence proof by Lyapunov stability theory in the situation that both exponential forgetting and directional forgetting factors exist.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On placement of logic schematics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We consider the problem of determination of the sequence of n modules of a logic schematic, that results in a minimum number of line intersections. We consider the case when the logic schematic consists of a union of zero or more P/sub r/,K/sub p,q/ and C/sub 2m/. We use a graph theoretic approach and present an algorithm of time complexity O(n) for sparse schematics and O(n/sup 3/) for dense schematic.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multicast model for WDM-based local lightwave networks with a passive star topology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: To achieve gigabit network service, WDM based lightwave network has been studied intensively. Many scheduling algorithms have bean proposed for single hop WDM based lightwave network with a passive star topology. But these algorithms didn't consider various network services, such as multicast. Multicast is an absolutely needed service for many modern applications, including distributed computing environment, multimedia communication, ..., etc. In this paper, a multicast model and a scheduling algorithm for WDM-based local lightwave networks with a passive star topology are proposed. Under this model, multicast requests can be scheduled efficiently. The simulation results show that our algorithm works well for unicast requests as well as multicast requests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Online tuning of PID controllers using delayed state variable filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Delayed state variable filters are implemented for the estimation of monotone open-loop processes which can be approximated by a dominant time delay coupled with a first order lag. Based on the delayed filtered step output response, the first and second order derivatives, the corresponding static process gain, the apparent dead time and the apparent time constant are evaluated. A new PID tuning formula is formed, which is based on the placement of the open loop zeros related to the apparent time constant and time delay. Coupling with the root locus design procedure, the algorithm provides a range of PID settings for different damping factors. Simulations are included to illustrate the concepts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital study of thyristor controlled series capacitor compensated EHV transmission systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper describes the digital simulation of controlled series capacitor compensated EHV transmission systems. In particular, a method is described for simultaneous digital simulation of thyristors, their firing circuit, and capacitor protection equipment. All these models are implemented by using the Electromagnetic Transients Program (EMTP) including extensive use of Transient Analysis of Control Systems (TACS). The paper concludes with the presentation of some interesting simulation results and analyses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Specification of deterministic execution timing schema for parallel programs on a multiprocessor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: To guarantee the correctness of hard real-time software systems, it is necessary to have a priori knowledge of the deterministic execution times of the system components. Timing schema are formulae based on source program elements to calculate the execution time of programs. Deterministic timing schema or formulae are proposed in this paper for predicting the best and worst case execution times of parallel and distributed programs. The total execution time is computed from the schema provided for a variety of parallel program constructs for shared variable interactions through critical sections and, general semaphores for distributed message passing and remote procedure calls. As an initial attempt to validate the proposition, we have conducted a series of experiments on a shared memory multiprocessor (tightly coupled) system. In one of such experiments involving simplest process structures, where no process interactions occur except to synchronize the initiation and termination of processes, the timing schema based approach has been shown to exhibit safe and reasonably tight predictions. The representative implementations that obey the schema and the methods of incorporating some of the underlying hardware contentions and indeterminacies have also been studied. Predictable timing behaviour in concurrent systems is indeed a possibility using the schema approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DSP-based field oriented control of a load commutated current source inverter (LCCSI)-fed AC motor drive
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In the power range of above 1 MW, industrial AC drive load-commutated current source inverters (LCCSI) are controlled by simple methods like the combination of V/f ratio constant control at low frequency and V/f ratio constant-angle control at high frequency. This gives a good steady-state but poor dynamic performance. This paper describes a drive control of LCCSI-fed induction motors which is based on the principle of field oriented control. Along with taking into account the output capacitor's effect, the direct field oriented control referred to rotor flux fixed reference frame without a speed sensor is applied to decouple torque and flux generating currents and to overcome the problem of instability caused by the output capacitor. This control scheme is implemented by a 32 bit floating point Digital Signal Processor (DSP) chip-TMS320C30. The availability of this control scheme is verified by computer simulation and experimental results for a laboratory LCCSI-induction motor (10 HP) system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The performance improvement of wormhole router for multicomputer systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Wormhole routing has been introduced into message-passing interconnection networks to reduce communication latency. However, the networks may reach saturation rapidly because of the small number of flit buffers. In this paper, a simulator is developed to investigate approaches to raise the performance of wormhole routers. The results suggest that 4 to 8 flit buffers, instead of one flit buffer, are more suitable for each channel. In addition, it shows that by adaptive routing, not only communication latency, but also throughput is better than deterministic routing. Finally, short packet length is suggested to reduce the blocking time, and it could lessen the deviation of communication latency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model of parallel interactive processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A model of interactive programs is proposed in this paper along with algorithms for program and data mapping onto parallel processors. We propose that parallel processing of interactive programs be based on interface systems. Algorithms for mapping interactive programs onto parallel computers are also developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Natural language understanding based on background knowledge
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Natural language understanding can be divided into five hierarchical levels, each level related to other levels. Background knowledge consists of all level's units and their usage in the real language environment. Co-occurence information of any two units of the same level can be provided by background knowledge. This paper discusses the usage of background knowledge in automatic Chinese word segmentation, and text understanding based on semantic relationships.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Speech enhancement using non-linear prediction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Describes a method for speech enhancement using multi-layer perceptrons (MLP) configured for time domain non-linear prediction (NLP) as originally proposed by Kaouri and Lin (1988) and Tamura and Waibel (1988). In addition, the authors present details of the influence of the non-linear operations compared directly with the linear case. Experimental results show that nonlinear MLPs provide better performances than linear equivalent systems. Results also show that MLPs with a multi-output structure give improved performances over MLPs with single-output structure and normalisation can affect MLPs performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Hierarchical clustering technique for the minimum cost design of a naturally clustered computer communication network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: We propose an optimization problem for minimizing the design cost and maintaining a proper grade of service for a computer communication network. This problem is solved by using the subgradient optimization technique. The technique is illustrated by a set of examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Damping common-mode torsional oscillations using static phase shifters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The paper presents a study on the application of static phase shifters to stabilize common-mode torsional oscillations in the IEEE Second Benchmark Model, system-2. In order to effectively suppress the unstable torsional modes, a unified approach based on modal control theory is proposed and a set of static phase shifter controllers (SPSC) are designed. The effectiveness of the proposed damping scheme is demonstrated by using the frequency-domain approach based on eigenvalue analyses and the time-domain approach based on dynamic response simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Direct method for model reference adaptive PI controller using the gradient approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Two types of PI controller configurations considered in this paper for the direct method of model reference adaptive PI controller using the gradient approach. The authors have generated significant insight on the inner workings of the gradient method from a 3-D spatial perspective. The type of PI control rules and the corresponding adaptation rate /spl theta/~/spl dot/ generate certain adverse effects on the overall adaptation trend. Extensive results of the adaptive algorithms for both the standard textbook PI and the modified PI control rules are presented for discussion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit for switched reluctance motor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A novel full fledged equivalent circuit for simple analysis of a switched reluctance motor (SRM) is developed. It is capable of explaining SRM operation in all modes, such as (a) with and without saturation, (b) continuous and discontinuous conduction, (c) operation in all four quadrants. Previous attempts in this direction can be shown to be special cases of this comprehensive equivalent circuit. Furthermore, this equivalent circuit could be integrated with that of the 'inverter' to optimize the drive as a single unit consisting of the SRM and inverter. Finally its merits are highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of switched reluctance motor driven by novel C-dump inverter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This study describes the influence of the mutual inductance between the adjacent phase windings of variable reluctance motor (VRM) and presents a new type of inverter for the reduction of such influence. In this inverter topology, though an additional power switch is used as compared with the conventional C-dump inverter circuit, unwanted negative torque produced by the mutual inductance in the winding next to the energizing phase is remarkably reduced. Hence the circuit results in an increase of the average torque and contributes to the improvement of overall drive efficiency. Theoretical prediction is verified by experimental results obtained with the integration of the presented inverter and a prototype 6/4 VRM.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Load assignment for determining substation service areas with the aid of digital mapping
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper, an effective method is presented to determine the optimal substation and feeder planning based on minimum feeder loss. A geographic information system (GIS) with distributed database, state-of-the-art computer graphics and the proposed method are integrated to solve the optimal sizing and siting of distribution substations, and to perform optimal feeder routing including load transfer to the neighboring substations in case of an overload. The GIS database was built and the facility data were retrieved from the database for planning applications. It can be shown that the network data in the GIS database were searched, facility data were retrieved for the proposed algorithm, and output results can be displayed on screen with the graphical displays of the GIS. The process provides a practical way for planners to facilitate the planning of the distribution system. The integration of digital maps, good man-machine interface, the state-of-the-art computer graphics and the application program (algorithm) proposes a concept for not only planning engineers but also operation dispatchers regarding a new way to look at the distribution system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimating rotor state of PMSM variable-speed system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In this paper an extended Kalman-filter is designed to estimate the rotor speed and position of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) simply by measuring the currents and voltages of the stator coils. With this method, the variable speed drive system is considerably simplified and alleviates the need for a tachodynamo and rotor position sensor. Simulation results by means of the Monte Carlo method show that the extended Kalman-filter has excellent tracking ability and can be used in practical applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of superconductive magnetic energy storage unit on damping subsynchronous resonance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A novel power system damping scheme using superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) unit is proposed in this paper to damp subsynchronous resonance (SSR) of the IEEE Second Benchmark Model, system-1 which is a widely employed standard model for computer simulation of SSR. The studied system contains a turbine-generator set connected to an infinite bus through two parallel transmission lines, one of which is series-capacitor compensated. In order to stabilize all SSR modes, simultaneous active and reactive power modulation and a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) damping controller designed by modal control theory are proposed for the SMES unit. A frequency-domain approach based on eigenvalue analysis and a time-domain approach based on nonlinear model simulations are performed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed damping method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A method of pattern recognition based upon synthetic technology of fuzzy logic and neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A method which uses the synthesis of fuzzy logic and neural networks is provided to solve 2D pattern recognition with incomplete information. When the object set is confirmed, we use a neural network detector to discover the edges and corners. After we have obtained that information, we get the conclusion from the fuzzy reasoning. Computer simulation shows that, although there remain a lot of improvements to make, the synthetic method of using neural networks and fuzzy logic is effective to solve such problems dealing with partially invisible objects. The method can be introduced to solve similar pattern recognition problems in 3D images.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of fuzzy neural networks in fuzzy adaptive control
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In recent years, studies on fuzzy neural networks (FNN) have been developed on the basis of the theory of neural networks and fuzzy sets. In this paper, we introduce the concept of fuzzy neurons and neural nets constructed from fuzzy neurons, present a new kind of FNN, and give its structure and its adaptive learning algorithm. Then we apply the FNN to fuzzy adaptive control. By simulation, we prove the effectiveness and feasibility of applying the FNN in fuzzy adaptive control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed intelligent railway traffic control based on fuzzy decision-making
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A multileveled distributed railway traffic control system, which overcomes the drawbacks of conventional centralized railway traffic control systems, is proposed in this paper. The system structure, function distribution and interactions among different hierarchies of the proposed system is addressed in detail. The intelligent control algorithm corresponding to the system is also put forward in detail. The algorithm, which is based on distributed intelligence, knowledge engineering and fuzzy multi-attribute decision-making, can realize the control strategy traffic control. The feasibility of the approach proposed has been proved by simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Variations on Ethernet traffic monitoring
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The network traffic depends upon the types of requests from network users. Consequently, network traffic monitoring is sensitive to system workload caused by the users. In this project, we study the Ethernet traffic analysis and performance factors which affect the data receiving performance. In brief, we have accomplished the following: study of related Ethernet monitoring efforts; writing the sending and receiving programs above the NIT protocol; working through the Sniffer's network analyzer; and tests of the performance effects of variations on NIT buffer size, CPU power, and available memory space. The report of this project gives insight into the performance issues with, various system parameters, particularly in the file server's alternatives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A theoretical approach for solving the post-fabrication tuning problem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: Post-fabrication tuning is always necessary in electrical circuits manufacturing to achieve a high percentage yield. Tuning can give good yield at low cost only if the suitable tuning parameters are identified. In this paper, a theoretical approach is proposed to identify those tuning parameters. The approach is implemented in an example and the results match with the predication.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On asynchronous stochastic learning control method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: In view of the limitation that a general asynchronous learning control method is unable to cope with systems with measurement noise, an asynchronous stochastic learning control system (ASLC) using stochastic approximation algorithm, is proposed. The corresponding convergence proof is given. To improve the convergence rate of stochastic approximation, ASLC with acceleration factor is further presented. A simulation example is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of the stability of power system governed by Duffing's equation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: A one-machine-to-quasi-infinite-bus (OMQIB) power system, which can be interpreted as Duffing's equation from the viewpoint of oscillations, has revealed that it may suffer instability (the "jump phenomena") due to the ill-combination of the system parameters. The authors investigate the stability problem of this kind of power system via the catastrophe theory approach. Discussions are given on the effects of the specific combination of system parameters to make the resonance curve triple-valued and on the identified bifurcation set which can be used to assess the power system stability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Incorporating the parallel processing techniques with the demand-driven model of functional programming languages
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid reduction scheme that incorporates parallel processing techniques into the demand-driven model of functional programs. With this scheme, functional language programs can be executed in parallel at three different levels, which are the parallel execution of vectors inside a redex, the parallel reduction of multiple redexes, and the high level pipeline processing. The high level pipeline consists of three stages that are redex detection, redex allocation and reduction execution. Moreover, memory latency and switch network latency that cannot be ignored in usual multiprocessor systems can effectively be eliminated by embedding the memory access and the switch network transmission into the high level pipeline. Experimental results of the software simulator reveal the potential performance of the hybrid reduction scheme. Functional language FL is chosen as the target language in our research work.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A review of robust techniques for the analysis of degraded speech
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: The severe effects of additive noise on automatic recognition systems has resulted in proposals of many different strategies. The paper reviews these strategies and loosely classifies them according to the stage at which the noise compensation occurs. the authors comment on the difficulty of making direct comparisons, given various inconsistencies, eg whether full knowledge of the noise degradation is known, either at the testing or the modelling stage. They suggest standards based on those criteria which define boundaries, and which would go some way to making comparisons more meaningful.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A VHDL approach to system design for multiprocessor circuit simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of TENCON '93. IEEE Region 10 International Conference on Computers, Communications and Automation
abstract: For the execution of a large circuit simulation problem on a bus-based master-slave multiprocessor system with shared memory, increasing the number of tasks does not always decrease the execution time. The tradeoff between communication and parallelism will have direct effect on the computation performance. To assess the performance of such a system, a behavioral simulation of its architecture is presented using the VHSIC Hardware Description Language (VHDL).
